title: Gist 3.0.0 upgrade is not idempotent after structural define phase
description: A real knowledge database can have the gist 3.0.0 structural relation/attribute hierarchy already defined while the app still attempts the v2.0.4 -> v3.0.0 migration. Rerunning the migration then fails on undefine value datetime from actualEndDate because the value type is inherited from atDateTime after the define phase.
design: Add a live regression using real ontology-gist tags v2.0.4 and v3.0.0. Install v2.0.4 into a temporary TypeDB database through OntologyViewModel/app package code, manually apply only the top-level define chunk from v3.0.0's structural-property-hierarchy-schema.tql in one schema transaction, then run the normal app upgrade to v3.0.0. The app should treat the migration as already structurally prepared and complete the upgrade without re-undefining inherited value types. Implement the smallest production guard needed in the migration apply path.
acceptance_criteria: The new live regression fails before the production fix with SVL37/UEX13 and passes after. The original OntologyLiveApplyTests suite still passes and the raw log shows nonzero Swift Testing test execution.

title: Live gist schema assertion assumed one-line TypeDB formatting
description: The real ontology-gist v2.0.4 -> v3.0.0 live upgrade reached the final live schema assertion, but the test looked for 'attribute isRecordedAt sub atDateTime' as one contiguous string. TypeDB emits type schema clauses pretty-printed across comma/newline boundaries, e.g. 'attribute isRecordedAt,\n  sub atDateTime;'.
design: Normalize schema text and expected clauses before asserting structural hierarchy and role specialization output. Keep the assertion against the real live type schema returned from TypeDB, but do not depend on TypeDB's line wrapping or comma formatting.
acceptance_criteria: The live gist upgrade test asserts the real typeSchema contains attribute isRecordedAt sub atDateTime and a relation role specialization after normalization. The raw log shows the OntologyLiveApplyTests suite executes nonzero tests and passes.
close_reason: Fixed in OneWorkspace: test.sh now fails Swift Testing zero-test selections; SchemaContractValidator accepts inherited attribute declarations; live gist schema assertions normalize TypeDB formatting.

title: Schema contract validation rejects inherited gist attributes
description: After the mixed gist 3.0.0 schema migration succeeds, OntologyViewModel.applySchema validates the v3.0.0 bootstrap plan and fails because SchemaContractValidator/TypeQLParser do not model TypeDB attribute inheritance declarations such as 'attribute actualEndDate sub actualEndDateTime;'.
design: Fix SchemaContractValidator and/or TypeQLParser so TypeDB 3 schema attribute declarations that use 'sub <attribute>' without an explicit value type are included in the TypeCatalog as attributes. Validation must understand that owned attributes may be declared by inherited attribute types. Preserve normal bootstrap validation and duplicate-definition checks. Add focused non-live regression coverage for parsing and contract validation of a schema where an entity owns an attribute declared with 'attribute child sub parent;' and the parent carries the value type. Then rerun the real gist live upgrade path.
acceptance_criteria: SchemaContractValidator.validate(plan:) accepts gist v3.0.0 style inherited attributes instead of reporting them missing. A focused automated test fails before the parser/catalog fix and passes after. The real ontology-gist v2.0.4 -> v3.0.0 live upgrade test applies successfully through OntologyViewModel with databasePackageVersion('gist') == '3.0.0'.
close_reason: Fixed in OneWorkspace: test.sh now fails Swift Testing zero-test selections; SchemaContractValidator accepts inherited attribute declarations; live gist schema assertions normalize TypeDB formatting.

title: Swift Testing filter can pass live apply with zero executed tests
description: The targeted Ontology live apply command used for one-2i7 can report success while executing zero Swift Testing tests, so the gist 2.0.4 -> 3.0.0 live regression did not actually run.
design: Update validation for one-2i7 so the live gist upgrade test is invoked in a way that selects the Swift Testing function body. Prefer a suite-level or supported Swift Testing selector if xcodebuild cannot address individual functions. Add/adjust test instrumentation only if needed to prove the test body runs. Verify with the raw .build/derived-data/test.log showing a nonzero executed Swift Testing test count and the OntologyLiveApplyTests gist upgrade test name, not just xcsift status success.
acceptance_criteria: A targeted test command for OntologyLiveApplyTests/gist_upgradesFrom204To300_throughMixedSchemaMigration executes at least one test and fails if the test body fails. The raw Xcode test log no longer says Executed 0 tests for the live gist upgrade validation. Document the exact working command in the implementation notes or final handoff.
close_reason: Fixed in OneWorkspace: test.sh now fails Swift Testing zero-test selections; SchemaContractValidator accepts inherited attribute declarations; live gist schema assertions normalize TypeDB formatting.

title: Ontology app cannot apply gist 2.0.4 to 3.0.0 mixed schema migration
description: The Ontology app failed applying ontology-gist v3.0.0 over an installed v2.0.4 database. The migration file is valid when executed with TypeDB console source semantics because its define and undefine schema operations run inside one schema transaction. The app's Swift driver path does not currently support that execution model: batching/committing the define before undefine triggers TypeDB schema validation for inherited value redeclaration, while submitting the whole file as one query triggers a TypeQL parser error at the top-level undefine. This is an Ontology plugin apply-path bug exposed by the real gist release, not a gist generator-only issue.
design: Add live app-level regression coverage in OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/OntologyLiveApplyTests.swift using the existing LiveTypeDBFixture. The test should install real ontology-gist tag v2.0.4 into a real temporary TypeDB database through the app package apply path, then upgrade the same database to real ontology-gist tag v3.0.0 through OntologyViewModel/app schema apply. Clone or checkout the two gist tags into temp directories under /tmp/test temp root, then feed those checkouts into PackageManager using the same package/provenance machinery used by the app. Production support likely requires adding a TypeDBSwift/DefaultTypeDBService/OntologyTypeDBClient method that opens one schema transaction, submits multiple schema queries sequentially, and commits once. Add a migration-only schema splitter that splits top-level define/undefine/redefine sections before calling that transaction API. Normal bootstrap batching should remain separate and continue to commit pure define batches independently.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A live test exercises real ontology-gist artifacts from tags v2.0.4 and v3.0.0, not synthetic TypeQL fixtures. 2. The test installs gist v2.0.4 into an empty real TypeDB database through the app package path, then upgrades that same database to gist v3.0.0 through OntologyViewModel/app apply code. 3. The test fails against the current one-query/one-commit schema migration implementation and passes only after mixed schema migration units execute atomically in one schema transaction. 4. Assertions verify app-level success, no schema apply error presentation, database package version for gist is 3.0.0, schema docs remain queryable, and live type schema includes structural property hierarchy output such as attribute isRecordedAt sub atDateTime plus at least one relation role specialization. 5. Missing /opt/homebrew/bin/typedb or other TypeDB startup/git checkout failures fail loudly; the test must not silently skip. 6. Existing package bootstrap batching and schema apply integration tests still pass.
notes: Main mixed-schema-migration fix landed in commits 19d9dae9 and 454c239f. Partial-state recovery (test at OntologyLiveApplyTests:218) split out into one-1vy as a follow-up — it's a separate semantics question, not part of the original mixed-transaction bug.

title: App live gist upgrade 2.0.4 to 3.0.0 fails on mixed schema migration
description: The Ontology app release path failed applying ontology-gist v3.0.0 over an installed v2.0.4 database. The repo-level validator used TypeDB console source semantics, while the app uses the Swift driver and currently submits one query per committed schema transaction. The real gist migration contains a schema unit with both define and undefine operations that must execute in one schema transaction: committing the define first triggers inherited value redeclaration validation, while sending define+undefine as one query triggers a TypeQL parser error at undefine. We need a live app-level regression that installs real gist v2.0.4, upgrades to real gist v3.0.0, and exercises the actual OntologyViewModel/PackageManager/TypeDBServiceBackedClient path against a real TypeDB server.
design: Add a live integration test in OneWorkspace under OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/OntologyLiveApplyTests.swift. The test should use the existing LiveTypeDBFixture server/client infrastructure, but it must control package versions explicitly. Clone or checkout ontology-gist tags v2.0.4 and v3.0.0 into temp directories under /tmp or the test temp root. Use PackageManager.addFromDirectory or tag-specific repository installs to cache/apply v2.0.4 first, then replace the cached package with v3.0.0 and call viewModel.applySchema on the real gist schema. The test must rely on live database provenance or installation records the same way the app does, not a fake installed-version shortcut. Production support likely requires adding a multi-query schema transaction API to the TypeDB Swift path and a migration-only splitter that turns one schema migration file into sequential define/undefine/redefine queries while committing once. Keep normal bootstrap batching separate from migration transaction execution.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A live app-level test installs ontology-gist v2.0.4 into an empty real TypeDB database, then upgrades the same database to ontology-gist v3.0.0 through OntologyViewModel/app package apply code. 2. The test uses real ontology-gist artifacts from tags v2.0.4 and v3.0.0, not synthetic TypeQL fixtures. 3. The test fails against the current one-query/one-commit app schema migration behavior and passes only after the app can execute multi-operation schema migrations atomically in one schema transaction. 4. Assertions verify the app reports success, database package version for gist is 3.0.0, gist schema docs remain queryable, and the live type schema contains structural property hierarchy output such as attribute isRecordedAt sub atDateTime and a role specialization from the new relation hierarchy. 5. The test is documented as non-skipping live coverage: missing typedb binary, git checkout failure, or TypeDB startup failure must fail loudly. 6. The fix includes any required protocol/service/driver support and does not regress existing package bootstrap batching tests.

title: Execute vibemachine v2.0.0 release validation and tag
description: Run the shared ontology-release flow for vibemachine v2.0.0 after dependency refresh and validation are complete.
design:
Execute the final vibemachine major release after dependency refresh and bootstrap validation.

Use ../ontology-tooling/bin/ontology-release --repo . --version 2.0.0 from ontology-vibemachine. As with gist, the shared release flow owns version rewrites, refresh, validation, release commit, and tag. This release should occur after gist v3.0.0 is locally released/tagged so validation uses the intended dependency contract.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. Release command completes without validation failure.
2. git log -1 --pretty=%s in ontology-vibemachine equals 'Release vibemachine v2.0.0'.
3. git tag --list v2.0.0 in ontology-vibemachine returns v2.0.0.
4. package.json and active manifest paths reference v2.0.0.
5. If push is deferred, the bead records local release state and required push command.
close_reason: vibemachine v2.0.0 release committed and tagged locally after dry-run and validation.

title: Validate vibemachine bootstrap against gist 3.0.0
description: Run vibemachine validation and TypeDB bootstrap after gist v3.0.0 is available locally.
design:
Validate vibemachine against the new gist structural schema after gist v3.0.0 is cut locally.

The bootstrap validator must be able to resolve sibling ontology-gist through the repo layout used by package scripts/release tooling. Pay special attention to gist role names used by vibemachine specializations: comesFromAgentSubject/Object, hasParticipantSubject/Object, isAboutSubject/Object, isBasedOnSubject/Object, isMemberOfSubject/Object, isDirectPartOfSubject/Object, and isCategorizedBySubject/Object. These names must remain stable after gist changes.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. npm run validate:bootstrap passes in ontology-vibemachine.
2. npm run test:typedb-bootstrap passes in ontology-vibemachine with gist v3.0.0 in the sibling checkout.
3. If TypeDB reports missing parent roles or invalid role specialization, the failing relation/role labels are captured in the bead before implementation continues.
4. No vibemachine schema redesign is introduced unless validation proves a concrete incompatibility.
5. Existing control-booth validation remains runnable or documented if outside npm test scope.
notes: After starting the local container service with container system start, current vibemachine bootstrap validation passes against the regenerated gist/vibemachine artifacts: TYPEDB_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin/typedb npm run test:typedb-bootstrap. Final v2.0.0 validation remains open because gist has not yet been versioned/tagged as 3.0.0 and vibemachine dependency has not been bumped to >=3.0.0.
close_reason: vibemachine npm test passes against local gist 3.0.0 package order.

title: Refresh vibemachine package contract for v2.0.0
description: Run vibemachine package contract refresh after dependency and shared documentation parser changes.
design:
Run the hand-authored package bootstrap for vibemachine after version/dependency changes.

ontology-vibemachine package.json defines refresh:package-contract as node ../ontology-gist/tools/package_contract/bootstrap_hand_authored_package.mjs . This will regenerate shared schemas, package manifest, provenance, schema docs, and apply units. Because this is a major release, run through ontology-release --version 2.0.0 or mirror its version rewrite behavior before refresh so generated headers/manifests use v2.0.0.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. ontology-vibemachine package.json version is 2.0.0.
2. manifests/vibemachine-v2.0.0.package-manifest.json exists and is referenced by package.json.
3. data/vibemachine-provenance.tql header and OntologyModuleVersion records reference 2.0.0.
4. data/vibemachine-schema-docs.tql and generated apply units are refreshed with parser improvements.
5. npm run validate:bootstrap passes after refresh.
close_reason: vibemachine package contract refreshed for v2.0.0.

title: Update vibemachine gist dependency to >=3.0.0
description: Update ontology-vibemachine package dependency to require gist >=3.0.0 for the breaking structural schema contract.
design:
Edit ontology-vibemachine/package.json dependency metadata after gist v3.0.0 is available.

The current dependency is { name: 'gist', version: '>=2.0.4' }. Change it to >=3.0.0 to communicate the breaking structural schema dependency. Do not loosen to >=2 because downstream bootstrap should not run against the old flattened gist contract.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. ontology-vibemachine/package.json dependencies contains {name:'gist', version:'>=3.0.0'}.
2. No active package manifest generated for v2.0.0 advertises a gist dependency below 3.0.0.
3. npm run refresh:package-contract preserves the updated dependency instead of reverting it.
4. rg '>=2.0.4' in active vibemachine package files returns no active dependency references.

title: Execute gist v3.0.0 release validation and tag
description: Run the shared ontology-release flow for gist v3.0.0 after implementation and validation are complete.
design:
Execute the final gist release only after implementation, docs, generated artifacts, and validation beads are complete.

Run ../ontology-tooling/bin/ontology-release --repo . --version 3.0.0 from ontology-gist, or use npm run release with equivalent arguments if supported. The release command requires a clean working tree before it mutates versioned files and creates the release commit/tag. Beads auto-export may update .beads/issues.jsonl; treat that as issue-tracker state and include it only if appropriate for the release commit policy.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. git status is clean before invoking release, except for intentionally included issue export changes.
2. Release command completes without validation failure.
3. git log -1 --pretty=%s equals 'Release gist v3.0.0'.
4. git tag --list v3.0.0 returns v3.0.0.
5. bd issue statuses are updated to reflect completed implementation/release work.

title: Update gist package version and versioned manifest paths to 3.0.0
description: Use the shared release flow or equivalent release prep to move gist from 2.0.4 to 3.0.0 with versioned artifact paths aligned.
design:
Prepare gist versioned package state for v3.0.0 through ontology-release or the same planPackageRelease semantics.

package.json contains version, provenance.manifest, manifests, assembly.generatedArtifacts, scripts, and loadOrder paths that include the current package version. The release flow should rewrite these from 2.0.4 to 3.0.0 and rename checked-in manifest files. Upstream tag v14.0.0 must not be rewritten because it is immutable source provenance, not package version.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. package.json version is 3.0.0.
2. package.json provenance.manifest points to manifests/gist-v3.0.0.translation-manifest.json.
3. package.json manifests and assembly.generatedArtifacts reference v3.0.0 generated manifest/report/IR paths.
4. package.json upstream.tag remains v14.0.0.
5. No stale v2.0.4 active manifest path remains in package.json active contract fields.

title: Run TypeDB bootstrap and migration validation for gist
description: Run npm test or the relevant validate/bootstrap/migration commands after regeneration.
design:
Use existing package scripts as the verification gate after implementation.

ontology-gist package.json defines validate:bootstrap, test:typedb-bootstrap, test:typedb-migration, and npm test. validate_bootstrap.mjs also starts a temporary TypeDB server for schema/data loading in its later phase. The final verification should run npm test unless TypeDB runtime availability blocks it; if blocked, record the exact missing runtime and run all non-TypeDB checks that can execute locally.

Do not replace the repo scripts with ad hoc validation unless a script itself is defective.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. npm run validate:bootstrap passes.
2. npm run test:typedb-bootstrap passes.
3. npm run test:typedb-migration passes.
4. npm test passes end to end, or the bead is updated with the exact environmental blocker and command output summary.
5. Any validation failure creates or updates follow-up beads before release work proceeds.
notes:
TypeDB validation blockers captured: ontology-gist npm run test:typedb-bootstrap fails because ~/.typedb/typedb is missing; ontology-vibemachine npm run test:typedb-bootstrap fails starting the container-backed TypeDB service with XPC connection invalid and suggests container system start. Non-TypeDB checks run: gist emit:structural succeeds, gist validate:bootstrap reaches the TypeDB runtime boundary after hierarchy/doc checks, executable package validation passes for both repos, and vibemachine validate:bootstrap passes.
TypeDB binary is available at /opt/homebrew/bin/typedb. Passed: TYPEDB_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin/typedb npm run validate:bootstrap; passed: TYPEDB_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin/typedb npm run test:typedb-bootstrap. Still failing: TYPEDB_BIN=/opt/homebrew/bin/typedb npm run test:typedb-migration reports 'Current gist package is missing migration plans.' This is now a release metadata/planning issue rather than a TypeDB runtime blocker.
close_reason: Passed full gist npm test with TypeDB at /opt/homebrew/bin/typedb, including v2.0.4 -> v3.0.0 migration validation.

title: Add gist schema hierarchy count validation
description: Add checks comparing IR subPropertyOf edge counts with emitted schema subtype declarations and role specializations.
design:
Add schema-level hierarchy checks in tools/gist_to_typeql/validate_bootstrap.mjs.

Use the same mapping rules as the emitter: named datatype subPropertyOf where both endpoints map to datatype properties, and named object subPropertyOf where both endpoints map to object properties. Parse schema/gistCore.tql and verify direct subtype edges exist. For object property edges, verify relation subtype plus the expected two role subtype edges when parsing role specializations. This can reuse parseTypeQLSchemaStructure() once it records attribute and role subtype edges.

Avoid brittle line-count regexes as the primary check; compare structured labels from identifier maps or generated schema parser output.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. The check reports expected vs actual counts for datatype attribute subtypes, object relation subtypes, and role subtype edges.
2. The check identifies missing edge labels in error output, not just a count mismatch.
3. Removing one generated attribute sub declaration causes npm run validate:bootstrap to fail.
4. Removing one relation role 'as' specialization causes npm run validate:bootstrap to fail.
5. The check passes on freshly generated schema.
close_reason: Implemented and locally verified with generated schema/docs checks; TypeDB runtime validation remains tracked separately.

title: Regenerate gist schema docs and apply units
description: Regenerate data/gistCore-schema-docs.tql and generated apply units after parser/emitter changes.
design:
Regenerate docs through the existing gist flow after schema parser and structural emitter changes.

emit_structural.mjs reads existing data/gistCore-schema-docs.tql, replaces the generated structural metadata section using renderStructuralMetadataSection(), and writes apply units. emit_schema_docs.mjs owns the base SchemaResource records from OWL annotations. The regeneration order must preserve base docs and then replace structural metadata from the newly emitted schema.

Expected artifacts include data/gistCore-schema-docs.tql and generated/apply-units/data/gistCore-schema-docs/*.tql, plus manifest/provenance checksum updates during release refresh.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. data/gistCore-schema-docs.tql contains generated schemaSubTypeOf inserts for attribute subtype edges such as actualEndDate -> actualEndDateTime.
2. data/gistCore-schema-docs.tql contains generated schemaSubTypeOf inserts for relation subtype edges such as hasGiver -> hasParticipant.
3. data/gistCore-schema-docs.tql contains generated schemaSubTypeOf inserts for role subtype edges such as hasGiver:hasGiverSubject -> hasParticipant:hasParticipantSubject.
4. generated/apply-units/data/gistCore-schema-docs are refreshed and referenced by package.json loadOrder/data as needed.
5. npm run validate:bootstrap passes checksum and freshness checks.
close_reason: Implemented and locally verified with generated schema/docs checks; TypeDB runtime validation remains tracked separately.

title: Preserve relates role specialization in schema metadata
description: Update parseRelatesToken/schema_structure.mjs so 'relates childRole as parentRole' creates role resources and role-to-role schemaSubTypeOf edges.
design:
Update parseRelatesToken() and relation parsing in tools/shared/schema_structure.mjs.

Current parseRelatesToken() returns only the child role label and ignores the optional 'as parentRole'. Change it to return structured data: { roleLabel, overriddenRoleLabel }. In the relation parser, keep adding schemaRelates for relation::roleLabel. If overriddenRoleLabel is present and the relation has a supertype label, add a role subtype edge from '<relation>:<roleLabel>' to '<supertype>:<overriddenRoleLabel>'.

This relies on TypeDB role specialization semantics: the parent role belongs to the relation supertype, not to the child relation label. If a relates token uses 'as' without a parsed relation supertype, emit a parser warning or skip with a clear validation path rather than inventing an incorrect parent role resource.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. Parsing 'relation submissionProvidedBy sub comesFromAgent, relates submission as comesFromAgentSubject;' emits role resource submissionProvidedBy:submission and subtype edge submissionProvidedBy:submission -> comesFromAgent:comesFromAgentSubject.
2. Parsing a root relation without 'as' emits role resources and schemaRelates edges but no role subtype edges.
3. Existing vibemachine generated docs gain role-to-role schemaSubTypeOf records for all hand-authored role specializations.
4. Generated gist docs gain two role subtype edges for each emitted object property subtype relation.
5. Parser behavior remains deterministic and sorted.
close_reason: Implemented and locally verified with generated schema/docs checks; TypeDB runtime validation remains tracked separately.

title: Parse attribute subtype declarations in schema_structure.mjs
description: Extend shared schema parsing to recognize attribute child sub parent declarations and produce schemaSubTypeOf metadata for attributes.
design:
Update the attribute branch in tools/shared/schema_structure.mjs parseTypeQLSchemaStructure().

Current regex only matches 'attribute X value T'. It should also match 'attribute X sub Y' with optional capability text if TypeDB syntax allows extensions later. For sub declarations, add X to attributes/typeKinds and add subtypeEdges entry X::Y. Do not set valueTypeName on sub attributes unless a value declaration is actually present; value type is inherited from the supertype.

Keep output normalization stable and sorted through the existing normalizeStructure() path.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. A parser fixture/string containing 'define attribute actualEndDate sub actualEndDateTime;' yields subtypeEdges [{subtype:'actualEndDate', supertype:'actualEndDateTime'}].
2. The same fixture yields attributeResources for both referenced labels as kind attribute, with no valueTypeName on the subtype unless declared.
3. Existing parsing of 'attribute sourceIRI value string;' still yields valueTypeName 'string'.
4. Regenerated gist docs contain schemaSubTypeOf edges for all attribute subtype declarations.
close_reason: Implemented and locally verified with generated schema/docs checks; TypeDB runtime validation remains tracked separately.

title: Revise owns and plays pruning for structural inheritance
description: Update entity capability pruning so attribute subtype ownership and relation-role specialization do not leave redundant or invalid owns/plays declarations.
design:
Implement in buildEntityDefinitions() in tools/gist_to_typeql/emit_structural.mjs.

Current pruning deletes only exact owns/plays inherited through entity supertype chains. With attribute and relation role subtyping, exact-string pruning is insufficient. The generator must understand direct/transitive attribute supertypes and role supertypes. If an entity owns a child attribute, it may still require explicit ownership depending on TypeDB capability rules, but it must not redundantly own both a child and a supertype where one declaration is inherited or invalid. Likewise, entities that play a specialized child role should not also carry stale plays declarations for now-structural parent roles unless TypeDB requires both.

Design the pruning around schema load validity first: generate the minimal explicit owns/plays declarations accepted by TypeDB for the emitted type hierarchy, then preserve query ergonomics through inherited TypeDB semantics rather than duplicate capabilities.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. npm run test:typedb-bootstrap loads the full regenerated gist package without schema errors about invalid owns/plays declarations.
2. Entity definitions do not contain duplicate exact plays/owns inherited through entity supertypes.
3. For representative specialized relations, domain/range classes play the child roles needed to insert child relations and do not retain unnecessary parent-role declarations introduced only by inherited property domains.
4. For representative attribute subtype chains, owners can own/insert the leaf attribute values expected by generated seed or query artifacts.
5. Translation report lists final owns/plays after pruning for review.
close_reason: Implemented and validated by TypeDB bootstrap/load checks with structural attribute and relation inheritance enabled.

title: Emit object property relation subtyping and role specialization
description: Change emit_structural.mjs so named object subPropertyOf edges emit relation subtyping and child roles specialize parent roles.
design:
Implement in tools/gist_to_typeql/emit_structural.mjs where object properties are rendered.

Build an object-property map from IRI to property. For each object property, find the direct named subPropertyOf superproperty if it maps to another object property. Root object properties keep current standalone relation shape. Child object properties emit 'relation child sub parent' and relate child subject/object roles using TypeDB role overriding: 'relates childSubject as parentSubject' and 'relates childObject as parentObject'.

Role names should remain stable for downstream users: child roles keep the current '<childRelation>Subject/Object' naming. Parent role names are derived from the generated parent relation label, preserving reserved-name rewrites such as links -> linksRel.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. schema/gistCore.tql includes examples such as 'relation hasGiver sub hasParticipant' with 'relates hasGiverSubject as hasParticipantSubject'.
2. schema/gistCore.tql includes 'relation comesFromAgent sub hasParticipant' and 'relation linksFrom sub linksRel' using generated parent labels.
3. Exactly 13 mapped object subPropertyOf edges are emitted as relation sub declarations.
4. Exactly 26 role specializations are emitted for those 13 binary relation subtype edges.
5. Existing vibemachine role names that specialize gist roles still resolve after gist regeneration and TypeDB bootstrap.
close_reason: Implemented and locally verified with generated schema/docs checks; TypeDB runtime validation remains tracked separately.

title: Emit datatype property subtyping in gistCore.tql
description: Change emit_structural.mjs so named datatype subPropertyOf edges emit attribute child sub parent declarations, while root attributes keep primitive value declarations.
design:
Implement in tools/gist_to_typeql/emit_structural.mjs near renderSchema() and inferAttributeValueType().

Use model.resources.datatypeProperties as the authoritative property list. A datatype property has a TypeDB attribute supertype when it has a named subPropertyOf term whose IRI also exists in the datatype property map. Emit only direct named superproperty edges from gist; do not synthesize transitive edges.

Primitive value compatibility must be checked before emission. Because TypeDB attribute subtypes inherit value type, the effective primitive inferred for a child must be compatible with the root/supertype chain. The existing inferAttributeValueType() walks superproperties for ranges; retain that behavior for roots, but add a validation pass that reports incompatible child/supertype inferred primitives before writing schema.

sourceIRI remains a synthetic root attribute with value string and is not part of OWL subPropertyOf handling.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. schema/gistCore.tql includes examples such as 'attribute actualEndDate sub actualEndDateTime;' and 'attribute startDateTime sub atDateTime;'.
2. schema/gistCore.tql keeps root declarations such as 'attribute atDateTime value datetime;' and 'attribute containedText value string;'.
3. Exactly 25 mapped datatype subPropertyOf edges from the IR are emitted as attribute sub declarations.
4. A validation error is thrown before writing output if a child/supertype attribute chain would require incompatible primitive value types.
5. npm run emit:structural is deterministic across two runs.
close_reason: Implemented and locally verified with generated schema/docs checks; TypeDB runtime validation remains tracked separately.

title: Cut ontology-vibemachine v2.0.0 against gist 3.0.0
description: Refresh ontology-vibemachine against gist 3.0.0, regenerate package metadata/docs, validate bootstrap, and cut the major v2.0.0 release.
design:
ontology-vibemachine is downstream of gist and should not be redesigned for this change unless bootstrap exposes incompatibility.

The schema already uses the revised relation specialization pattern, e.g. schema/vibemachine.tql submissionProvidedBy sub comesFromAgent and multiple sub hasParticipant relations. Main work is dependency/version refresh, generated docs refresh through ontology-gist shared package_contract tooling, and validation against gist v3.0.0. Because the dependency contract changes to a breaking gist major, vibemachine also releases as v2.0.0.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. package.json version is 2.0.0 and dependency on gist is >=3.0.0.
2. Generated vibemachine schema docs include role subtype metadata for existing relation specializations.
3. npm run validate:bootstrap passes in ontology-vibemachine.
4. npm run test:typedb-bootstrap passes with local gist v3.0.0 available.
5. Release commit/tag exist for vibemachine v2.0.0.
close_reason: ontology-vibemachine v2.0.0 release is committed and tagged locally against gist >=3.0.0.

title: Cut ontology-gist v3.0.0 major release
description: Regenerate, validate, and release ontology-gist as v3.0.0 after the structural hierarchy and documentation metadata changes land.
design:
Use the shared ontology-release flow from ../ontology-tooling/bin/ontology-release for the major gist release.

The release tool rewrites package.json versioned paths, runs refresh:package-contract, validate:bootstrap, test:typedb-bootstrap, optional migration validation, creates a release commit, and tags v<version>. Because this is a breaking schema contract change, use --version 3.0.0 rather than patch/minor bump. Ensure generated docs and reports are already semantically correct before invoking the final release.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. ontology-release dry-run or plan shows gist 2.0.4 -> 3.0.0 and expected versioned manifest renames.
2. Release validation runs refresh:package-contract, validate:bootstrap, and test:typedb-bootstrap successfully.
3. Final commit subject is 'Release gist v3.0.0'.
4. Git tag v3.0.0 exists locally.
5. If push is not performed, the bead records that release is local-only and lists the exact push command/next operator action.
close_reason: ontology-gist v3.0.0 release is committed and tagged locally.

title: Add hierarchy coverage validation to gist package checks
description: Add validation coverage so stale generated artifacts cannot pass when IR hierarchy edges are missing from emitted TypeDB schema or generated docs.
design:
Validation belongs primarily in ontology-gist because the hierarchy gap is in gist generation/validation, not ontology-tooling release orchestration.

Extend tools/gist_to_typeql/validate_bootstrap.mjs and/or supporting helpers to compare the source IR/model against emitted schema/docs. Keep checks deterministic and local: parse manifests/gist-v3.0.0.ir-summary.json or load the model, parse schema/gistCore.tql with the shared schema parser, and inspect generated docs text/structure. The checks should fail before TypeDB bootstrap when generated artifacts are stale or structurally incomplete.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. validate:bootstrap fails on the old flattened schema because it has 25 datatype edges in IR and 0 attribute sub declarations.
2. validate:bootstrap fails on the old standalone relation schema because it has 13 object edges in IR and 0 relation sub declarations/role specializations.
3. validate:bootstrap fails if generated schema docs omit attribute/relation/role subtype metadata for emitted schema edges.
4. validate:bootstrap passes after regeneration.
5. npm test still runs validate:bootstrap plus TypeDB bootstrap/migration checks.
close_reason: Hierarchy schema/docs validation and full TypeDB bootstrap/migration gates pass.

title: Update schema documentation metadata for subtype and role specialization
description: Investigate and update the self-describing documentation parser/data generation so generated docs accurately capture attribute subtype, relation subtype, and role specialization metadata.
design:
Files: schema/self-describing-schema.tql, tools/shared/schema_structure.mjs, data/*-schema-docs.tql, generated/apply-units/data/*-schema-docs.

The documentation schema already models every documented type/role as SchemaResource and has a generic schemaSubTypeOf relation. That appears sufficient for attribute subtype, relation subtype, and role specialization metadata. The actual gap is parser/data generation: parseTypeQLSchemaStructure() records entity/relation sub edges, records role resources from relates clauses, but currently parses attributes only when they have value declarations and discards the parent role in 'relates child as parent'.

Target design: make the shared parser faithfully recover TypeQL structural metadata from schema text and reuse existing schemaSubTypeOf for role-to-role subtype edges unless the decision task proves a dedicated relation is needed. Regenerate gist docs and vibemachine docs because both use the same parser path.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. parseTypeQLSchemaStructure() returns subtypeEdges for attribute child sub parent declarations.
2. parseTypeQLSchemaStructure() returns subtypeEdges for role specializations from relates childRole as parentRole.
3. Generated gist docs include schemaSubTypeOf records for all emitted attribute, relation, and role subtype edges.
4. Generated vibemachine docs include schemaSubTypeOf records for existing hand-authored role specializations such as submissionProvidedBy:submission -> comesFromAgent:comesFromAgentSubject.
5. No self-describing schema migration is introduced unless the documented decision says schemaSubTypeOf is insufficient.
close_reason: Documentation parser/schema-data work completed; generated gist and vibemachine docs now include attribute/relation/role subtype metadata.

title: Implement gist structural property hierarchy emission
description: Update the gist structural emitter so explicit rdfs:subPropertyOf edges are represented as TypeDB attribute and relation subtyping instead of flattened peer declarations.
design:
Files: tools/gist_to_typeql/emit_structural.mjs and generated schema/gistCore.tql.

Current code path: inferPropertyTypes() already reads property.subPropertyOf and propagates inherited domain/range information, but renderSchema() still emits all datatype properties as independent attribute value declarations and all object properties as standalone relations. buildEntityDefinitions() then adds owns/plays against those standalone labels and only prunes inherited entity-supertype capabilities.

Target design: introduce explicit property hierarchy helpers over model.resources.datatypeProperties and model.resources.objectProperties. Datatype roots emit 'attribute root value primitive'; datatype children emit 'attribute child sub parent'. Object roots emit standalone relation roles; object children emit 'relation child sub parent' with child subject/object roles specializing the corresponding parent roles. Capability generation and pruning must use the structural role/attribute hierarchy so owners/players are declared on valid direct capabilities without duplicating inherited equivalents.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. Regenerated schema/gistCore.tql contains 25 attribute subtype declarations corresponding to named datatype subPropertyOf edges in manifests/gist-v3.0.0.ir-summary.json.
2. Regenerated schema/gistCore.tql contains 13 relation subtype declarations corresponding to named object subPropertyOf edges.
3. Each relation subtype has two role specializations using 'relates <childRole> as <parentRole>'.
4. No child datatype property with a mapped named superproperty emits a peer 'value <primitive>' declaration.
5. npm run validate:bootstrap and npm run test:typedb-bootstrap pass.
close_reason: Structural datatype and object property hierarchy emission is implemented and TypeDB bootstrap/load checks pass.

title: Release gist 3.0.0 and vibemachine 2.0.0 for structural inheritance support
description: Major release program to preserve explicit gist property hierarchies as TypeDB structural inheritance and refresh downstream vibemachine against the new gist contract.
design:
Scope: major-version release program across ontology-gist and ontology-vibemachine.

The breaking contract is that explicit gist hierarchy edges must become TypeDB structural schema edges whenever the source resource maps to a TypeDB type. The core implementation lives in ontology-gist because the current gap is in tools/gist_to_typeql/emit_structural.mjs and tools/shared/schema_structure.mjs. ontology-vibemachine is downstream: it already hand-authors relation subtype + role-specialization patterns, but its generated documentation metadata currently drops role specialization because the shared schema parser ignores the 'as parentRole' portion of relates clauses.

Release sequencing is mandatory: implement and release gist v3.0.0 first; then update ontology-vibemachine to depend on gist >=3.0.0 and release vibemachine v2.0.0. ontology-tooling remains release orchestration only unless validation discovers a shared release-flow defect.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance tests:
1. gist v3.0.0 generated schema preserves every mapped datatype and object property hierarchy edge from the IR as TypeDB structural inheritance.
2. generated documentation metadata for gist and vibemachine includes entity, relation, attribute, and role subtype edges.
3. gist validation fails if IR hierarchy edges are missing from schema or docs.
4. npm test passes in ontology-gist after regeneration.
5. vibemachine package metadata depends on gist >=3.0.0, generated artifacts are refreshed, and npm test passes in ontology-vibemachine.
6. release commits/tags exist for gist v3.0.0 and vibemachine v2.0.0, or release dry-runs document any operator-controlled push/tag blocker.
close_reason: Implemented structural inheritance support and cut local gist v3.0.0 plus vibemachine v2.0.0 releases.

title: Seed GIST executable corpus for ontology agents
description: Create the first GIST-owned executable corpus: fixture overlays, known-good TypeQL examples, negative repair examples, and mise tasks that validate/export examples through the shared corpus runner.
design:
## Scope
This repo owns GIST-grounded corpus content. The corpus should teach agents and developers how to model and query against GIST using executable TypeQL examples rather than passive prose.

## Corpus Layout
Add:

```text
corpus/
  manifest.json
  fixtures/
    meeting-decisions-schema.tql
    meeting-decisions-data.tql
  queries/
    meeting-decisions.json
  negative/
    typedb2-get.json
    missing-relation-roles.json
```

## Initial Content
Include examples for the modeling pattern that recently failed in Lingo:
- Meeting as a domain subtype grounded in the GIST Activity area
- Decision as a domain subtype grounded in the GIST Content area, not Activity
- a relation with explicit roles connecting the meeting/activity-like thing to the decision/content-like thing
- a read query answering which meetings produced decisions
- at least one prompt-export-eligible select or fetch example

If exact Meeting/Decision labels are not in GIST, define them only in corpus fixture overlays as domain subtypes grounded in GIST. Do not hand-edit generated GIST schema outputs.

## Mise Tasks
Add repo-local tasks:

```bash
mise run corpus:test
mise run corpus:export
```

Both delegate to the shared ontology corpus runner. They must be deterministic and must not call an LLM.

## Capability Contract
This bead exports `gist-corpus-seed` when the initial GIST corpus exists, validates against real TypeDB, and exports prompt-ready examples.
acceptance_criteria:
- `corpus/` exists with manifest, fixtures, known-good queries, and separated negative/repair examples
- Corpus includes Meeting/Activity + Decision/Content examples grounded in GIST
- Known-good query answers which meetings produced decisions against real fixture data
- `mise run corpus:test` validates the corpus through the shared runner without using an LLM
- `mise run corpus:export` writes a deterministic prompt artifact under `generated/corpus/`
- Generated GIST schema/data outputs are not hand-edited for corpus-only examples
- Bead is labeled `export:gist-corpus-seed` and can be shipped with `bd ship gist-corpus-seed` after closure

title: Add ontology corpus runner CLI surface
description:
Provide the durable Rust corpus runner and operator surface for executable ontology corpora. The runner lives in this repo so OneApp, Lingo, and other Vibe Machine products can embed `vibe-ontology` directly; the `ont` binary is the operator-facing CLI/TUI.

DESIGN
## Scope
ontology-tooling owns the Rust workspace that exposes:
- `vibe-ontology` library crate — corpus model, discovery, validation, prompt-export. Zero CLI/TUI dependencies; safe to embed in OneApp, Lingo, etc.
- `ont` binary crate — unified CLI/TUI that depends on `vibe-ontology` plus clap/ratatui/tokio.

## v0 Command Surface
```bash
ont --help
ont version [--format json|text]
ont completions <shell>
ont tui                                    # interactive TUI scaffold
ont corpus list     --repo <path> [--tag <t>] [--item <id>] [--format json|text]
ont corpus validate --repo <path>                              [--format json|text]
```

`ont corpus generate` and TypeDB-backed execution (`ont corpus run`, prompt export) are deliberately deferred — see follow-up beads.

## Output Discipline
- stdout is data only (single JSON value per invocation when `--format json`).
- stderr carries `tracing` progress and errors.
- Non-zero exit on any validation or runtime failure.

## Architecture
- Workspace layout follows `docs/rust-workspace.md`.
- Library/binary split keeps clap/ratatui out of `vibe-ontology` consumers.
- TUI follows the foundation spec: TerminalSession (RAII), panic hook, unified event loop, App update/draw split.
- `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide; clippy `-D warnings` gated.

## Out of Scope (follow-up beads)
- `ont corpus generate` (LLM-backed)
- TypeDB-backed corpus execution
- Prompt-export artifact emission via `ont corpus export`
- Additional `ont` subcommands (packages, ontology explorer, etc.)
- Distribution/release of the `ont` binary

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Cargo workspace at repo root with `crates/vibe-ontology/` and `crates/ont/`
- `cargo build --workspace` succeeds; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes
- `cargo test --workspace` passes (lib unit + integration tests + assert_cmd CLI tests + TUI app tests)
- `unsafe_code = "forbid"` set workspace-wide
- `vibe-ontology` exposes corpus model, `discover_corpus`, `select_exportable_items`, `PromptExportArtifact`, `ItemFilter`, `Error` — without clap/ratatui in its public surface
- `ont` binary supports `--help`, `version`, `completions <shell>`, `tui`, `corpus list`, `corpus validate`
- `ont corpus *` commands shape-validate the manifest, fixture references, and item shape; `--tag` and `--item` filters work
- stdout/stderr discipline holds: `--format json` emits a single JSON value to stdout; tracing logs go to stderr
- TUI scaffold exits cleanly on `q`, `Esc`, and `Ctrl-C`; panic hook restores the terminal
- mise.toml pins Rust 1.83 and exposes `mise run build`, `mise run cargo-test`, `mise run lint`
- Docs: `docs/rust-workspace.md` (layout) and `docs/corpus-runner.md` (command surface, expected ontology repo layout, integration)
- Bead is labeled `export:ontology-corpus-runner` and ships with `bd ship ontology-corpus-runner` after closure
design:
## Scope
This repo owns the shared command/tooling surface that ontology repos use from mise. It should expose deterministic corpus operations without making each ontology repo duplicate bootstrap, filtering, reporting, or export logic.

## Boundary
The durable Rust domain implementation is tracked from OneWorkspace under one-2xg.16.13 / rust/ontology-core. This ontology-tooling bead owns the repo-local tooling bridge and operator surface:
- command entrypoints usable from ontology repos
- stable invocation contract for `mise run corpus:test` and `mise run corpus:export`
- documentation of expected repo layout and generated artifact paths
- transitional wrapping of existing Node/package tooling where needed

## Commands To Provide
Expose a command surface equivalent to:

```bash
ontology corpus test --repo <ontology-repo> [--tag <tag>] [--item <id>] [--database <name>] [--keep-db] [--format json|text]
ontology corpus export --repo <ontology-repo> [--tag <tag>] [--output <path>] [--format json|text]
```

If the Rust binary lives outside this repo during the transition, this repo may provide thin bin wrappers or mise-friendly scripts that locate and call it. The wrapper must preserve stdout/stderr discipline: data on stdout, progress/logging on stderr.

## Capability Contract
This bead exports `ontology-corpus-runner` when ontology repos can call a stable command to validate and export corpus examples. The capability is considered shipped only after at least ontology-gist can use the command from its repo-local mise tasks.

## Integration Notes
Coordinate with:
- OneWorkspace `one-2xg.16.13` for Rust core/CLI implementation details.
- ontology-gist corpus bead for the first real corpus consumer.
acceptance_criteria:
- A stable corpus command surface exists for `corpus test` and `corpus export`
- Commands accept `--repo` and can target ontology-gist without repo-specific hardcoding
- Commands preserve stdout/stderr discipline and support JSON output for agent harnesses
- ontology-gist can delegate `mise run corpus:test` and `mise run corpus:export` to this surface
- Documentation explains corpus repo layout, command examples, and generated prompt artifact path
- Bead is labeled `export:ontology-corpus-runner` and can be shipped with `bd ship ontology-corpus-runner` after closure
notes:
Direction shifted mid-implementation (2026-05-04): the durable Rust corpus runner now lives in this repo (not OneWorkspace), exposing `vibe-ontology` as a reusable library and `ont` as the CLI/TUI binary. one-2xg.16.13's Rust workspace direction is therefore relocated here; that bead should be updated or split to reflect the move.

Cross-repo: ontology-gist gist-u1j depends on this surface for its `corpus:test` mise task. ontology-gist will eventually expose `corpus:test` and other tasks that delegate to the `ont corpus *` commands.
close_reason: v0 ships: vibe-ontology lib + ont CLI/TUI binary, shape-only corpus validation, all tests + clippy green. Follow-ups filed for export/typedb-exec/generate/tui-browser.

title: TypeQL3 prompt guide and fixture corpus
description: Create a compact runtime TypeQL 3 generation guide and an executable corpus of known-good TypeQL examples so Lingo synthesis learns from validated examples rather than prose-only prompt rules.
design: Add a shared TypeQL3PromptGuide used by SchemaGeneratorAgent and any direct Lingo proposal prompt path. Extract only runtime-relevant material from .claude/skills/typedb/SKILL.md: root kinds, schema definition forms, relation/role/player syntax, attribute ownership, CQ query output clauses, reserved-word pitfalls, and bad-to-good TypeDB 2 habit corrections. Add a fixture corpus of canonical TypeQL 3 examples for entity specialization, relation roles/plays, produced-content, part/whole or membership precedent, attribute ownership, select/fetch/reduce CQs, and relation traversal. Fixtures should be executable against TypeDB or otherwise parsed/validated by existing TypeDB-backed test harnesses; avoid passive markdown-only examples. Remove contradictory runtime prompt guidance such as separate 'X sub Y' subtype assertions when the TypeDB 3 kind-keyword form is required.
acceptance_criteria: A TypeQL3PromptGuide exists as a shared runtime prompt component and is injected into SchemaGeneratorAgent plus any direct Lingo schema proposal path that can still generate TypeQL. The guide includes compact known-good TypeQL 3 examples and explicit bad-to-good corrections for the live failure classes. A fixture corpus exists under OntologyTests or support fixtures and is validated by deterministic tests against real parser/TypeDB paths where practical. Tests assert the runtime prompts include the guide, include canonical examples, exclude TypeDB 2 habits, and no longer contain contradictory 'X sub Y' guidance. The corpus can be extended when future live LLM regressions are found.
notes: Corpus source changed: prompt/fixture examples should preferentially consume exported examples from one-2xg.16.13's ontology-gist corpus lab artifact once available. The prompt guide can still include hand-curated TypeQL language examples, but GIST-grounded examples should be executable corpus items, not ad hoc prompt text.

title: Dedicated live LLM test task
description: Live Lingo/LLM tests should run only through an explicit mise task, not by setting an environment flag on the normal test task. This makes provider calls and cost/latency obvious.
design: Add a dedicated mise task for live LLM tests, likely mise run test-live-llm, that sets the live-test sentinel and invokes the targeted Ontology live regression suite through the normal xcodebuild/xcsift path. Remove or neutralize ONE_RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS behavior from the regular mise run test path so normal targeted/all tests cannot accidentally run live provider tests. Keep Swift Testing-level gating as a second line of defense.
acceptance_criteria: A named mise task exists for live LLM tests and documents that it calls the real provider. mise run test Ontology without the live task removes/does not create the live sentinel and skips live tests. The dedicated task creates the sentinel for the run, cleans it up afterward, and runs the live Lingo regression selector. Targeted default test pass/skips; the live task reaches the live test path.
close_reason: Added a dedicated mise run test-live-llm task for live LLM integration tests. Regular mise run test now clears/ignores the old public ONE_RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS switch, so live tests only run through the explicit task. The live task creates the sentinel for the run, invokes the Ontology live regression selector, and cleans the sentinel afterward.

title: Fix live Meeting synthesis TypeQL generation
description: The new opt-in live LLM regression for the Meeting prompt reaches the real service/provider/TypeDB path and currently fails. The live provider generated invalid TypeQL across the bounded retry loop: a CQ query using TypeDB 2 get syntax, schema deltas using TypeDB 2 style declarations such as 'Meeting sub Activity;' and 'meetingProducedDecision sub relation', and no accepted proposal.
design: Use the live regression output to harden generator prompting/repair and deterministic tests. The generator should emit TypeDB 3 define syntax such as 'entity Meeting sub Activity;' and CQ TypeQL that compiles under TypeDB 3 query syntax. The retry loop should feed Judge parse feedback strongly enough that attempt 2/3 correct syntax rather than reusing TypeDB 2 forms.
acceptance_criteria: With ONE_RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS=1, LingoLiveSynthesisRegressionTests for the Meeting prompt no longer fails with bounded three-attempt rejection. Add deterministic coverage for the observed TypeDB 2 syntax regressions before relying on the live test as the only guard.
notes: Implemented a synthesis-boundary TypeQL repair pass for observed live LLM failures: TypeDB 2 subtype shorthand, relation root shorthand, standalone relates, entity plays shorthand, old get CQ output, context-grounded top-level Meeting, and Decision-as-Content consistency. Strengthened SchemaGeneratorAgent TypeDB 3 instructions. Validation: mise run test Ontology -- -only-testing:OntologyTests/SynthesisWorkflowTests -only-testing:OntologyTests/SchemaGeneratorAgentTests; mise run test Ontology -- -only-testing:OntologyTests/SynthesisWorkflowTests -only-testing:OntologyTests/LingoLiveSynthesisRegressionTests; mise run test-live-llm.

title: Live LLM regression for Meeting synthesis failure
description: The exact prompt 'I want to model a Meeting as a kind of Activity. It should let me ask which meetings produced decisions.' failed twice in manual Lingo sessions. The first fix only added deterministic tests; it did not create an opt-in live LLM integration test that reproduces the real provider path.
design: Add an opt-in live integration test gated by ONE_RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS=1. The test should use DefaultMuseRuntime, OntologyAgentService, a live TypeDB fixture sandbox, and the exact user prompt from the failing transcripts. It should assert the turn does not end in the repeated ApplyToShadow TypeQL syntax-error rejection loop, and ideally produces a proposal/clarification with actionable diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: A disabled-by-default live LLM test exists for the exact failing Meeting prompt. Default test runs skip it. When enabled, it exercises the same service-level Lingo path as the app and fails if the output or synthesis metadata contains the three-attempt TypeQL syntax parse rejection loop.
close_reason: Added a reusable opt-in live LLM scenario harness for the exact failing Meeting prompt. The harness uses DefaultMuseRuntime, OntologyAgentService, LingoSystemPrompt, LingoAgent.makeTools, a live TypeDB sandbox, and diagnostic JSONL capture. Updated the test wrapper/scheme so ONE_RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS=1 actually reaches the test process via a sentinel file. Default targeted run skips; opt-in live run now executes and reproduces a bounded synthesis failure, tracked in one-537.11.

title: Surface synthesis rejection trail in Lingo
description: When Lingo routes a schema-design turn through SynthesisWorkflow and Judge rejects every generated delta, the user only sees 'Judge did not accept after 3 attempts.' and the diagnostic JSONL lacks generator outputs or rejection reasons. This makes synthesis failures non-actionable.
design: Record the synthesis verdict, rejection trail, and final Judge reason in both transcript and diagnostic output. For bounded rejection, present a validation-failure or clarification-style assistant message with the actual rejection reasons instead of a bare completed output. Preserve the existing proposal path for accepted deltas and the old chat/tool path for non-schema turns.
acceptance_criteria: A rejected synthesis turn records a Lingo transcript item containing the bounded-retry rejection trail and final reason. The completed event output and diagnostics include the same actionable reason text. Tests cover an all-rejected synthesis workflow and assert the user does not only receive 'Judge did not accept after 3 attempts.'
close_reason: Rejected synthesis turns now surface the bounded retry rejection trail in the Lingo transcript and completed event output, and completed diagnostic events include synthesis metadata in both full and summary traces. Added regression tests for all-rejected synthesis and diagnostic metadata recording.

title: Per-bead validation matrix for synthesis runtime
description: Attach a fast/integration/epic-close validation matrix to each one-537 child bead so agents can move quickly without guessing when to run targeted versus full tests.
design:
## Implementation Shape
Document a validation matrix on each child bead in one-537. Each matrix should name:

- Fast required tests: the smallest local test slice expected while implementing that bead.
- Integration checkpoint tests: broader tests owed when the bead joins sibling work or crosses runtime boundaries.
- Epic close tests: expensive/full tests owed before the whole one-537 epic closes.

The matrix should preserve the repo's testing policy: no mocks, real implementations, transcript fixtures and TypeDB-backed integration where practical, and live-LLM coverage only behind an explicit opt-in flag.

This bead is complete when the matrices are attached to the existing child beads and a future agent can pick up any one-537 child without asking which level of tests to run.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every existing one-537 child bead has notes naming fast required tests, integration checkpoint tests, and epic close tests.
- The matrix explicitly keeps live-LLM tests opt-in and out of the default loop.
- Dependencies and ready work remain clear after adding the matrix.
notes:
## Validation Matrix
Fast required tests: bd show one-537 --children and bd show each child to verify matrices are attached.
Integration checkpoint tests: not applicable; this bead is documentation/coordination for test speed.
Epic close tests: verify one-537 children still carry current validation notes before closing the epic.
close_reason: Attached fast, integration, and epic-close validation matrices to each one-537 child bead.

title: Default Lingo schema turns use synthesis workflow
description: Route user-facing Lingo schema-design turns through ElicitationWorkflow and SynthesisWorkflow instead of the monolithic prompt manually sequencing granular tools.
design:
## Feature Scope
Detect schema-design turns in the Lingo chat service and route them through the conversational synthesis runtime: elicitation, GIST alignment, pattern retrieval, schema generation, judging, migration routing, and proposal/commit handling.

The existing monolithic prompt path can remain for general Q&A and direct inspection, but schema evolution should not depend on the model manually loading low-level tools in the correct order.

The user-facing result should be one of: a useful clarification question, a schema proposal visible in the Lingo explorer, an accepted/committed delta when explicitly allowed, or a clear validation failure with reasons. Max-iteration exhaustion should be treated as a runtime failure to investigate, not as user guidance to ask a narrower question.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lingo schema-design turns enter the synthesis workflow by default.
- General ontology Q&A and inspection turns still work without forcing synthesis.
- Proposal output opens or updates the Lingo proposal browser when applicable.
- Max-iteration failures no longer produce misleading “try a narrower question” guidance for orchestration failures.
- Regression tests cover routing for schema-design, general Q&A, proposal revision, and validation failure turns.
notes:
## Validation Matrix
Fast required tests: routing tests for schema-design versus general Q&A turns; assert schema turns enter synthesis workflow and non-schema inspection turns remain usable.
Integration checkpoint tests: deterministic end-to-end Lingo tests covering schema proposal creation, proposal revision, browser focus/update, validation rejection, and clarification escalation.
Epic close tests: full Ontology test target, app-level smoke if practical, and opt-in live-LLM tests over curated Lingo prompts.
close_reason: Default schema-design turns with an active sandbox now bypass the monolithic tool-orchestration path and run SynthesisWorkflow with user-confirmation required; accepted deltas are recorded as Lingo Explorer proposals, while inspection/query/apply turns stay on the existing path. Covered routing, proposal browser output, and non-routing Q&A detection in LingoAgentTests.

title: Sandboxed TypeQL ontology workbench
description: Give Lingo a broad, safe TypeQL workbench analogous to bash for ontology work: inspect, probe, try deltas, verify CQs, and discard shadow state.
design:
## Feature Scope
Provide a coarse tool/workflow surface that lets an ontology agent reason experimentally inside TypeDB without committing live changes. The workbench should support creating or cloning a shadow database, inspecting schema slices, running arbitrary read/probe TypeQL, attempting schema define/undefine fragments, inspecting TypeDB errors, compiling/executing competency-question TypeQL, and discarding shadow state.

This is intentionally broader than current granular tools, but still safe: it operates on sandbox/shadow databases by default and commits only through the validated Committer path.

The workbench should be usable both by the synthesis workflow and by future diagnostic UI/tests. It should produce structured traces so failures are debuggable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Agent runtime can create/use a shadow TypeDB workspace for exploratory ontology operations.
- Workbench supports schema inspection, read/probe TypeQL, candidate schema application, error inspection, CQ execution, and discard.
- Workbench operations are structured and traceable in logs/tests.
- No live schema mutation occurs except through the validated commit path.
notes:
## Validation Matrix
Fast required tests: workbench tests against real temporary TypeDB shadow databases for schema inspection, read/probe TypeQL, candidate define/undefine attempts, TypeDB error capture, CQ execution, and discard semantics.
Integration checkpoint tests: run JudgeStep/SynthesisWorkflow slices using the workbench as the shadow execution substrate; verify live schema is untouched on failed probes.
Epic close tests: full Ontology test target and opt-in live-LLM smoke that uses the workbench path for exploratory schema synthesis.
close_reason: Added TypeQLOntologyWorkbench for shadow TypeDB exploration, moved JudgeStep shadow apply/schema/CQ checks onto it, and covered schema probe/error/CQ/discard semantics with live TypeDB tests.

title: Competency-question-first proposal validation
description: Make claimed CQ coverage the primary validation contract for schema proposals instead of generic candidate sanity checks.
design:
## Implementation Shape
Schema proposals should carry explicit claims about which competency questions they answer. Validation should apply the candidate delta to a shadow TypeDB state, compile each claimed CQ's TypeQL form, execute it where possible, and mark claimed coverage as accepted only when the query succeeds against the post-delta state.

Generic sanity checks may remain as supplementary diagnostics, but they should not be treated as proof that a proposal satisfies the user's modeling need.

The default chat path, proposal browser state, JudgeStep, and any validate_candidate-style tooling should agree on this contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- Candidate validation applies deltas to shadow TypeDB state before checking claimed CQs.
- Claimed answered CQs fail validation if their TypeQL form does not compile or execute against the post-delta shadow state.
- Generic count/sanity checks are supplementary and cannot mark a proposal as CQ-satisfying by themselves.
- Tests cover both accepted CQ coverage and false claimed coverage.
notes:
## Validation Matrix
Fast required tests: CQ validation tests that apply candidate deltas to shadow TypeDB state and verify claimed CQs compile/execute; include false-claim failures and malformed TypeQL forms.
Integration checkpoint tests: run proposal validation through JudgeStep and any validate_candidate-compatible public tool path to ensure the same CQ-first contract is enforced.
Epic close tests: full Ontology test target plus opt-in live-LLM smoke confirming accepted proposals cite verified CQ coverage.
close_reason: Candidate validation now applies proposed TypeQL to a shadow workbench before verifying claimed CQs, records CQ pass/fail evidence, and rejects propose_schema_change when claimed CQ validation fails. Covered accepted and false CQ claims through targeted schema-evolution tool tests.

title: Opt-in Lingo synthesis regression harness
description: Add a test harness that catches brittle Lingo schema-design failures, including max-iteration transcript regressions, without putting live LLM calls in the default test loop.
design:
## Implementation Shape
Create regression coverage for Lingo schema-design turns at two levels.

Deterministic integration tests should run by default and use real app services where practical: transcript replay, real tool registry, real schema/sandbox service boundaries, and real TypeDB test databases. These tests should assert orchestration outcomes such as tool budget use, surfaced proposal/clarification, browser focus request, and absence of misleading max-iteration guidance.

Live-LLM tests should be opt-in behind an explicit environment flag such as ONE_RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS=1 and should be excluded from normal mise/make test targets. They should use the production LLM path with a small curated prompt set and real TypeDB sandbox. The goal is not exhaustive correctness; it is catching prompt/tool-regression failures before a human hits them.

The 2026-05-04 Lingo transcript that exhausted 10 iterations before proposing anything should be represented as a fixture or minimized reproduction. The expected behavior is a useful schema proposal, an explicit need-for-clarification response, or a domain validation failure before iteration exhaustion.

Follow the repo testing rule: no mocks. Use real implementations, fakes/stubs only when they have real behavior and preserve the production contract.
acceptance_criteria:
- Default test target includes deterministic Lingo orchestration regression coverage with no live LLM dependency.
- Live-LLM Lingo tests only run when an explicit opt-in flag is set.
- The 2026-05-04 max-iteration failure scenario is covered by a regression fixture or minimized equivalent.
- Failing orchestration produces actionable test output identifying whether the failure is tool loading, retrieval quality, sandbox setup, proposal generation, validation, or UI handoff.
- Tests use real implementations per the no-mocks policy.
notes:
## Validation Matrix
Fast required tests: deterministic Lingo orchestration regression tests for transcript/minimized prompt replay; assert no max-iteration exhaustion, no misleading narrow-question guidance, and a proposal/clarification/validation-failure outcome. Keep live LLM disabled.
Integration checkpoint tests: run the Ontology synthesis/orchestration test slice that exercises real tool registry, sandbox boundary, proposal state, and transcript diagnostics once the harness is wired to production code.
Epic close tests: run the full Ontology test target plus opt-in live-LLM smoke tests with ONE_RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS=1 against curated schema-design prompts.
close_reason: Added deterministic Lingo diagnostic regression coverage for max-iteration-before-proposal traces, gated live-LLM posture validation behind ONE_RUN_LIVE_LLM_TESTS=1, and changed max-iteration guidance to identify orchestration/setup failure instead of telling users to ask a narrower question.

title: Unified schema synthesis context assembly
description: Replace fragmented context gathering with one synthesis-context operation that gives agents the schema slice, CQs, deltas, GIST candidates, patterns, and relevant transcript context for a turn.
design:
## Implementation Shape
Define a production context assembler for Lingo schema-design turns. Given a user turn and active session, it should produce a typed context object containing: relevant live schema slice, active sandbox identity, recent conversation turns, open competency questions, prior accepted deltas, rejected alternatives and judge feedback, candidate GIST anchors, retrieved ontology patterns, and proposal/browser state.

This should become the input boundary for the synthesis workflow so the model does not manually call search_ontology_memory, getSchemaModel, create_sandbox, and proposal tools in an ad hoc order. Individual low-level tools can remain available for inspection, but the runtime should prefer this coarse context operation for modeling turns.

The context object should be inspectable in tests and small enough for prompt use. Retrieval failures should be represented explicitly, not hidden as empty context.
acceptance_criteria:
- A typed synthesis context object exists and is used by schema-design orchestration.
- Context includes schema slice, active CQs, prior deltas, rejected alternatives, GIST candidates, pattern candidates, and relevant transcript turns.
- Retrieval and sandbox failures are explicit fields with actionable diagnostics.
- Tests cover a turn that previously required multiple manual tool loads and assert the assembled context is sufficient for downstream synthesis.
notes:
## Validation Matrix
Fast required tests: context assembler tests using real schema/session fixtures; assert schema slice, active CQs, prior deltas, rejected alternatives, GIST candidates, pattern candidates, and transcript turns are present with explicit diagnostics for missing retrieval pieces.
Integration checkpoint tests: run context assembly through the deterministic Lingo harness from one-537.1 and through downstream generator input construction.
Epic close tests: full Ontology test target; live-LLM smoke verifies generated context is sufficient for a real schema-design turn without manual low-level tool sequencing.
close_reason: Added typed synthesis context assembly with schema slice, open CQs, prior deltas, transcript/proposal context, elicitation outputs, diagnostics, generator input rendering, and SynthesisWorkflowInput integration; covered by SynthesisWorkflowTests.

title: Conversational ontology synthesis runtime
description: Make Lingo's user-facing schema-design experience use the conversational schema-synthesis architecture instead of the brittle monolithic tool-dispatch path.
design:
## Concept
Lingo should behave like an expert ontologist operating a durable TypeQL synthesis workbench, not like a generic chat model manually sequencing narrow tools. The runtime should center the loop from the Conversational Schema Synthesis design: elicitation, GIST alignment, pattern retrieval, schema generation, TypeDB-backed judging, migration synthesis, and transactional commit.

## Boundaries
In scope: schema-design turns in Lingo, competency-question capture and verification, shadow TypeDB validation, GIST/pattern retrieval quality, proposal display handoff, durable synthesis state, and regression tests for brittle orchestration failures.

Out of scope: replacing TypeDB, maintaining SHACL/OWL runtime representations, coupling the ontology loop to Beads task lifecycle, or giving production users unbounded shell access.

## Architectural Direction
The default user path should route schema-design turns through an explicit synthesis workflow. Low-level tools remain available for inspection and administration, but they should not be the primary orchestration mechanism for ontology modeling turns.

The system needs a broad but safe ontology workbench analogous to bash for Claude Code: create a shadow workspace, inspect schema context, run arbitrary TypeQL read/probe queries, try schema deltas, inspect errors, verify competency questions, and discard or commit through controlled paths.

The system should become accretive by persisting competency questions, accepted deltas, rejected alternatives, user decisions, GIST alignments, pattern choices, and judge feedback as future synthesis context.

## Prior Art
RIGOR (Nayyeri et al., Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Ontologies from Relational Databases, arXiv:2506.01232, 2025) contributes the generate/judge/retry loop and CQ-based ontology quality framing.

SchemaAgent (arXiv:2503.23886, 2025) contributes multi-agent role decomposition for schema construction, adapted here to ontology elicitation, alignment, retrieval, generation, judging, migration, and commit.

Migrator (Wang, Feng, Bavishi, Dillig et al., Synthesizing Database Programs for Schema Refactoring, arXiv:1904.05498, 2019) contributes value-correspondence thinking for non-additive schema evolution.
acceptance_criteria:
- Schema-design turns in Lingo route through the synthesis architecture by default.
- A transcript like the 2026-05-04 max-iteration failure is covered by regression tests and no longer exhausts iterations before producing a useful proposal, clarification, or explicit validation failure.
- Competency questions are captured, persisted, and used as the primary verification contract for claimed schema progress.
- Candidate schema deltas are judged in shadow TypeDB state before any live commit.
- GIST and pattern knowledge are explicit, inspectable, and reusable in future turns.
- Live-LLM coverage exists behind an opt-in flag and is excluded from the default fast test loop.

title: Show invalid Lingo schema proposals in browser
description: Lingo proposal validation can fail before propose_schema_change records or opens the proposal, leaving users with only a tool error and no Lingo browser artifact to inspect. The 2026-05-04 lingo transcript also shows candidate validation using invalid TypeDB 3 'isa thing' query.
design: Adjust propose_schema_change so failed local/role/candidate validation records the supplied TypeQL as a visible proposal in Lingo Explorer before returning an error. Keep apply gated: failed validation must not be confirmable or applyable as if ready. Replace validate_candidate's generic 'match  isa thing' probe with TypeDB 3-valid schema-derived count queries. Add Swift Testing coverage for both visible failed proposals and the absence of the invalid 'isa thing' validation query.
acceptance_criteria: Given a proposal with invalid role coverage, the tool opens Lingo Explorer and currentLingoProposal contains the TypeQL for inspection while the tool still fails. validate_candidate never emits a query containing 'isa thing'. Relevant Ontology tests pass through xcsift.
close_reason: Fixed Lingo proposal failures so invalid proposals stay visible in the Lingo Explorer with validationFailed status, disabled confirm/apply for failed proposals, and removed the invalid TypeDB 3 isa thing validation query.

title: Lingo run_read_query lacks TypeDB-3 syntax guidance — emits TypeDB-2 forms
description:
Across 5 distinct sessions in the corpus 2026-04-25 → 2026-05-04, Lingo emits run_read_query calls in TypeDB-2 syntax that TypeDB 3 rejects with [TQL03]. Concrete bad queries pulled directly from the transcripts:

Session 2026-04-25/lingo-20260425T235402Z-b13c8c36.jsonl @ 23:54:28Z:
  match \$r isa VibeGitRepository; get \$r; count;     — trailing count; after get
  match \$r isa VibeGitRepository; count;              — count without get
  match \$r isa VibeGitRepository; get;                — bare get;

Session 2026-04-26/lingo-20260426T233257Z-5f302bf3.jsonl @ 23:47:00Z:
  match \$vet isa VibeEngineeringTask; \$vet sub? \$super; get \$vet;   — sub? wildcard operator (TypeDB 2)
