  match \$sub sub VibeEngineeringTask; get \$sub;                       — sub constraint behaves differently in TypeDB 3
  match \$rel type decomposesFeature; get \$rel;                        — get statement form

Session 2026-04-27/lingo-20260427T235129Z-ebbba147.jsonl @ 2026-04-28T01:09:20-25Z:
  Three retries within the same turn iterating through `get \$x;`, `fetch \$x;`, then `links: \$parent` until something parses — the agent has no anchor for the canonical TypeDB-3 form.

Root cause is two-fold:
1. `RunReadQueryTool.description` in `OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/QueryTools.swift:15-17` is just "Execute a read-only TypeQL query against a named database. Returns a row list." — no syntax pointers, no canonical forms.
2. `LingoSystemPrompt.swift:51` documents TypeDB-3 root declaration syntax but does NOT cover read-query syntax. The model's pre-training defaults to TypeDB-2; without prompt counter-pressure it regresses.
design:
1. Prompt: add a read-query syntax canon section to `LingoSystemPrompt.swift`, parallel to the line-51 root-declaration guidance. Include canonical TypeDB-3 read-query forms with worked examples (5-10 lines):
   - `match … fetch { name: \$x.name };` for projection
   - `match … select \$x;` for variable bindings
   - `match … reduce \$count = count;` for aggregates
   - explicit `sub` chains in match clauses (no `sub?` wildcard operator)
   - no trailing `count;` after `get` (deprecated form)

2. Tool description: anchor to canonical form. Update `RunReadQueryTool.description` to "Execute a TypeDB 3 read-only TypeQL query (`match … select|fetch|reduce …`) against a named database." This is the model's first-line reference when it picks the tool.

3. Validation: lightweight syntax pre-check in `RunReadQueryTool.execute` (`OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/QueryTools.swift:15-...`). Before sending to the driver, scan the query for known-bad patterns and reject with an error message naming the TypeDB-3 replacement:
   - trailing `count;` after `get` → suggest `reduce \$count = count;`
   - `sub?` operator → reject with explanation
   - bare `get;` → require explicit variable list
   Cost: ~1ms per query; turns three failed turns into zero.

4. Optional follow-on (separate child if desired): a canned `read_query_examples(schema: ...)` tool that returns 3-5 TypeDB-3 read-query templates against the active schema. Cheap to implement; breaks the iteration-blind loop seen in the 2026-04-27 session.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Focused test: RunReadQueryTool.execute with `match \$r isa X; get \$r; count;` returns a syntax error citing the TypeDB-3 form (`reduce \$count = count;`) before any driver round-trip.
2. Focused test: same for `sub?` operator and bare `get;`.
3. Updated LingoSystemPrompt.swift includes the read-query syntax section; regression test asserts the canonical examples are present (parallel pattern to the test added by one-2xg.38.12 for root-declaration guidance).
4. Updated RunReadQueryTool.description references TypeDB 3 explicitly and lists the canonical query verbs.
5. Transcript-replay against 2026-04-25/lingo-20260425T235402Z-b13c8c36.jsonl shows zero TypeDB-2-form run_read_query calls reaching the driver.
close_reason: Added TypeDB 3 read-query prompt/tool guidance and preflight rejection for TypeDB 2 get/count/sub? forms; query tool and prompt tests cover the guidance.

title: Lingo loses Membrane KV-swap error reason on resolve_pointer failures
description:
In session /Users/kenpo/.config/one/sessions/lingo/2026-05-04/lingo-20260504T120550Z-147797a3.jsonl, resolve_pointer failed three times — at 12:11:47Z, 12:11:49Z, and 12:26:26Z — each surfaced to the agent as `Tool 'resolve_pointer' failed: The operation couldn't be completed. (MembraneCore.MembraneError error 8.)`.

Error case 8 in `Vendor/Swarm/.build/checkouts/Membrane/Sources/MembraneCore/Errors/MembraneError.swift:9-36` is `kvSwapIOError(reason: String)`, NOT `pointerResolutionFailed` (which is case 9). So the failure mode is a KV-swap I/O error in the Membrane runtime — surfaced as a generic NSError with the `reason: String` payload thrown away on the way out. The agent only sees `error 8`, making diagnosis from transcript impossible.

Recovery: agent calls membrane_load_tool_schema then re-issues the original tool. Works, but adds two extra iterations and ~5s of latency per turn. Today's session pays this tax twice (turns 2 and 5).

Pointer IDs that failed: ptr_6dc71f64d7da, ptr_2026a691b9d5, ptr_859c88f34785. Each was issued by a prior propose_schema_change result and should have been resolvable in the same session.
design:
Three coordinated fixes, in order of decreasing scope-safety.

1. Surface the reason text (low-risk, lands first).
   The Membrane error bridge currently maps the Swift error to NSError with no userInfo, so the `reason: String` associated value of kvSwapIOError is dropped. Add a translation layer at the boundary in the Lingo agent's tool-runner shim — Vendor/ is read-only per CLAUDE.md, so this lives in our code, not in Membrane. Catch `MembraneError` cases and re-throw as `OneAgentError.toolRuntimeError(toolName:, code:, reason:, recoverable: Bool)`. The agent loop, telemetry, and transcript all gain human-readable diagnostics. This alone unblocks root-cause investigation for future sessions.

2. Investigate and fix the underlying KV-swap I/O failure (root cause).
   Likely candidates to check:
   a. Sandbox path not writable in the worktree (`Local.xcconfig` retokenises bundle-id and app-group; KV swap may write to a path tied to the unsuffixed bundle).
   b. Bytes-limit hit by the proposal-context payload (today's [Lingo current-proposal context] block is ~3KB but propose_schema_change result payloads can be larger; check thresholds).
   c. Cached-pointer staleness across turns — Membrane's InMemoryPointerStore has no TTL, but the wrapper that swaps it to disk may be evicting between turns. Inspect typical pointer payload size for propose_schema_change results.
   Work plan: instrument the bridge from (1), reproduce the today-session sequence, and grep `reason:` for the actual cause once it's visible.

3. Eliminate the schema-reload tax.
   Today the agent recovers by calling membrane_load_tool_schema then re-issuing propose_schema_change. If the underlying tool schema was once available in this session, reload should be a no-op or cached. Add a session-scoped tool-schema cache in the Lingo agent's tool-runner so the recovery doesn't trigger a second LLM round-trip.
acceptance_criteria:
1. resolve_pointer failures present `OneAgentError.toolRuntimeError` to the model with the kvSwapIOError reason text intact, visible in the next user turn's tool-result transcript (no more bare `error 8`).
2. Repro: today's session replayed against fresh Membrane KV swap shows zero `error 8` failures (root cause fixed) OR shows them with full reason text (boundary fix only) — whichever lands first.
3. Pointer-size guard: a unit test confirms a propose_schema_change payload at the upper end of typical proposal size (today's was ~3KB; test at 32KB) does not trigger KV swap I/O failures.
4. Schema-reload recovery path no longer triggers a second LLM round-trip — verified by counting llm_started events per recovery sequence in a regression transcript.
close_reason: Promoted Membrane KV-swap failures from stringified Swarm tool failures into OneAgentError.toolRuntimeError while preserving or clarifying the reason; bridge tests cover both forms.

title: Lingo cannot apply pending proposals from chat — apply gate is UI-only
description:
In two distinct sessions across the corpus the user said "apply this" / "I approve" / "go ahead" in chat after a proposal was visible, and Lingo refused with "click the proposal's UI confirm action" or equivalent. apply_schema_delta was never invoked from chat in either session.

Sessions:
- 2026-05-04: lingo-20260504T120550Z-147797a3.jsonl — turns 3 and 4 (12:25:34Z "Cool. Apply this proposal." → 12:25:36Z agent: "I can apply it after you confirm the pending proposal in the UI."; 12:25:56Z "But I just told you I appove." → 12:25:58Z agent: "I need the UI confirmation action specifically, not just chat approval.")
- 2026-04-27: lingo-20260427T001821Z-2319f9e9.jsonl — three refusal pairs at 00:33:14Z, 00:36:12Z, and a third repeat. User said "Yeah, go ahead." then "I approve of this proposal. Please continue."

Gate location: `OneApps/Ontology/ViewModels/OntologyViewModel+Lingo.swift:720-727`:
```
guard proposal.status == .confirmed else {
  recordLingoTranscript(kind: .error, title: "Apply proposal",
    message: "Confirm the proposal in the UI before applying schema changes.")
  return false
}
```
`proposal.status == .confirmed` is set ONLY by an Explorer/Editor UI button. From the user's perspective, conversational approval is dead code.

Context-injection asymmetry adds insult: `OntologyAgentService.userTurnForInference` (lines 146-172) injects current-proposal context into user turns matching diagnostic vocabulary ("wrong", "error", "fix") but NOT for apply vocabulary. So apply-intent turns reach the model without the proposal even being in scope.
design:
Add a chat-side confirmation path that preserves the shadow-then-commit semantics demanded by the epic ("Validation runs against a disposable copy. The live ontology is mutated only after the user explicitly confirms.") without forcing a UI click.

1. New tool: confirm_proposal(proposal_id: String, source: "chat" | "ui").
   The agent calls this after recognising explicit chat approval. The tool transitions `proposal.status` from `.pending` to `.confirmed` with `confirmationSource = .chat` and persists the originating user-turn text as the audit record. apply_schema_delta then runs unchanged, satisfying the existing `.confirmed` gate at `OntologyViewModel+Lingo.swift:720-727`.

   Approval recogniser (in agent prompt + tool flow): explicit phrases — "apply", "approve", "go ahead", "do it", "ship it", "yes apply", "confirm". Non-recogniser: hedged ("maybe", "should I"), questioning ("does this look right?"), or undirected ("ok"). Err toward a clarifying question over a false positive.

2. Inject current-proposal context for apply-intent turns.
   In `OntologyAgentService.userTurnForInference`, extend `userTurnReferencesLatestProposal` to return true for apply vocabulary in addition to the existing diagnostic vocabulary. This means even when the user's wording is ambiguous, the agent at least responds with reference to the right proposal instead of asking for clarification or talking generically.

3. Audit record. The `confirmationSource` field is the audit trail the epic's principles require: "Every accepted delta is recorded with the conversation that motivated it." Persist source, timestamp, and the user-turn text that triggered confirmation. UI-driven confirmation continues to record `confirmationSource = .ui` — this is additive, not a removal.

4. Optional follow-on (file as separate child if desired): a "preview vs. apply" delta panel surfaced inline in chat that the agent can render without forcing the user into the Explorer.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Focused test: user-turn "apply this proposal" after a pending proposal results in confirm_proposal then apply_schema_delta being called in the same turn. Final state: proposal.status == .applied, confirmationSource == .chat persisted.
2. Negative test: user-turn "actually let me look first" or "what does this do?" does NOT trigger confirm_proposal — the recogniser is conservative.
3. Existing UI confirm path continues to set confirmationSource = .ui (regression check).
4. Transcript-replay against 2026-05-04/lingo-20260504T120550Z-147797a3.jsonl shows the apply succeeding at turn 3 ("Cool. Apply this proposal."), not blocked through turn 5.
5. apply-vocabulary turns ("apply", "approve", "go ahead") get current-proposal context injected — visible as the [Lingo current-proposal context] block in the user turn passed to the model.
close_reason: Added confirm_proposal chat/UI confirmation metadata and chat apply-turn context injection; tests cover explicit chat confirmation, UI confirmation, and hedged non-approval.

title: Lingo never runs validate_candidate before propose_schema_change
description:
Across 27 distinct Lingo sessions and 42 propose_schema_change invocations from 2026-04-25 to 2026-05-04, validate_candidate was called before propose_schema_change exactly zero times — 0/42 = 100% skip rate.

Survey command (reproducible):
```
find /Users/kenpo/.config/one/sessions/lingo -name '*.jsonl' ! -name '*.summary.jsonl' \
  | xargs jq -c 'select(.event=="tool_call_started")
      | (.fields.tool_name | if type=="object" then .string._0 else . end) as $t
      | select($t=="propose_schema_change" or $t=="validate_candidate")
      | {file:input_filename, ts:.timestamp, tool:$t}'
```

The validate_candidate tool exists and is registered in `OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/SchemaEvolutionTools.swift:446-559`. The system prompt at `OneApps/Ontology/Agent/LingoSystemPrompt.swift:77` mentions calling it "before asking the user to commit a larger sandbox change set" — but this advisory phrasing has 0% adherence in practice.

Consequence: every parser error and every semantic surprise in a proposal reaches the user surface instead of being caught earlier in the loop. The 2026-05-04 transcript (lingo-20260504T120550Z-147797a3.jsonl) is one example of many — Lingo emitted invalid TypeQL, the user pasted the parser error five turns later, and the loop spent another full turn diagnosing what the validator could have caught up front.
design:
Two complementary fixes. Ship both.

1. Defense-in-depth at the tool boundary.
   In `ProposeSchemaChangeTool.execute` (`OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/SchemaEvolutionTools.swift:18-83`), after `SchemaContractValidator().validate(...)` succeeds and before the proposal is registered as `pending`, invoke ValidateCandidateTool's sanity-query pass against the sandbox. If sanity queries fail, return an `OneAgentError.invalidToolArguments`-style response that includes the failing queries so the model can self-repair in the same turn — this composes with the self-repair behaviour shipped in one-2xg.38.15. This makes validation non-skippable without changing the tool surface or asking the model to call two tools.

2. Tool-flow nudge.
   Update `LingoSystemPrompt.swift` to make pre-validation explicit and structural, not advisory: list validate_candidate as a required pre-flight when the proposal touches relations or attributes (the empirically common defect surface). Use the prompt-injection pattern from `OntologyAgentService.userTurnForInference` (`OntologyAgentService.swift:146-172`) so the nudge appears in the user-turn itself, not just the system prompt — context blocks injected into user turns survive context compression better than system-prompt clauses.

Why both: prompt nudge improves observability and explanation when validation does run; tool-boundary check is what actually closes the gap, since the survey shows prompt-only guidance has 0% adherence empirically.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Focused test: propose_schema_change with TypeQL that defines a relation referencing a missing role player raises an error from the tool that names the failing sanity query (driven by the new tool-boundary validation pass).
2. Transcript-replay test against `2026-05-04/lingo-20260504T120550Z-147797a3.jsonl` shows the bad proposal v1 rejected by propose_schema_change itself, not by the user pasting the parser error five turns later.
3. Adherence audit script (re-runs the survey jq and reports `proposes_with_prior_validate_or_internal_check / total_proposes`) reaches >90% on new sessions captured after the fix lands.
4. LingoSystemPrompt.swift includes the explicit pre-flight requirement, with a regression test asserting the canonical wording is present.
close_reason: Propose schema change now runs internal validate_candidate preflight before storing proposals when a sandbox is active; regression covers failing validation preventing proposal storage.

title: Lingo proposal validator misses comma-form 'entity X, sub Y' root declarations
description:
In Lingo session /Users/kenpo/.config/one/sessions/lingo/2026-05-04/lingo-20260504T120550Z-147797a3.jsonl at 12:06:14Z and 12:11:58Z, Lingo emitted invalid TypeDB-3 root declarations of the form `entity Meeting, sub gist:PlannedEvent;` and `relation meetingDecision, sub gist:Categorization, relates ...` to propose_schema_change. The proposal validator accepted both. TypeDB rejected them on apply with `[TQL03] expected annotation` near the `sub` token.

The closed bead one-2xg.38.11 added rejection for `sub <kind-keyword>` patterns (e.g. `sub relation`). It does not catch this comma-form, which is a different invalid TypeDB-3 syntax: a root declaration cannot mix the kind keyword with a `sub` clause in the same statement; the kind keyword is the root form, and subtype assertions belong in a separate `X sub Y;` statement.

Validator location: `OneApps/Ontology/Schema/SchemaContractValidator.swift`, function validateGeneratedSchemaSyntax(_:assetPath:) at lines 229-250. Current regex matches only `\bsub\s+(entity|relation|attribute)\b`.
design:
Extend `validateGeneratedSchemaSyntax` to scan statement-by-statement instead of operating on the whole TypeQL string as one regex target. After the existing `stripComments` + `maskingQuotedStrings` normalisation, split on `;` to get root statements, then for each statement check:
1. Existing rule: reject `\bsub\s+(entity|relation|attribute)\b` (preserves one-2xg.38.11 fix).
2. New rule: reject any statement matching `^\s*(entity|relation|attribute)\s+\w+\s*,\s*sub\b` — kind keyword followed by `, sub`.

Per-statement scanning is the more durable foundation for future syntactic checks (e.g. `attribute X, sub Y, value string;`) than the current line-soup regex.

Reuse `SchemaContractValidationIssue.invalidGeneratedSchemaSyntax` for the new case, with a message that quotes the offending root declaration and shows the corrected split form: `entity X;` then `X sub Y;`. Mirror the explanation style from `.12` so error wording stays consistent.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Focused test: propose_schema_change called with `entity X, sub gist:Y;` is rejected at the validator. Error message names the offending statement and proposes the split form (`entity X;` then `X sub Y;`).
2. Same coverage for relation comma-form: `relation R, sub gist:C, relates a, relates b;`.
3. Existing tests for `sub entity`/`sub relation`/`sub attribute` (from one-2xg.38.11) continue to pass.
4. Today's pasted TypeDB parser error from 2026-05-04 transcript becomes a regression fixture.
close_reason: Extended schema contract validation to reject comma-form root subtype declarations with corrected split-form guidance; entity and relation regressions cover the bug.

title: Prevent Lingo proposal diffs from crashing on duplicate labels
description: The app crashed while executing propose_schema_change because Lingo proposal diff construction used Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:) on verifier labels. A proposal can produce duplicate labels (for example repeated declarations or parser/resolver duplicates), which triggers a Swift assertion on the main actor and terminates OneApp.
design: Make proposal diff construction duplicate-tolerant and deterministic. Coalesce repeated label checks instead of assuming uniqueness, preserving the highest-risk status/kind for the UI. Add a regression test that exercises duplicate proposal labels through the same diff path used by recordEngineeringHierarchyProposal.

title: Lingo should validate role coverage when reusing relation patterns
description: Lingo can reuse an existing relation pattern by declaring one proposed type plays one role while failing to account for the relation's other required roles and role-player types. The meeting/hasParticipant case is one regression example, but the fix must generalize to any reused relation pattern.
design:
## General Problem
This is not specifically a meeting-attendance bug. It is a semantic proposal-completeness bug: Lingo may choose an existing relation pattern, assign one role to a proposed type, and leave the counterpart roles unmodeled or unexplained. TypeDB may accept this structurally, but the proposed domain pattern is incomplete.

## Desired Behavior
When Lingo reuses a relation as a modeling pattern, it should reason over the whole relation shape:
- relation label
- all declared roles from live schema/proposal schema
- which proposed or live type plays each role
- which roles are still unbound
- whether unbound roles are intentionally out of scope or require clarification

## Validation Layer
Do not implement this as a raw TypeDB syntax/type validator. Partial `plays` declarations can be legitimate. This belongs in Lingo's semantic proposal verifier/adjudicator layer, where it can distinguish an incomplete modeling pattern from an intentionally partial schema edit.

## Regression Examples
- Meeting attendance with `hasParticipant`: a meeting/event side without an attendee/participant side should be flagged or clarified.
- Add at least one non-attendance fixture such as `isAbout` or `hasPart` to prove the rule is relation-pattern coverage, not a hardcoded `hasParticipant` check.
acceptance_criteria: Proposal semantic verification detects relation-pattern reuse where only a subset of the relation's declared roles are assigned or accounted for. Diagnostics name the relation, declared roles, assigned roles, and missing/unaccounted roles. Lingo either proposes all needed role-player declarations or asks a domain clarification before presenting the proposal. Tests include hasParticipant as the meeting-attendance regression and at least one additional relation pattern such as isAbout or hasPart to prove the behavior is not hardcoded.
close_reason: Added relation role coverage verification for proposals that reuse relation patterns; tests cover incomplete hasParticipant and isAbout role assignments.

title: Worktree-aware build setup
description: Fix the mise build pipeline so it works correctly in git worktrees. Currently, working in a worktree falls over because (1) the wholesale cp -Rl of Vendor/container hardlinks path-baked module-cache pcm files from main, (2) container-libs.sh's submodule SHA detection falls back to the parent repo HEAD when the worktree's submodule .git file is stripped, and (3) partial-state recovery (e.g. after a wiped .build/) doesn't repair the safe-to-hardlink subdirs. Build at the main checkout (~/SoftwareProjects/collection-one/OneWorkspace) must remain unchanged; all changes must be no-ops there.
design:
## Scope
Three code fixes to the mise build pipeline plus one new mise task plus one new agent skill. All changes must be no-ops when running in the main (non-worktree) checkout.

## Files touched
- `.mise/tasks/setup.sh` — selective .build/ hardlink for worktrees.
- `.mise/lib/container-libs.sh` — SHA detection that handles stripped-.git submodule.
- `.mise/tasks/worktree-doctor.sh` (new) — diagnostic + remediation task.
- `mise.toml` — register new task.
- `.claude/skills/git-worktree-setup/SKILL.md` (new) — agent guidance.

## Fix 1: container-libs.sh SHA detection
Current code (line 46):
```bash
current_sha="$(git -C "$container_dir" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
```
In a worktree, setup.sh removes `Vendor/container/.git` (line 40 of setup.sh), so `git -C ...` falls through to the parent repo and returns the parent branch HEAD instead of the actual submodule SHA.

Replace with:
```bash
if [ -e "$container_dir/.git" ]; then
  current_sha="$(git -C "$container_dir" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
else
  # Worktree case: .git was stripped during setup. Read the recorded
  # gitlink SHA from the parent repo's tree.
  current_sha="$(git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree HEAD -- Vendor/container 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $3}')"
  [ -z "$current_sha" ] && current_sha="unknown"
fi
```
This preserves the original behavior in main checkouts (where `.git` exists as a gitlink file) and uses the parent's recorded gitlink in worktrees.

## Fix 2: setup.sh selective .build/ hardlink
Current code wholesale-hardlinks `Vendor/container/` including path-sensitive subdirs.

Replace the worktree branch in section 1 with:
```bash
for dep in "${VENDOR_SWIFT_PKGS[@]}"; do
  # Source tree
  if [ ! -d "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep" ] || [ ! -f "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep/Package.swift" ]; then
    [ -L "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep" ] && rm "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep"
    [ -d "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep" ] && rm -rf "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep"
    cp -Rl "$MAIN_VENDOR/$dep" "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep"
    rm -f "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep/.git"
    echo "  $dep: copied (hardlinked)"
  fi
  # Selective .build/ subdirs (idempotent — runs even when source tree exists)
  if [ -d "$MAIN_VENDOR/$dep/.build" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep/.build"
    # Hardlink only path-independent subdirs.
    for safe in vendored checkouts repositories artifacts; do
      if [ -d "$MAIN_VENDOR/$dep/.build/$safe" ] && [ ! -d "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep/.build/$safe" ]; then
        cp -Rl "$MAIN_VENDOR/$dep/.build/$safe" "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep/.build/$safe"
      fi
    done
    # Strip path-sensitive subdirs that may have been hardlinked previously
    # (or by an older setup.sh). Each rebuild repopulates these per-worktree.
    for unsafe in arm64-apple-macosx x86_64-apple-macosx debug plugins build.db build.db-journal debug.yaml plugin-tools.yaml; do
      rm -rf "$VENDOR_DIR/$dep/.build/$unsafe"
    done
  fi
done
```
This change only runs inside `if [ "$IS_WORKTREE" = "1" ]; then` — main checkout is unaffected.

## Fix 3: New `mise run worktree-doctor` task
Script `.mise/tasks/worktree-doctor.sh`:
- Detects `IS_WORKTREE`. If not in a worktree, exits with informational message — no-op for main.
- Strips path-sensitive `.build/` subdirs in all hardlinked vendor packages.
- Re-runs `mise run setup` to repair any holes.
- Reports what was cleaned.

Register in `mise.toml`:
```toml
[tasks.worktree-doctor]
description = "Repair a git worktree's vendor build state after manual edits"
file = ".mise/tasks/worktree-doctor.sh"
```

## Skill: .claude/skills/git-worktree-setup/SKILL.md
Documents:
- The worktree architecture (cp -Rl hardlink scheme + bundle-id suffix in Local.xcconfig).
- Path-sensitive vs path-independent invariants in `Vendor/container/.build/`:
  - SAFE to hardlink: vendored, checkouts, repositories, artifacts.
  - UNSAFE: arm64-apple-macosx, x86_64-apple-macosx, debug, plugins, build.db*, debug.yaml, plugin-tools.yaml.
- "Don't rm -rf Vendor/container/.build" — use `mise run worktree-doctor` instead.
- Recovery recipe: `mise run worktree-doctor` then `mise run build-aggregate`.

## Verification plan (read-only inspection)
After implementing:
1. Re-read setup.sh to confirm worktree-only changes are gated by `IS_WORKTREE`.
2. Re-read container-libs.sh to confirm `.git` existence check correctly preserves main-checkout code path.
3. Run `mise run worktree-doctor` to recover this worktree's state.
4. Run `mise run build-aggregate` to verify end-to-end build.
5. Inspect main checkout (read-only — no commands executed there) to confirm files unchanged would still produce the original behavior.

## Out of scope
- Refactoring the broader build system.
- Changing how Vendor submodules are pinned.
- Touching main checkout state.
acceptance_criteria:
- container-libs.sh's SHA detection works correctly in both main checkouts (uses rev-parse HEAD) and worktrees (uses ls-tree HEAD on parent).
- setup.sh's worktree branch hardlinks only safe .build/ subdirs (vendored, checkouts, repositories, artifacts) and strips path-sensitive ones.
- setup.sh's worktree branch is idempotent — re-running it after a partial wipe restores .build/vendored from main.
- New mise task `worktree-doctor` exists and is registered in mise.toml.
- Skill `.claude/skills/git-worktree-setup/SKILL.md` exists and documents the hardlink invariants.
- After running `mise run worktree-doctor` in this broken worktree, `mise run build-aggregate` succeeds.
- Main checkout build behavior is unchanged — all changes gated on `IS_WORKTREE` or `[ -e $container_dir/.git ]`.
close_reason: Verified end-to-end: build-aggregate succeeds in worktree with proper signing; ChatPanelView ZStack overlay with height preference key working.

title: Reconcile synthesis-loop bead designs with Workflow API; close blocked sub-beads
description: With Swarm 0.4.8 in place, update the design fields of the synthesis-loop child beads (38.4.5/.6/.7/.8) to reference the new Workflow API, and close the three sub-beads under 38.4.1 that were blocked because their primitives were MISSING — they're transitively satisfied by 0.4.8.
design:
Beads with old-API design references that need updates (use bd update --design):

- one-2xg.38.4.5 (Interviewer agent) — uses `Agent`, `ConversationMemory`. `Agent(...)` shape is similar in 0.4.8; `ConversationMemory(maxMessages:)` survives. The design says `ConversationMemory(maxTokens: 8000, truncationStrategy: .summarize)` which never existed; reconcile to `ConversationMemory(maxMessages: 100)` per 0.4.8 actuals.

- one-2xg.38.4.6 (GIST Aligner) — same as above.

- one-2xg.38.4.7 (Pattern Retriever) — uses `Agent` only. Should be cleanest migration.

- one-2xg.38.4.8 (ELICITATION orchestration) — uses `Parallel`, `ParallelItem`, `OrchestrationStep`, `Parallel.MergeStrategy.custom`. Replace with `Workflow().parallel([interviewer, aligner, retriever], merge: .custom { results in ... }).run(input)`. The `.custom` closure signature in 0.4.8 is `(@Sendable [AgentResult]) -> String`. Per-agent identity must be carried via metadata or by index in the array. The merge function returns a JSON string (the turn summary).

- one-2xg.38.4.10 (posture validation harness) — uses `Tracer` + `BufferedTracer`. Both survive. Remove the "Tracer is INTERNAL" caveat.

Sub-beads to close as "transitively satisfied by 0.4.8":
- one-15i (Branch — MISSING) → close with: Workflow.route { input in agent } is the binary/N-ary branching primitive in 0.4.8. Phase 2 38.4.17 should compose .route + .step instead of Sequential/Branch.
- one-car (RepeatWhile — MISSING) → close with: Workflow.repeatUntil(maxIterations:_:) is native in 0.4.8.
- one-1lr (Interrupt — MISSING) → close with: WorkflowError.workflowInterrupted + .humanApprovalTimeout + .humanApprovalRejected are first-class cases in 0.4.8.

Method: bd update --design ... for each Phase 1 bead; bd close --reason ... for the three sub-beads. No code changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- one-2xg.38.4.5 design references Agent + ConversationMemory(maxMessages:) instead of the non-existent (maxTokens:truncationStrategy:) form
- one-2xg.38.4.6 design same
- one-2xg.38.4.7 design references the 0.4.8 Agent shape
- one-2xg.38.4.8 design references Workflow().parallel([...], merge: .custom) instead of Parallel + ParallelItem
- one-2xg.38.4.10 design no longer flags Tracer as INTERNAL-not-exposed
- one-15i, one-car, one-1lr are closed with the rationale above

title: Convert Vendor/Swarm from snapshot to git submodule pinned at 0.4.8

design:
Preflight: `bd show one-2xg.38.5.2` design captured the diff against upstream — 13-14 local mods, all transitively explained, none load-bearing once Wax is bumped. No further preflight needed.

Steps:

1. Remove Vendor/Swarm directory.
   `rm -rf Vendor/Swarm`

2. Add as a real submodule pinned at 0.4.8.
   `git submodule add https://github.com/christopherkarani/Swarm.git Vendor/Swarm`
   `git -C Vendor/Swarm checkout 0.4.8` (annotated tag dereferences to commit dd6b6bf6)
   `git add Vendor/Swarm` (records the gitlink at the tag commit)

3. Update .mise/tasks/swarmagent-setup — currently calls `git submodule update --init Vendor/Swarm Vendor/Wax`. After this bead, Vendor/Wax is gone, so the line becomes `git submodule update --init Vendor/Swarm`.

4. Delete Vendor/Wax submodule entirely.
   `git submodule deinit Vendor/Wax`

   Remove Vendor/Wax block from .gitmodules (git rm should do this).

notes:
# Implementation pivot: xcodebuild archive → swift build + libtool

## What we tried first (and why it failed)

The original plan kept the existing xcodegen project (Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgentBuild/SwarmAgentBuild.xcodeproj) and ran \`xcodebuild archive\` against the upgraded Swarm pin. Two cascading failures hit:

1. Wax 0.1.19 had a Swift 6.2 strict-concurrency bug in WaxVectorSearchMiniLM. Resolved by bumping Swarm's Wax pin from 0.1.19 → 0.1.20 — see christopherkarani/Swarm#80 and the bridge tag oneapp-0.4.8-wax-fix in objectiveous/SwarmFork.

2. NumKong's CNumKong is a header-only C target (no .c sources). xcodebuild's \`archive\` action with \`MACH_O_TYPE=staticlib\` puts every target's .o in a LinkFileList that libtool then links — header-only targets get included expecting a .o that SPM correctly never produced. The fundamental tension is between xcodebuild's archive flow (auto-generated link list assumes one .o per non-system target) and SPM's correct handling of header-only C library targets.

Per Apple's own guidance (developer.apple.com/forums/thread/650163): wrapping a SwiftPM package with an Xcode target to produce an xcframework is officially unsupported.

## What we landed on

The community-canonical SPM-to-xcframework pattern (per the Swift Forums + trinhngocthuyen.com): \`swift build\` directly, then libtool consolidate, then \`xcodebuild -create-xcframework -framework\`. This is the same shape as the Ghostty pattern this repo already uses for libghostty.a.

Replaced files:
- \`Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgentBuild/SwarmAgentBuild.xcodeproj/\` — DELETED (xcodegen project)
- \`Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgentBuild/project.yml\` — DELETED
- \`Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgentBuild/Package.swift\` — NEW (swift package wrapper that depends on Vendor/Swarm and produces a SwarmAgentRuntime static library product)
- \`Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgentBuild/Sources/SwarmAgentRuntime/SwarmAgentRuntime.swift\` — UPDATED (now just \`@_exported import Swarm\`; Conduit travels as transitive dep, no need to re-export from the shim)
- \`Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgentBuild/.gitignore\` — UPDATED (removed SwarmAgentBuild.xcodeproj entries; kept .build / .swiftpm / Package.resolved)
- \`scripts/build-swarmagent-xcframework.sh\` — REWRITTEN end-to-end:
  - Cache key now derives from the pinned Vendor/Swarm submodule commit (no tree-content hashing)
  - Uses \`swift build -c release --product SwarmAgentRuntime\`
  - \`find ... -name '*.o' | xargs libtool -static\` to consolidate (we control the input list, header-only C targets simply absent)
  - Manually assembles SwarmAgentRuntime.framework bundle with Modules/ + Modules/CHeaders/ + Resources/
  - \`xcodebuild -create-xcframework -framework\` packages the bundle
- \`.mise/tasks/swarmagent-setup.sh\` — UPDATED (just submodule update + invoke build script)
- \`.mise/tasks/build.sh\` — UPDATED (comment refresh)

## What didn't change

- \`OneApp/SwarmAgent.xcconfig\` and \`OneApps/SwarmAgentConsumer.xcconfig\` — already point at \`SwarmAgent.xcframework/macos-arm64/SwarmAgentRuntime.framework/Modules\` and reference USearchC + CNumKongDispatch + GRDBSQLite C-modules (matches the new graph). No consumer-side change required.
- \`Vendor/Prebuilt/.gitignore\` — already ignores \`SwarmAgent.xcframework\`. The xcframework remains a symlink to a local cache; no binary checked into git. Same pattern as Vendor/GhosttyKit.xcframework.

## Verification (in progress)

title: Migrate SwarmAgent target to Swarm 0.4.8 API
description: 0.4.8 deletes Orchestration/, DSL/, ReActAgent, PlanAndExecuteAgent, RelayAgent, AgentBuilder, and a number of supporting types. The SwarmAgent target's BaseAgentService uses ReActAgent and InMemorySession; the bridge files reference AgentEvent / AgentError / ToolParameter shapes that may have shifted. This bead does the API migration and gets `mise run build app` and `mise run test app` green again.
design:
Surveyed differences between Feb-10 snapshot and 0.4.8:

1. Agent runtime — `ReActAgent` is gone; `Agent` (tool-calling, with tool-calling APIs natively) is the replacement. Agent's surface is similar: `Agent(tools:instructions:configuration:memory:inferenceProvider:tracer:inputGuardrails:outputGuardrails:guardrailRunnerConfiguration:handoffs:)`. Migrate `BaseAgentService` to construct `Agent` instead. The .stream(input:session:) surface should still exist; verify against actual 0.4.8 API.

2. Memory — `ConversationMemory(maxMessages:)` survives at 0.4.8. `InMemorySession` survives. No migration needed beyond confirming.

3. Bridges — 
   - `AgentEventBridge` exhaustively switches on `AgentEvent` (30 cases). 0.4.8 may have added/removed cases; the switch must be re-exhausted.
   - `AgentErrorBridge` switches on `AgentError` (17 cases) — same caveat.
   - `ToolBridge` (AnyJSONToolAdapter, ToolParameterBridge, ToolCallBridge, ToolResultBridge, AgentResultBridge, PartialToolCallUpdateBridge, GuardrailTypeBridge, MemoryOperationBridge) — verify each Swarm type still exists with the same shape. ToolParameter / ToolCall / ToolResult / TokenUsage / PartialToolCallUpdate / GuardrailType / MemoryOperation may have moved or been renamed.

4. SwarmAgentRuntime shim (Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgentBuild/Sources/SwarmAgentRuntime/SwarmAgentRuntime.swift) — re-exports of Swarm types. Re-validate against 0.4.8.

5. `@_spi(Synthesis)` SPI export at OneApp/SwarmAgent/Synthesis/SwarmSynthesisExports.swift — `@_exported @_spi(Synthesis) import Swarm` is API-agnostic; it'll just re-export whatever 0.4.8 exposes. No change needed unless 0.4.8 changed the SPI tag conventions.

6. `MuseResolvedInferenceProvider.inferenceProvider` (added under @_spi(Synthesis)) — `InferenceProvider` protocol survives at 0.4.8 as the inference boundary. No change needed.

Method:
1. After task A lands and Vendor/Swarm = 0.4.8, run `mise run build app`. Capture every compile error.
2. Walk error list top-down, fixing each. Use the actual 0.4.8 source under Vendor/Swarm/Sources/ as the reference for current shapes.
3. After build is green, run `mise run test app` and triage any test failures.
4. Capture any new event/error/parameter cases that appeared and add them to the bridge switches (Swift will force exhaustive coverage).

Scope flag: This bead does NOT migrate any plugin code (Ontology, etc.) — that's plugin-side work and most plugins use the OneApp facade types and don't see Swarm types directly. The synthesis-loop SPI re-export is the one exception, but the Phase 1 synthesis agents haven't been written yet (those are tasks 38.4.5/.6/.7) — so plugin code today doesn't reference any Swarm primitive that changed shape.

- BaseAgentService.startConversation constructs the new `Agent` instead of `ReActAgent`; per-turn streaming still works
- All bridge files (AgentEventBridge, AgentErrorBridge, ToolBridge.swift) compile against 0.4.8 with exhaustive switches
- SwarmAgentRuntime shim still works
- mise run build app is green
- mise run test app passes (existing tests; no new tests in this bead)
- One.xcworkspace builds in Xcode without warnings new to this change

title: Upgrade Vendor/Swarm from Feb-10 snapshot to upstream 0.4.8
description: Vendor/Swarm is a 3-month-stale content snapshot. Upstream 0.4.8 is the latest tag and ships the Workflow API (step / parallel / route / repeatUntil / durable.checkpoint), which natively covers the four primitives the 38.4.1 audit flagged as MISSING (Branch, RepeatWhile, Interrupt, durable checkpoint store). design:
Vendor/Swarm has 13-14 local modifications carried forward from a Feb-10 snapshot. Per project policy (codified in 38.5.5) we do not modify vendored code. The fix path is: pin Vendor/Swarm to the upstream 0.4.8 tag verbatim, drop the local mods, and let SwiftPM handle the transitive dep cascade by fetching the exact pins from Swarm 0.4.8's Package.swift.

Cascade is bounded:
- Wax: exactly 0.1.19 (upstream tag exists)
- Conduit: exactly 0.3.14 (fetched, not vendored)
- ContextCore: 1.0.0; Membrane: 0.1.3; Hive: 0.1.9 (fetched)

Plugins import only the OneApp SwarmAgent facade.

Workspace-level Wax/Conduit consumers outside Vendor/: only OneApp/SwarmAgent/ (which is allowed) and one dead LocalPackages/ConduitTraits with an empty marker struct that nothing imports. The host build configuration test forbids it from being linked. Will be removed in 38.5.4.

- 38.5.2: Convert Vendor/Swarm to submodule pinned at 0.4.8 + delete Vendor/Wax + update build script (Wax now fetched by SwiftPM)
- 38.5.1: Migrate OneApp/SwarmAgent (BaseAgentService → Agent, refresh bridges) — depends on .2
- 38.5.3: Reconcile synthesis-loop bead designs (38.4.5/.6/.7/.8/.10) with Workflow API; close one-15i, one-car, one-1lr — depends on .1

title: Surface Swarm AgentResult for orchestration-step direct access
description: Phase 1 ELICITATION merge function (38.4.8) operates on `Swarm.AgentResult` values handed in by `Parallel.MergeStrategy.custom`. The closure type is `([(String, AgentResult)]) -> String` — `AgentResult` itself is the parameter type. Today `AgentResult` is mirrored as `OneAgentResult` but the raw type is internal.
design:
Approach B (recommended): satisfied transitively by `SwarmSynthesisExports.swift`.

Source reference: `Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Core/AgentResult.swift:23` — `public struct AgentResult: Sendable, Equatable` with `output: String`, `toolCalls`, `toolResults`, `iterationCount`, `duration`, `tokenUsage`, `metadata: [String: SendableValue]`.

The synthesis-loop merge function reads `agentResult.output` for the per-agent free-form result and parses Aligner / Retriever JSON outputs from there. The `metadata` field carries Swarm-side per-agent annotations (the per-item name is plumbed via the `(String, AgentResult)` tuple, not metadata).

Approach A alternative: extend `OneAgentResult` with a `fromSwarm(_ swarm: AgentResult)` factory and rewrite the merge to operate on facade types. Cost: every `Parallel.MergeStrategy.custom` site needs a translation layer, and per-step `AgentResult`-typed parameters cannot be silently retyped without extending Swarm. Rejected for Phase 1.
acceptance_criteria:
- 38.4.8's `mergeElicitation` closure compiles against the actual `Parallel.MergeStrategy.custom` signature.
- The merge function returns the final `String` payload (JSON-encoded turn summary) per the Swarm signature; structured types propagate through orchestration context if needed downstream.

title: Surface Swarm Parallel + ParallelItem + ParallelErrorHandling
description: Phase 1 ELICITATION step (38.4.8) is a `Parallel` orchestration step composing three Swarm `Agent` actors. Plugin code today cannot construct `Parallel`; the type is not surfaced.
design:
Approach B (recommended): satisfied transitively when `SwarmSynthesisExports.swift` re-exports Swarm under `@_spi(Synthesis)`.

API caveats from 38.4.1 audit (the implementer of 38.4.8 must reconcile):

1. `Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Orchestration/OrchestrationBuilder.swift:548` — `public struct Parallel: OrchestrationStep` init signature is `(merge: MergeStrategy = .concatenate, maxConcurrency: Int? = nil, errorHandling: ParallelErrorHandling = .continueOnPartialFailure, @ParallelBuilder content: () -> [ParallelItem])`. The 38.4.8 design uses `Parallel(errorHandling:.bestEffort, mergeStrategy:.custom(...))` which (i) reverses the arg order, (ii) uses `mergeStrategy:` instead of `merge:`, (iii) references `.bestEffort` which is not a `ParallelErrorHandling` case (only `.failFast` / `.continueOnPartialFailure`).

2. `Parallel.MergeStrategy.custom` (nested at `OrchestrationBuilder.swift:564`) takes `@Sendable ([(String, AgentResult)]) -> String` — note: returns `String`, NOT `AgentResult`. The 38.4.8 design's `mergeElicitation` returning `AgentResult` will not type-check. The merger must serialize the merged turn summary as a JSON string and let the orchestration-step boundary wrap it; structured fields propagate through subsequent steps via context, not via the AgentResult.

3. `ParallelItem` at `OrchestrationBuilder.swift:502` has init `(name: String? = nil, agent: any AgentRuntime)`. The 38.4.8 design's `ParallelItem(agent: ..., name: ...)` reverses the arg order.

4. There is a top-level `ParallelMergeStrategy` enum at `AgentOperators.swift:559` that is distinct from `Parallel.MergeStrategy`. The top-level enum is used by the older `ParallelGroup` actor; the orchestration-step `Parallel` uses the nested type. Do not confuse them.

title: Posture validation harness (Phase 1 — elicitation only)
description: Replays recorded conversations through the ELICITATION-only workflow. Assesses posture via Tracer events + LLM-judge against a rubric. The gate for confirming Phase 1 tone before committing to Phase 2 / 38.1.
design:
Replays recorded conversations through the ELICITATION-only Workflow and assesses posture via Tracer events plus an LLM-judge agent against a rubric. This is the gate that determines whether Phase 1's conversational tone is right before committing to Phase 2 / 38.1.

File: OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/Synthesis/PostureValidationHarnessTests.swift (new test file; new directory)
Fixtures: OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/Synthesis/Fixtures/*.json (3 sessions to start)

Swarm 0.4.8 has a public `Tracer` protocol and `BufferedTracer` implementation. Use that surface through the SwarmAgent facade; remove the old caveat that Tracer is internal or unavailable. If tests need event inspection, add or use a project-local in-memory tracer conforming to the public `Tracer` protocol rather than modifying Vendor/Swarm.

Components:

1. Fixture sessions. Each JSON file describes a sequence of user turns and qualitative properties the harness checks:

```json
{
  "name": "track-meetings",
  "sessionId": "harness-track-meetings",
  "turns": [
    { "userInput": "I want to track meetings my team has." },
    { "userInput": "Each meeting has an agenda and produces decisions." },
    { "userInput": "I want to know later who attended each meeting." }
  ],
  "expectedProperties": [
    "agent restates meeting in gist terms",
    "agent maps attended to a role-player concept",
    "agent captures who attended each meeting as a CQ",
    "agent does not emit TypeQL"
  ]
}
```

Three initial fixtures:
- track-meetings.json — gist:Event / gist:Activity territory, role players
- product-feature-hierarchy.json — gist:Category, hierarchical membership
- document-ownership.json — gist:Agreement, isPartOfOrg, membership

2. Replay runner. Build `ElicitationWorkflow.make(viewModel:)`, then call `workflow.run(turn.userInput)` for each fixture turn against a real `OntologyViewModel` backed by `LiveTypeDBFixture`.

3. Deterministic checks. Consume tracer events and assert:
- exactly one `record_elicitation` tool call per turn from the Interviewer
- zero schema mutation tool calls (`propose_schema_change`, `apply_schema_delta`, `run_write_query`)
- GIST Aligner produces non-empty structured output for each turn

4. LLM-judge agent. Use a Swarm `Agent` with judge instructions to score each turn for:
- vocabularyMirrored: yes/no
- gistTaught: yes/no/n/a
- elicitationBeforeProposal: yes/no
- tone: 1-5
- expected fixture properties: yes/no/partial

Judge output must be JSON, e.g. `{ "perTurn": [...], "fixtureProperties": {...}, "overall": 4 }`.

5. Test harness shell. Iterate all fixtures, replay through the real workflow, run deterministic checks, run judge, log scores via os.Logger, and fail if any fixture scores below the initial 3/5 threshold.

Constraints:
- Real TypeDB / real provider per project no-mocks policy. Consult `testing-guidelines` before implementation.
- Do not edit Vendor/Swarm to add tracing helpers. Any missing convenience belongs in OneApp/SwarmAgent or the test target.

Depends on:
- 38.4.8 — ElicitationWorkflow exists
- 38.4.9 — chat surface, useful adjacent for visual verification
- 38.5.1 — Swarm 0.4.8 API migration
- one-uys — Swarm Tracer protocol/default tracer surfaced through SwarmAgent facade

- 3 fixture session JSON files exist under OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/Synthesis/Fixtures/
- Replay runner executes all turns of a fixture through the ELICITATION Workflow against a real TypeDB sandbox
- Deterministic checks verify: one record_elicitation call per turn, zero schema-mutation tool calls
- LLM-judge agent produces per-turn and fixture-level scores
- Initial overall threshold: 3/5; test fails if any fixture scores below
- Test runs in CI; scores logged via os.Logger for review

title: Implement Pattern Retriever agent
description: Swarm Agent that returns top-k TypeQL patterns from the ontology memory corpus. Wraps the existing search_ontology_memory tool.
design:
The Pattern Retriever returns top-k TypeQL patterns from the ontology memory corpus that match the conceptual shape the user is describing. It wraps the existing `search_ontology_memory` tool.

File: OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Synthesis/PatternRetrieverAgent.swift

Implement as a Swarm `Agent` through the SwarmAgent facade. This agent is stateless: use `memory: nil`.

Factory shape:

```swift
import Foundation
import SwarmAgent

enum PatternRetrieverAgent {
  @MainActor
  static func make(viewModel: OntologyViewModel) -> Agent {
    Agent(
      name: "PatternRetriever",
      instructions: instructions,
      tools: tools(for: viewModel),
      memory: nil,
      configuration: AgentConfiguration(name: "PatternRetriever", maxIterations: 2)
    )
  }

  @MainActor
  private static func tools(for viewModel: OntologyViewModel) -> [any AnyJSONTool] {
    [SearchOntologyMemoryTool(viewModel: viewModel).asAnyJSONTool()]
  }
}
```

Instructions must require JSON-array-only output. For each retrieved pattern, include:

```json
{
  "package": "<package name>",
  "file": "<source file>",
  "typeLabel": "<the type the pattern centers on>",
  "kind": "entity | relation | attribute",
  "description": "<one-line summary>",
  "snippet": "<the relevant TypeQL fragment, max 20 lines>"
}
```

Constraints:
- Output is only a JSON array. No prose and no markdown fences.
- Use `search_ontology_memory` with descriptive natural-language queries derived from the user's concepts and goal.
- Do not pass raw TypeQL as the search query; the corpus is indexed by natural-language descriptions.
- maxIterations: 2, allowing one refinement if first results are thin.
- Phase 2 may replace the wrapped-tool approach with direct VectorMemory + EmbeddingProvider if needed, but Phase 1 should reuse the validated Wax-backed corpus.

title: Implement Interviewer agent (the only voice the user hears)
description: Swarm Agent that drives the user-facing conversation. Elicits before proposing. Mirrors vocabulary in gist terms. Teaches gist primitives. Phase 1: never emits TypeQL.
design:
The Interviewer is the only agent the user talks to. It elicits domain and goals, mirrors the user's vocabulary in gist terms, and teaches gist primitives in plain language. In Phase 1 it never emits TypeQL; it verbally describes what it would propose.

File: OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Synthesis/InterviewerAgent.swift (new file; new directory for synthesis-loop agents)

Implement as a Swarm `Agent` through the SwarmAgent facade. The Swarm 0.4.8 memory API is message-count based, so use `ConversationMemory(maxMessages: 100)`. Do not use the old/non-existent `ConversationMemory(maxTokens:truncationStrategy:)` form.

Factory shape:

```swift
import Foundation
import SwarmAgent

enum InterviewerAgent {
  @MainActor
  static func make(viewModel: OntologyViewModel) -> Agent {
    Agent(
      name: "Interviewer",
      instructions: instructions,
      tools: tools(for: viewModel),
      memory: ConversationMemory(maxMessages: 100),
      configuration: AgentConfiguration(name: "Interviewer", maxIterations: 6)
    )
  }

  @MainActor
  private static func tools(for viewModel: OntologyViewModel) -> [any AnyJSONTool] {
    let oneTools: [any OneTool] = [
      RecordElicitationTool(viewModel: viewModel),
      ExplainGistConceptTool(viewModel: viewModel),
      SearchOntologyMemoryTool(viewModel: viewModel)
    ]
    return oneTools.map { $0.asAnyJSONTool() }
  }
}
```

Instructions must enforce:
- ELICITATION-FIRST: ask before proposing; confirm goal, examples, and questions the ontology should answer.
- VOCABULARY MIRRORING: restate domain words in gist terms before introducing TypeQL or schema concepts.
- GIST TEACHING: explain every gist primitive introduced, in plain language tied to the user's domain.
- Phase 1 constraint: never emit TypeQL.
- Tool discipline: use `explain_gist_concept` before introducing any gist primitive, use `search_ontology_memory` for precedent, and call `record_elicitation` once at the end of every concept/CQ-introducing turn.

Key constraints:
- NO schema-write tools. Phase 1 strict separation: elicit, do not synthesize.
- maxIterations: 6 to allow search -> explain -> record sequences within one turn.
- Tool list explicitly excludes anything that can mutate schema.
- Bridge from OneTool to AnyJSONTool should use the existing SwarmAgent facade extension verified during 38.4.1/38.5.1 work.

title: Implement explain_gist_concept tool
description: Swarm tool that returns a non-modeler-friendly definition, canonical use, and example for any gist primitive. Sourced from the loaded ontology-gist package.
design:
A Swarm tool that returns a non-modeler-friendly explanation of any gist primitive: definition, canonical use, an example. Sourced from the loaded ontology-gist package.

File: OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/GistConceptTools.swift (new file)

Pattern: same OneTool/@unchecked Sendable convention as other tools in OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/.

Tool definition:
```swift
struct ExplainGistConceptTool: OneTool, @unchecked Sendable {
  let name = "explain_gist_concept"
  let description = "Return a plain-language definition, canonical use, and example for a gist primitive. Use this when the agent needs to teach the user what a gist concept means or how it is typically used. Accepts labels with or without 'gist:' prefix."
  let parameters: [OneToolParameter] = [
    OneToolParameter(name: "label", description: "The gist type label (e.g. 'gist:Activity', 'Activity', 'isPartOf').", type: .string, isRequired: true)
  ]
}
```

Implementation strategy:
1. Normalize the label: strip leading "gist:" prefix.
2. Look up the type via `viewModel.allEntities`, `viewModel.allRelations`, `viewModel.allAttributes` (these are populated by PackageManager when ontology-gist is loaded — see OntologyViewModel for the exact accessors).
3. Pull the typedoc entry for the type from the loaded gist package data — Resources/Packages/ontology-gist/data/gistCore-typedoc.tql contains @doc-style annotations for gist types. The view model exposes these via `viewModel.typeDoc(for: label)` (verify exact name in Models/TypeDocEntry.swift).
4. Compose the response:
   - definition: the @doc text (or fall back to the type's annotations[".doc"] from ParsedEntity/ParsedRelation/ParsedAttribute if no typedoc entry)
   - canonicalUse: pull from the typedoc's "canonical use" section if present; otherwise compose a sentence based on the type's place in the gist hierarchy (parent label + role)
   - example: pull from typedoc's "example" section if present; otherwise return null and let the prompt instruct the agent to compose one
   - related: array of nearby labels — direct supertype, direct subtypes, and any relation/attribute the type plays/owns
5. If label not found: do a fuzzy match (Levenshtein distance < 3, or substring match) over loaded gist labels and return up to 5 suggestions in `suggestions: []`.

Return shape:
```
.dictionary([
  "label": .string(normalized),
  "definition": .string(...) | .null,
  "canonicalUse": .string(...) | .null,
  "example": .string(...) | .null,
  "related": .array([.string, ...]),
  "suggestions": .array([.string, ...])  // empty unless not found
])
```

The "framed for a non-modeler" framing is the responsibility of how the Interviewer renders the result conversationally — the tool returns structured data; the prompt instructs the Interviewer to translate it into plain language tied to the user's domain.

Registration: GistConceptTools.makeTools(viewModel:) → wired into LingoAgent.makeTools.

Used by: Interviewer (38.4.5) for teaching turns; GIST Aligner (38.4.6) for verifying alignment candidates.

No sandbox dependency — this is a pure read against the loaded gist package (which is bundled via Resources/Packages/ontology-gist/, always available).

notes:
# Implementation notes

## Deviation from design: data source

The bead's design proposed reading from \`viewModel.entitiesByDomain[\"gist\"]\`
and \`viewModel.typeDoc(for:)\`. Both of those go through the explorer-side
caches that are filtered by \`entitySourceMode\` (a UI toggle: \"database\" vs
\"packageDefinitions\"). In \`.database\` mode (the default), those caches
are populated from a live TypeDB introspection — empty when TypeDB isn't
running, e.g. unit tests with no live server.

The tool reads from \`viewModel.parsedEntities\` / \`parsedRelations\` /
\`parsedAttributes\` and \`viewModel.typeDocs\` directly. These are the raw
package-derived data (populated by \`loadSchemas()\` / \`loadTypeDocs()\` from
\`PackageManager.resolveLoadOrder()\`) and are independent of the UI's
source-mode toggle. This matches the bead's stated intent: \"this is a pure
read against the loaded gist package (which is bundled via Resources/Packages/ontology-gist/, always available)\".

## Test results

\`mise run test Ontology -- -only-testing:OntologyTests/GistConceptToolsTests\`
passes 10/10:
- known entity (Event) — definition + related populated
- gist: prefix stripping
- known relation (isPartOf) — kind = \"relation\", related has roles
- known attribute (name) — kind = \"attribute\"
- unknown label \"Categori\" — fuzzy suggests \"Category\"
- unrelated label \"zzzqqqxyz\" — empty result
- missing label argument — throws
- normalize() handles edge cases (gist:, GIST:, whitespace, non-gist prefixes)
- levenshtein sanity (kitten/sitting = 3, etc.)
- registered in LingoAgent.makeTools by exact name \"explain_gist_concept\"

## Bead-design label list note

The bead's acceptance lists Activity, Event, Category, PhysicalThing, Agreement,
isPartOf, isMemberOfCollection, Magnitude as a minimum. The trimmed
gistCore fixture (in OntologyTests/Fixtures/Packages/gist/) does not include
Activity or PhysicalThing — only the production ontology-gist clone does
(via LiveTypeDBFixture). Tests run against whichever gist version is
available; the tool itself works with any gist labels present in the loaded
package data.

title: Implement record_elicitation tool (writes ConversationTurn + CQs)
description: Swarm tool the Interviewer calls at end of every turn. Writes a ConversationTurn entity with the structured turn summary as JSON, plus any new CompetencyQuestion entities introduced this turn.
design:
A Swarm tool the Interviewer agent calls at the end of every turn to persist its structured understanding into the active sandbox.

File: OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/ElicitationTools.swift (new file, follow ChangeIntentTools.swift / SchemaIntrospectionTools.swift conventions)

Pattern: implement as `OneTool` (the existing protocol, see SearchOntologyMemoryTool for canonical example) — do NOT introduce the @Tool macro for this single tool; @Tool migration is a separate consideration. Use the same `@unchecked Sendable` + `viewModel: OntologyViewModel` MainActor pattern as the rest of Tools/.

Tool definition:

```swift
struct RecordElicitationTool: OneTool, @unchecked Sendable {
  let name = "record_elicitation"
  let description = "Persist the structured turn summary into the active sandbox. Captures user goal, inferred concepts (with proposed gist anchors), unresolved vocabulary, next actions, and any new competency questions introduced this turn. Call once per turn that introduces new concepts or CQs."
  let parameters: [OneToolParameter] = [
    OneToolParameter(name: "session_id", description: "Stable session identifier (Lingo session UUID).", type: .string, isRequired: true),
    OneToolParameter(name: "turn_index", description: "Zero-based index of this turn within the session.", type: .int, isRequired: true),
    OneToolParameter(name: "user_goal", description: "Single-sentence restatement of what the user is trying to achieve in this turn.", type: .string, isRequired: true),
    OneToolParameter(name: "inferred_concepts_json", description: "JSON array of {label: string, proposedGistAnchor: string?, role: string}.", type: .string, isRequired: false),
    OneToolParameter(name: "unresolved_vocabulary_json", description: "JSON array of strings — domain terms whose meaning the agent has not pinned down.", type: .string, isRequired: false),
    OneToolParameter(name: "next_actions_json", description: "JSON array of strings — what the agent plans to do next.", type: .string, isRequired: false),
    OneToolParameter(name: "new_cqs_json", description: "JSON array of {nlForm: string} for new CQs introduced in this turn.", type: .string, isRequired: false)
  ]
  // viewModel-injected MainActor pattern
}
```

execute() implementation:
1. Generate `turnId` = UUID().lowercased().
2. Open a write transaction on `viewModel.activeSandbox?.name` via `viewModel.typeDBClient.oneShotQuery(transactionType: .write, commit: true)`.
3. Insert ConversationTurn:
   ```
   insert
     $t isa ConversationTurn,
       has turnId "<uuid>",
       has sessionId "<from arg>",
       has turnIndex <from arg>,
       has turnRole "assistant",
       has turnSummary "<JSON-encoded full payload>",
       has turnAt <now>;
   ```
4. For each entry in new_cqs_json: insert CompetencyQuestion (cqStatus="unanswered") and create cqIntroduction relation linking the new turn and the new CQ. Generate cqId = UUID().lowercased() per CQ.
5. Mirror the persisted state to view-model fields if needed (e.g., maintain an in-memory CQ count for UI). Follow the pattern in ChangeIntentTools' record_intent execute().
6. Append a transcript entry via `viewModel.recordLingoTranscript(kind: .tool, title: "record_elicitation", message: "Recorded turn \(turnIndex) (\(newCQCount) new CQs).")`.
7. Return: `.dictionary(["turnId": .string(turnId), "newCqIds": .array(cqIds.map(.string))])`.

Registration: add `ElicitationTools.makeTools(viewModel:)` and call it from `LingoAgent.makeTools(viewModel:)` (OneApps/Ontology/Agent/LingoAgent.swift) so the tool is available to whichever agent receives the tool list. In Phase 1 this is the Interviewer; in Phase 2 the Committer also writes ConversationTurn entries but does it directly via ChangeIntentWriter rather than through this agent tool.

Error handling:
- If no active sandbox: throw OneAgentError.toolExecutionFailed with message "No active sandbox. The Interviewer should not be running without an active sandbox."
- If write transaction fails: surface the TypeDB error verbatim.

Depends on: 38.4.2 (CompetencyQuestion + ConversationTurn entities must exist in the sandbox meta-schema).

notes:
# Implementation notes

## Deviation from design: value type for `turnIndex`

The design field specifies \`attribute turnIndex, value long;\`. TypeDB 3
does not have a \`long\` value type — only \`integer\`, \`string\`,
\`boolean\`, \`double\`, \`decimal\`, \`datetime\`, \`datetimetz\`,
\`duration\`. Schema apply with \`value long\` fails with
\`[SYR4] The value type 'long' was not found.\`. (TypeDB 2.x had \`long\`;
that was renamed when the type system was reworked.)

The schema fragment uses \`value integer\` for \`turnIndex\` (and the test
assertions match). All other value types in the bead's design verbatim —
\`string\`, \`datetime\` — are valid TypeDB 3 types and unchanged.

## Test results

\`mise run test Ontology -- -only-testing:OntologyTests/ChangeIntentSchemaTests\`
passes 7/7:

- existing 4 tests remain green (drift / shape / empty-DB / on-top-of-gist)
- new \`fragment constant contains the CompetencyQuestion / ConversationTurn extensions\` (constant-shape assertion)
- new round-trip test: insert one \`ConversationTurn\`, one \`CompetencyQuestion\`, one \`cqIntroduction\` relation between them, query back the relation by both player vars, expect one row containing the inserted ids and \`nlForm\`.
- existing live-DB tests pick up the new types via \`assertFragmentTypesPresent\` (extended).

## Follow-up

If 38.4.11 (Phase 2 Delta Log extensions) adopts this same convention,
apply the same \`long\` → \`integer\` correction in that bead's design when
unblocked.

## Method

1. Read every file under `OneApp/SwarmAgent/Facade/`, `OneApp/SwarmAgent/Adapters/`, `OneApp/SwarmAgent/SwarmAgent.swift`, and `OneApp/SwarmAgent/Testing/`.
2. Grepped `Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm` for every primitive listed in 38.4.1's design.
3. Cross-checked Phase 1 child-bead designs (38.4.5 / 38.4.6 / 38.4.7 / 38.4.8) for the exact primitives the Synthesis loop will reach for.

`SwarmAgent.swift` does **not** `@_exported import Swarm`. The umbrella module exposes only OneApp-defined wrapper types (`OneTool`, `OneAgentEvent`, `OneAgentResult`, `OneToolValue`, …) and the `BaseAgentService` runtime. The only direct Swarm exposure is `SwarmTestingExports.swift`, which `@_exported @_spi(Testing) import`s Swarm so test bundles can author `InferenceProvider` stubs. Production plugin code does not see Swarm types — that boundary is documented in `SwarmAgent.swift` and is load-bearing.

Classification:
- **EXPOSED** — directly callable from plugin code via `import SwarmAgent` (or via the `MuseRuntime` provider abstraction)
- **INTERNAL** — present in the vendored Swarm package and used by SwarmAgent internally, but not surfaced through the facade
- **MISSING** — not present in upstream Swarm at all (we would need to either build a OneApp-defined equivalent, switch to an existing Swarm primitive that fills the role, or contribute upstream)

## Architectural recommendation

Two viable paths to surface the orchestration primitives Phase 1 needs:

**A. OneApp wrapper types** (status quo direction). Build a `OneAgent` / `OneOrchestrationStep` / `OneParallel` / `OneParallelItem` / `OneAgentConfiguration` / `OneConversationMemory` / `OneTracer` mirror per primitive, with bridges into Swarm internals. Pros: preserves the documented decoupling boundary; failure modes the same as the existing `OneAgentEvent` mirror. Cons: the orchestration surface is large and evolves with Swarm; every API drift requires a facade update.

**B. SPI-scoped re-export.** Add a new `@_spi(Synthesis) @_exported import Swarm` in a dedicated file under `OneApp/SwarmAgent/`, parallel to `SwarmTestingExports.swift`. Plugin code that opts into the synthesis-loop tier writes `@_spi(Synthesis) import SwarmAgent`. Pros: zero-translation, the orchestration surface stays in lock-step with upstream Swarm. Cons: a second SPI-marked seam through the boundary; the seam is opt-in but discoverable.

Recommendation: **B**, scoped to the orchestration / agent / memory / tracer primitives. The synthesis loop is one consumer; mirroring the entire orchestration surface in OneApp types is high-cost low-leverage. The sub-beads below assume Approach B and call out where wrappers are still needed (e.g. `OneTool.asAnyJSONTool()` so plugin tool authors don't need the SPI).

## Sub-beads filed (acceptance gate)

One sub-bead per INTERNAL or MISSING primitive listed in the acceptance criteria. See child issues of one-2xg.38.4.1.

title: Conversational synthesis loop
description: A multi-agent conversational system that helps domain experts create and evolve GIST-grounded TypeQL ontologies via iterative competency-question-driven synthesis. Replaces one-2xg.38.3.
design:
A six-agent conversational synthesis loop where the user describes their domain and the system iteratively evolves a GIST-grounded TypeQL ontology that satisfies a registry of competency questions (CQs). Two phases per conversational turn:

ELICITATION (parallel) — Interviewer talks to the user; GIST Aligner proposes anchors; Pattern Retriever returns candidate templates from existing ontology memory.

SYNTHESIS (sequential, with routing) — Schema Generator proposes a delta + claimed CQ typeql-forms; Judge validates against a shadow TypeDB sandbox (apply / type-check / CQ-verify / GIST conformance / LLM semantic review) with bounded retries; Branch dispatches additive vs. breaking; Migrator synthesizes data migration when breaking; Interrupt waits for user confirmation; Committer writes the delta + Delta Log + CQ updates.

Built on Swarm orchestration primitives (Agent, Parallel, Sequential, Branch, RepeatWhile, Guard, Interrupt, FileSystemWorkflowCheckpointStore). Three artifacts co-evolve in the active sandbox: the core ontology (TypeQL types + functions), the CQ Registry (CompetencyQuestion + ConversationTurn entities, extending today's ChangeIntent meta-schema), and the Delta Log (extended ChangeIntent with judgeVerdict, rejectionTrail, MigrationPlan).

Implementation is split into two phases so the conversational tone can be validated before committing to the schema-model investment:

PHASE 1 — Elicitation-only experience. Interviewer + Aligner + Retriever run end-to-end. The Interviewer verbally describes what would be proposed but does NOT emit TypeQL. CQs are captured. No SchemaModel dependency. Validates the world-class-ontologist conversational tone before Phase 2 builds on top.

PHASE 2 — Full synthesis pipeline. Generator + Judge + Migrator + Committer + workflow wiring + checkpointing. Depends on one-2xg.38.1 (SchemaModel) for slice computation and validation context.

Replaces and supersedes one-2xg.38.3 (ontologist posture), which framed the work as prompt edits on the existing single-agent runtime. The new architecture makes posture an emergent property of the Interviewer agent's role within a multi-agent orchestration.
acceptance_criteria:
- Phase 1: a novice user can describe their domain and receive an elicitation summary that mirrors vocabulary, teaches gist primitives, captures CQs, and ends without writing schema. Posture validation harness passes a rubric against at least three recorded fixture sessions.
- Phase 2: a confirmed proposal flows through Generator → Judge → (Migrator | direct) → Interrupt → Committer; ChangeIntent + Delta Log + CQ status updates land atomically in the active sandbox.
- Generator/Judge retry loop bounded at 3 attempts; reject-after-max escalates to needs-clarification.
- Breaking deltas trigger Migrator; ambiguous value correspondences route back to the Interviewer.
- Per-turn checkpoints written after Judge acceptance (not after Generator output) via FileSystemWorkflowCheckpointStore.
- All child tasks closed.
- one-2xg.38.3 superseded by this feature.
close_reason: Closed after all conversational synthesis loop child tasks landed: Phase 1 elicitation agents/workflow/chat surface/posture harness, CQ and Delta Log schema, CoreOntologySlice with scoped documentation, Phase 2 generator/judge/migrator/committer workflow, post-commit checkpoints, and seven-scenario live TypeDB synthesis-loop harness. Verified latest modified synthesis suites through xcsift/raw logs and pushed each implementation slice.
