title: Refactor BaseAgentService API; collapse OntologyAgentService and VibeMachine AgentService
description: Reshape AgentService protocol and BaseAgentService to consume the new facade types and provide both streaming models (continuous events stream for Ontology, per-call AsyncThrowingStream for VibeMachine). Eliminate ReActAgent direct-construction sites in OntologyAgentService.swift and VibeMachine/Agent/AgentService.swift+DesignAgent.swift by collapsing them into thin BaseAgentService consumers.
design:
AgentService protocol (OneApp/SwarmAgent/AgentService.swift):
- events: AsyncStream<OneAgentEvent> (was AgentEvent).
- startConversation(systemPrompt: String, tools: [any OneTool], resolvedProvider: MuseResolvedInferenceProvider, memoryConfig: OneAgentMemoryConfig) async throws.
- send(userTurn: String) async throws — unchanged.
- cancel() async — unchanged.

BaseAgentService:
- Internal: maintains private var agent: ReActAgent? (still uses Swarm under the hood — facade is consumer-side only).
- startConversation: wraps tools via ToolBridge.adapt(_:) (returns [any AnyJSONTool]). Constructs ReActAgent with mapped tools, instructions, memory derived from memoryConfig (.none -> nil; .conversation(n) -> ConversationMemory(maxMessages: n)), inferenceProvider unwrapped from resolvedProvider.provider.
- send(userTurn:) Task body: maps stream events via AgentEventBridge before yielding to eventContinuation.
- New helper: run(userTurn: String) -> AsyncThrowingStream<OneAgentEvent, Error> — fresh stream per call that maps Swarm events through AgentEventBridge and propagates errors via stream throw. Uses agent.stream(message) directly (not session-based) when invoked. For VibeMachine which currently does `agent.stream(message)` returning AsyncThrowingStream<AgentEvent, Error>.

MuseResolvedInferenceProvider (OneApp/SwarmAgent/MuseRuntime.swift):
- Change `public let provider: any InferenceProvider` to `internal let provider: any InferenceProvider`.
- Public init signature stays compatible (selection: ProviderSelection, provider: any InferenceProvider) but the resulting struct's provider property is internal.

OntologyAgentService (OneApps/Ontology/Agent/OntologyAgentService.swift, ~340 -> ~100 lines):
- Remove: ReActAgent ownership, dual startConversation overloads, InMemorySession+ConversationMemory plumbing, AgentEvent direct usage in send() Task.
- Keep: error message mapping (OntologyAgentServiceError.userFacingMessage and helpers), diagnostic recorder lifecycle wiring, transcript-recording event consumer (subscribes to baseService.events).
- Becomes: actor-wrapping a private let baseService: BaseAgentService. startConversation calls baseService.startConversation; send() calls baseService.send(userTurn:); event consumer is a separate Task that listens to baseService.events.

VibeMachine/Agent/AgentService.swift (~280 -> ~150 lines):
- Remove: DesignAgentFactory.makeAgent ReActAgent construction, currentAgent property, agent.stream/agent.run direct calls.
- Keep: startSession state machine (isSessionActive, currentEpic), API key management methods (getAPIKey/setAPIKey/deleteAPIKey/hasAPIKey via legacyKeychainService).
- send(message:) -> AsyncThrowingStream<OneAgentEvent, Error>: now calls baseService.run(userTurn:) and returns its stream directly.
- run(message:) -> OneAgentResult: aggregates the run-stream into a final result; OR removes this method if no callers (audit needed).

VibeMachine/Agent/DesignAgent.swift (~75 -> ~30 lines):
- DesignAgentFactory.makeAgent becomes DesignAgentFactory.makeSystemPrompt(epic:designState:toolsEnabled:) -> String. Returns just the systemInstructions String. AgentService now constructs tools via DesignTools.createTools and calls baseService.startConversation directly.

- BaseAgentService is the only place that imports/constructs ReActAgent.
- Plugin code never references InferenceProvider, ReActAgent, ConversationMemory, InMemorySession, AgentEvent (Swarm), AgentError (Swarm), AgentResult (Swarm) — only OneApp facade types.

- OneApp/SwarmAgent/MuseRuntime.swift:6-17 (MuseResolvedInferenceProvider definition)
- OneApps/Ontology/Agent/OntologyAgentService.swift:43-118 (current dual-overload + provider resolution)

- OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/DesignAgent.swift:5-75 (current factory)

title: Decouple plugins from Swarm via SwarmAgent facade
description:
Plugins (Muse, Ontology, VibeMachine) currently import Swarm types directly via @_exported re-exports from SwarmAgent (SwarmAgent/SwarmAgent.swift: @_exported import Swarm; @_exported import Conduit; @_exported import ConduitTraits). This couples plugin code to Swarm's evolving API and is the root cause of why the SwarmAgent.xcframework migration runs into the C-modulemap problem: every transitive C interop module (CSQLite from GRDB, USearchC + simsimd + stringzilla from USearch) has to be packaged into the xcframework because plugin compilers must resolve the type graph through Swarm/GRDB/USearch.

This feature replaces the @_exported re-export pattern with a SwarmAgent-defined facade: type mirrors (OneAgentEvent, OneTool, OneAgentError, OneToolValue, OneAgentResult, etc.) plus internal Swarm-to-OneApp adapters. After this lands, plugins import only SwarmAgent and never type-mention Swarm/Conduit/Wax/GRDB/USearch. The SwarmAgent.xcframework prebuild migration that follows becomes mechanical because the consumer Swift compiler only needs SwarmAgent.swiftmodule.

Plugin sites verified by grep: 37 AnyJSONTool refs, 17 AgentEvent refs (LingoDiagnosticSessionRecorder switches on all 30 cases exhaustively), 34 AgentError refs, 24 InferenceProvider refs (all already wrapped via MuseResolvedInferenceProvider), 7 ReActAgent direct construction sites in 3 files. Plugins do not use Swarm macros (verified empty grep for @Tool, @Builder, @Agent, @Parameter, @Prompt, @Traceable).

Three sub-tasks split the work along natural boundaries: (1) define facade types, (2) refactor BaseAgentService and collapse plugin agent wrappers, (3) mechanical plugin migration of tool conformances and LingoDiagnosticSessionRecorder switch.
design:
New public types in OneApp/SwarmAgent/Public/Types/ (estimated ~225 lines total):
- OneAgentEvent: 30-case enum mirroring Swarm.AgentEvent. Required exhaustive coverage because LingoDiagnosticSessionRecorder.recordAgentEvent does an exhaustive switch on all 30 cases.
- OneAgentError: 17-case enum mirroring Swarm.AgentError (all primitive payloads: String/Int/Duration/TimeInterval).
- OneAgentResult: struct mirroring AgentResult (output, toolCalls, toolResults, iterationCount, duration, tokenUsage, metadata).
- OneToolCall: struct mirroring ToolCall (id, providerCallId, toolName, arguments:[String:OneToolValue], timestamp). Sendable, Equatable, Identifiable, Codable.
- OneToolResult: struct mirroring ToolResult (callId, isSuccess, output:OneToolValue, duration, errorMessage).
- OnePartialToolCallUpdate: struct mirroring PartialToolCallUpdate.
- OneTokenUsage: struct (inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens computed).
- OneToolValue: enum mirroring Swarm.SendableValue (.string, .dictionary, .array, .boolean, .integer, .number, .null). Codable.
- OneGuardrailType, OneMemoryOperation: small string-rawValue enums.

New public protocol in OneApp/SwarmAgent/Public/Tools/:
- OneTool: protocol mirroring AnyJSONTool surface (name:String, description:String, parameters:[OneToolParameter], execute(arguments:[String:OneToolValue]) async throws -> OneToolValue). Sendable.
- OneToolParameter: struct (name, description, type:OneToolParameterType, isRequired). Sendable.

Internal adapter layer in OneApp/SwarmAgent/Internal/Adapters/ (estimated ~200 lines, never plugin-visible):
- AgentEventBridge: maps Swarm.AgentEvent -> OneAgentEvent (single switch with 30 cases).
- AgentErrorBridge: maps Swarm.AgentError -> OneAgentError.
- SendableValueBridge: bidirectional mapper between SendableValue and OneToolValue (recursive for nested cases).
- ToolBridge: AnyJSONToolAdapter<T: OneTool> wraps any OneTool as Swarm.AnyJSONTool with name/description/parameters/execute proxied through bridges.

AgentService protocol redesign:
- events: AsyncStream<OneAgentEvent> (was AgentEvent)
- startConversation(systemPrompt:String, tools:[any OneTool], resolvedProvider:MuseResolvedInferenceProvider, memoryConfig:OneAgentMemoryConfig) async throws
- New OneAgentMemoryConfig enum: { case none; case conversation(maxMessages: Int) } — captures the Ontology-vs-VibeMachine memory divergence (Ontology uses ConversationMemory(maxMessages: 100), VibeMachine uses memory: nil).
- BaseAgentService gains run(userTurn:) -> AsyncThrowingStream<OneAgentEvent, Error> for per-call request/response semantics (used by VibeMachine's existing AsyncThrowingStream model). Continuous events stream remains for Ontology's chat shape.
- MuseResolvedInferenceProvider.provider visibility: public -> internal. Plugins consume the wrapper opaquely; they never type-mention any InferenceProvider.

Plugin collapse:
- OntologyAgentService.swift (~340 lines today -> ~100): remove ReActAgent ownership, dual startConversation overloads, InMemorySession/ConversationMemory plumbing. Keep error message mapping, diagnostic recorder wiring, transcript event consumer.
- VibeMachine/Agent/AgentService.swift (~280 -> ~150): use BaseAgentService.run(userTurn:) for throwing-stream shape. Keep API key keychain logic.
- VibeMachine/Agent/DesignAgent.swift: collapse to a system-prompt builder; no ReActAgent reference.

Plugin tool migration (mechanical):
- ~10 tool files in OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/ and OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/Tools/: rename AnyJSONTool->OneTool, ToolParameter->OneToolParameter, SendableValue->OneToolValue. Sed-able.
- LingoDiagnosticSessionRecorder.swift: type recordAgentEvent parameter as OneAgentEvent. Switch body adapts mechanically (case names and payloads preserved 1:1 by mirror).
- SwarmToolToMCPAdapter.swift: change [any AnyJSONTool] -> [any OneTool]; internal logic unchanged.

Final cleanup:
- SwarmAgent.swift: remove @_exported import Swarm/Conduit/ConduitTraits lines once plugin code stops needing them.

Phase relationship:
- This feature is Phase 1 of the Swarm/Wax build migration.
- Phase 2 (xcframework prebuild) tracked separately as a sibling task that depends on this feature.
- Splitting them is necessary because the C-modulemap problem (CSQLite, USearchC, simsimd, stringzilla) only becomes solvable once plugins no longer have type-graph dependencies on those C modules transitively.
acceptance_criteria:
- Zero `import Swarm`, `import Conduit`, `import Wax`, `import ConduitTraits`, `import GRDB`, `import USearch` statements outside OneApp/SwarmAgent/ (verified by grep).
- Zero references to AnyJSONTool, AgentEvent, AgentError, AgentResult, ReActAgent, ConversationMemory, InMemorySession, any InferenceProvider, ToolParameter, SendableValue from inside OneApps/Ontology, OneApps/VibeMachine, OneApps/Muse (verified by grep).
- LingoDiagnosticSessionRecorder.recordAgentEvent's exhaustive switch covers all OneAgentEvent cases without losing any diagnostic field that was previously logged.
- SwarmAgent.swift no longer has @_exported import Swarm/Conduit/ConduitTraits lines.
- All existing test schemes pass: LingoAgentTests, OntologyMemoryCorpusTests, MuseTests, OneAppTests, SwarmAgentTests, VibeMachineTests, all tool-specific tests in OntologyTests.
- Sandbox app launch (mise run dev --sandbox) loads all plugins; Lingo chat produces a real assistant turn end-to-end; VibeMachine Design session produces a streaming assistant response.
- All 3 sub-tasks closed.
notes: Sanity checks completed in the planning conversation: (1) all 30 AgentEvent cases must be mirrored due to exhaustive switch in LingoDiagnosticSessionRecorder, (2) MuseResolvedInferenceProvider.provider visibility narrowing is the cleanest way to hide InferenceProvider from plugins, (3) BaseAgentService pattern accommodates both Ontology (continuous events) and VibeMachine (per-call throwing stream) with two real customization points: memory config and streaming shape. Estimated total: ~525 lines new SwarmAgent code, ~250 lines net plugin deletion, ~190 lines mechanical renames, 2 days of focused work. References: planning-n-design conversation in this beads session, OneApp/SwarmAgent/AgentService.swift, OneApps/Ontology/Agent/OntologyAgentService.swift, OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/AgentService.swift, OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/DesignAgent.swift, Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Core/AgentEvent.swift.
close_reason: All subtasks (31.1, 31.2, 31.3) closed. Plugins decoupled from Swarm via SwarmAgent facade. 32 (xcframework prebuild) is now unblocked.

title: Prebuild SwarmAgent.xcframework; remove SwiftPM from app build graph
description: Replace the Swarm SwiftPM local package reference inside SwarmAgent.framework with a prebuilt SwarmAgent.xcframework that statically links Swarm + Wax + Conduit + transitives and embeds all resources. After this, OneApp.xcodeproj has zero XCLocalSwiftPackageReference entries for Vendor/Swarm or Vendor/Wax, plugins continue consuming SwarmAgent.framework with no surface change, and Vendor/Swarm and Vendor/Wax remain unmodified upstream submodules. This is Phase 2 of the Swarm/Wax build migration; Phase 1 (runtime Wax_Wax.bundle workaround in MuseRuntime) is tracked under one-2xg.15.53 and will be removed as part of this bead.
design:
Build pipeline:
- Add scripts/build-swarmagent-xcframework.sh (also wired as 'mise run build:swarmagent-xcframework').
- Script drives SwiftPM against Vendor/Swarm/Package.swift to compile Swarm + Wax + Conduit + transitives (USearch, GRDB.swift, swift-tiktoken, swift-log, SwarmMacros via swift-syntax) for macOS arm64 (and x86_64 if needed for sandbox debugging on Intel; default arm64-only).
- Slice resulting binaries into a single SwarmAgent.xcframework using xcodebuild -create-xcframework.
- Embed resources into the xcframework: Wax_Wax.bundle (RAG/Resources, Shaders), all-MiniLM-L6-v2.mlmodelc, bert_tokenizer_vocab.txt. Verify Bundle.module accessors resolve to the xcframework's Resources at runtime.
- Macro plugin handling: SwarmMacros is a SwiftSyntax-based compiler plugin. Bundle the compiled plugin dylib inside the xcframework following the Swift 5.9+ binary macro plugin pattern (a CompilerPluginSupport binary). Risk: this path is newer in Xcode 16; if it does not link cleanly, fallback is to keep a tiny SwarmMacros SwiftPM compiler-plugin reference (compile-time only, no runtime/transitive leak into the app process) while still removing Swarm itself from the package graph.

Output:
- Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgent.xcframework/ checked into the repo. Submodule SHAs (Vendor/Swarm, Vendor/Wax) plus toolchain version pin determine when a rebuild is needed. If the artifact size proves prohibitive, switch to a Makefile/CI-built artifact downloaded into a gitignored Vendor/Prebuilt cache.

Project surgery:
- OneApp/OneApp.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj:
  * Remove XCLocalSwiftPackageReference '../Vendor/Swarm' (AGNT000E0000000000001).
  * Remove the 'Swarm' product reference (AGNT000D0000000000001) and the corresponding 'Swarm in Frameworks' build file (AGNT00010000000000004) from the SwarmAgent target.
  * Add Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgent.xcframework as a binary framework reference linked + embedded by the SwarmAgent target.
- OneApp/SwarmAgent/ source: stays as-is (AssistantConfigStore, KeychainService, ProviderResolver, MuseRuntime, Providers/, UI/, SwarmAgent.swift). The @_exported import Swarm / Conduit lines continue to work because those modules now come from the prebuilt xcframework.
- Remove WaxResourceBundleLookup runtime probe in OneApp/SwarmAgent/MuseRuntime.swift once xcframework embedding is verified working.

Submodule policy:
- Vendor/Swarm and Vendor/Wax remain pinned submodules; no patches applied. Bumping a submodule SHA requires re-running build:swarmagent-xcframework and committing the new artifact in the same commit.
- Document this contract in Vendor/Prebuilt/README.md (one short page).

Verification:
- mise run build app (clean derived data first).
- xcodebuild test on schemes: SwarmAgentTests, OntologyTests (filter LingoAgentTests, OntologyMemoryCorpusTests, MCP suites), MuseTests, OneAppTests.
- mise run dev --sandbox launches successfully; Muse + Ontology + VibeMachine plugins all activate; LingoChatView produces a real model response end-to-end.
- Confirm 'otool -L' on SwarmAgent.framework's binary references the xcframework path, not Vendor/Swarm SwiftPM build outputs.

Out of scope:
- Forking Vendor/Swarm or Vendor/Wax (no upstream divergence).
- Replacing Swarm's macro-based public API with hand-written types.
- Producer plugin wiring (its dependence on SwarmAgent comes for free once SwarmAgent migration lands).
acceptance_criteria: OneApp.xcodeproj contains zero XCLocalSwiftPackageReference entries pointing at Vendor/Swarm or Vendor/Wax. The SwarmAgent target links Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgent.xcframework. The build script (scripts/build-swarmagent-xcframework.sh and equivalent mise task) reproducibly produces SwarmAgent.xcframework from a clean checkout in a single command. Wax_Wax.bundle, all-MiniLM-L6-v2.mlmodelc, and Metal shaders resolve at runtime without any PACKAGE_RESOURCE_BUNDLE_PATH or Bundle.allBundles scan; the WaxResourceBundleLookup helper in MuseRuntime.swift is removed. SwarmAgentTests, OntologyMemoryCorpusTests (6), LingoAgentTests (13), MuseTests (1), and OneAppTests (390+) all pass. mise run dev --sandbox launches and Lingo chat produces a real assistant turn. one-2xg.15.53 can be closed once this bead lands.
notes:
2026-04-29 progress (architecture validation in flight):

Created committed scaffolding:
- Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgentBuild/{project.yml, Sources/SwarmAgentRuntime/SwarmAgentRuntime.swift, .gitignore}
- Vendor/Prebuilt/.gitignore (ignores generated SwarmAgent.xcframework symlink)
- scripts/build-swarmagent-xcframework.sh (cache-keyed, locked, idempotent; mirrors scripts/build-ghosttykit.sh)
- .mise/tasks/swarmagent-setup.sh (mirrors .mise/tasks/ghostty-setup.sh)

The wrapper consumes Vendor/Swarm via XCLocalSwiftPackageReference inside the build pipeline. The OneApp host project will see only Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgent.xcframework as a binary framework reference.

Build chain: xcodegen project.yml -> SwarmAgentBuild.xcodeproj -> xcodebuild archive (MACH_O_TYPE=staticlib, BUILD_LIBRARY_FOR_DISTRIBUTION=YES) -> xcodebuild -create-xcframework -> Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgent.xcframework. Cache key includes Swarm and Wax submodule SHAs, project.yml content, and Swift toolchain identity.

Two issues hit + resolved during validation:
1. First archive attempt failed due to transient github.com timeout when cloning USearch's fp16/simsimd/stringzilla submodules. Resolved by pointing -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath at workspace's existing .build/source-packages cache.
2. Second attempt failed because OTHER_SWIFT_FLAGS=-enable-experimental-feature StrictConcurrency was applied globally, breaking swift-log compilation. Removed; Swarm sets that flag at its own target level via Package.swift.

Open architectural validation (in flight): does xcodebuild -create-xcframework include the dependent Swift modules (Swarm.swiftmodule, Conduit.swiftmodule, etc.) inside the resulting xcframework, or only the wrapper's own SwarmAgentRuntime.swiftmodule? If only the latter, downstream code in OneApp/SwarmAgent that does `@_exported import Swarm` will fail at compile time. Workarounds available: (a) post-process the xcframework to copy dependent swiftmodules from derived-data, (b) switch the wrapper to a dynamic framework, (c) change OneApp/SwarmAgent.swift to `@_exported import SwarmAgentRuntime` only and rely on Swarm symbol re-export through the chain.

Punted to next session: pbxproj surgery (remove XCLocalSwiftPackageReference for Swarm + ConduitTraits, add xcframework binary ref), edit OneApp/SwarmAgent/SwarmAgent.swift import path, full test verification (LingoAgentTests, OntologyMemoryCorpusTests, MuseTests, OneAppTests, sandbox launch), removal of WaxResourceBundleLookup, integration with build.sh bootstrap, README.

title: Convert vendored Swarm and Wax off SwiftPM package integration
design: Finish the vendoring migration for Swarm/Wax by making SwarmAgent.framework own vendored sources/resources directly instead of relying on SwiftPM local package products at runtime. Remove or reduce SwiftPM package-resource lookup failures such as Wax_Wax.bundle in Ontology tests. Keep a single shared framework target consumed by Muse/Ontology/future Producer.
acceptance_criteria: Ontology memory Wax-backed tests no longer require SwiftPM resource bundle workarounds. Swarm/Wax are built through the shared framework path used by plugins, not independently as local package runtime resources. Focused OntologyMemoryCorpusTests pass.
notes:
Progress 2026-04-29: repaired the immediate Wax resource failure by moving Wax_Wax.bundle discovery into SwarmAgent/MuseRuntime instead of keeping a test-local PACKAGE_RESOURCE_BUNDLE_PATH workaround. OntologyMemoryCorpusTests now pass without test-specific Wax bundle setup. Also restored Swarm ConversationMemory + InMemorySession wiring in BaseAgentService and OntologyAgentService so Lingo multi-turn prompts include Conversation History and Relevant Context from Memory; LingoAgentTests pass. Remaining work: full removal of SwiftPM local package integration for Swarm/Wax is still open because Swarm currently brings Swift macros plus Conduit, Wax, SwiftSyntax, GRDB, USearch, SwiftTiktoken, and package resources through the package graph.
Verification: OntologyMemoryCorpusTests passed (6), LingoAgentTests passed (13), MuseTests passed (1), and app/OneApp tests passed (390). SwarmAgent has no separate test scheme in mise.
close_reason: Closed by one-2xg.32. Vendored Swarm/Wax now consumed exclusively through Vendor/Prebuilt/SwarmAgent.xcframework. Wax_Wax.bundle and the other SwiftPM resource bundles ride along inside SwarmAgent.framework/Resources/ via the resource-bundle copy phase. No SwiftPM Swarm/Wax integration in OneApp build graph.

title: Lingo loses conversation history across turns (memory and session not wired)
description: OntologyAgentService creates ReActAgent with memory: nil and never passes a Session to agent.stream(...). As a result, every user turn is sent to the model in isolation; pronouns and references to prior turns ('this ontology information', 'the schema you found') have no antecedent in the prompt. Also, prior tool observations (e.g. search_ontology_memory results) are lost between turns, defeating the agent's stated workflow of grounding answers in tool results. Fix: pass a ConversationMemory (cross-turn tool/observation memory) to the ReActAgent, and pass an InMemorySession on every stream call (cross-turn user+assistant transcript). Add a regression test that drives a recording InferenceProvider through two turns and asserts the second-turn prompt contains the first-turn user message and assistant reply.
acceptance_criteria: Two-turn integration test passes: turn 2 prompt contains turn 1 user text and turn 1 assistant text. ReActAgent is constructed with non-nil memory. agent.stream is called with a Session. Session and memory are torn down in cancel().
close_reason: Conversation memory + Session wiring shipped in d4a0f17e; regression tests now cover BaseAgentService two-turn history and cancel-clear behavior.

title: Ontology memory must only index packages installed in knowledge
design: Change ontology memory corpus construction so it only indexes ontology packages that are actually installed in the knowledge database. Use PackageBootstrapRegistry/SchemaApplyRegistry provenance for the target knowledge database and require package version/checksum alignment where available. If a package is loaded in the local cache but not installed, or if the cached version does not match the installed version, exclude it from memory and expose skipped-package diagnostics. This prevents Lingo from treating uninstalled or stale ontology packages as active modeling authority.
acceptance_criteria: search_ontology_memory indexes only packages installed in the knowledge database. Installed package versions/checksums are checked against loaded package metadata. Stale or uninstalled packages are skipped and reported. Tests cover installed match, uninstalled exclusion, and version mismatch exclusion.
close_reason: Ontology memory now filters to packages installed in the knowledge database with matching version/checksum metadata; focused filter tests pass.

title: Lingo must prefer gist primitives and produce review-quality summaries
design: Lingo schema proposals must treat gist as the modeling authority. Before proposing a new relation/type, the agent should search ontology memory and live schema for existing gist primitives and prefer reuse when a suitable primitive exists. The final assistant response should include well-crafted prose: verified schema facts, gist precedent, proposed TypeQL, rationale, caveats, and a concise summary that the user can compare against the Lingo Type Editor. Add prompt/tool guidance and tests using the Engineering Task hierarchy case where gist isDirectPartOf/isPartOf/isMemberOf should be preferred over invented Vibe-specific relations.
acceptance_criteria: For the engineering-task hierarchy prompt, Lingo proposes reuse of gist isDirectPartOf/isPartOf and Collection/isMemberOf rather than inventing vibeEngineeringTaskHierarchy or containsTopLevelEngineeringTask. The response narrative includes a clear summary section suitable for manual verification against the Type Editor. Tests assert gist primitive names appear and invented duplicate relation names do not.
close_reason: System prompt now names gist relation primitives (isPartOf, isDirectPartOf, isMemberOfCollection, Collection, OrderedCollection, isMemberOfOrg) and instructs the agent to consult them before inventing hierarchy/membership relations. propose_schema_change response gains existing_relation_labels (sorted list of all relations in live schema) so the agent has the structured precedent at proposal time. New prompt rule mandates a structured 'verifiable summary' after every proposal: verified live-schema facts, gist precedent, proposed TypeQL, rationale, drift/collisions, assumptions — comparable against the Lingo Type Editor. Tests in LingoAgentTests assert prompt names the gist primitives and requires the verifiable-summary structure; SchemaEvolutionToolsTests asserts existing_relation_labels surfaces gist's isPartOf/isDirectPartOf/isMemberOfCollection when gist is loaded. Pure agent-output behavior assertions remain LLM-dependent; structural enforcement is now in the prompt + tool response.

title: Lingo chat input lost history slash commands and model affordances
design: Restore chat composer affordances: input history navigation with arrow keys, slash command discovery/selection, and model/provider selection affordance if prior code exists. Preserve text selection and multiline entry behavior. Prefer reusing any previous shared composer implementation if present.
acceptance_criteria: The Lingo chat input recalls previous prompts with arrow keys when appropriate. Slash commands are discoverable/selectable. The user can see or choose the active model/provider using the restored affordance. Sending messages still works.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Lingo inheritance inspector lacks ontology context
design: Enhance the selected type inspector for Lingo proposal rows so inheritance displays the known hierarchy path and ontology/domain context for each type when available. For proposed types, distinguish proposed nodes from base/live ontology nodes. Use available parsed schema/proposal metadata; do not hard-code domain concepts.
acceptance_criteria: The inspector inheritance section makes parent/child hierarchy clear for selected rows. It includes ontology/domain context when available and labels proposed vs existing types.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Proposed relation inspector documentation is generic
design: Improve LingoTypeEditorPresentation so relation rows derive useful documentation from proposal payload fields and TypeQL structure. For relation rows, describe the relation and roles in domain terms when possible rather than falling back to 'Defined by the proposed TypeQL.'
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a proposed relation in the inspector shows documentation that names the relation and its roles. The old generic fallback is not used for relation rows when role/type information is available.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Proposed relation inspector motivation is generic
design: Improve relation motivation text by using proposal rationale, modeling_approach, concept metadata, and role structure. The motivation should explain why the relation exists in the proposed model, not merely that it came from proposed TypeQL.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a proposed relation shows motivation that explains the modeling purpose. The text is specific to the relation/roles when enough proposal data exists. The old generic 'Defined by the proposed type' fallback is removed from relation motivation.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Lingo Type Editor should auto-connect to Development Database
design: Rename user-facing sandbox language in the Lingo flow to Development Database. When the Lingo Type Editor opens and no active sandbox/development database exists, automatically create/select the single development database instead of requiring an inline chat sandbox affordance. Keep underlying SandboxHandle/SandboxManager names unless a deeper persistence rename is explicitly scoped later.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the Lingo Type Editor ensures there is an active development database. User-facing Lingo editor/inspector labels say Development Database, not Sandbox. Existing sandbox database names may remain internal implementation details.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Verify ontology memory against live schema
description: Ensure Lingo never treats Wax retrieval as authoritative schema state. Retrieved ontology memory must be checked against installed TypeDB state or parsed package TypeQL before schema proposals are generated.
design: Add the verification policy and implementation hooks after memory retrieval. For exact facts, use existing live schema/TypeDB tools, TypeQL parsing, package checksums, or package source lookup. If Wax says a concept exists but live TypeDB or current package source disagrees, surface the disagreement as drift/staleness in the assistant response or proposal assumptions. This bead is part of removing hard-coded domain knowledge: memory suggests context, verification proves current facts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Schema-design flow distinguishes retrieved precedent from verified current schema facts
- Proposal generation checks relevant type labels/relations/attributes/functions against live TypeDB or parsed package source
- Drift between Wax memory and live schema is visible to the user
- Tests cover stale memory and current-schema disagreement using real fixture components
- No hard-coded EngineeringTask/Umbrella hierarchy assumptions are introduced
close_reason: propose_schema_change now computes a live_schema_verification block via LingoProposalVerifier (parses the proposal TypeQL, compares each affected label against viewModel.currentSchemaLabelKinds()). Returns per-label status (new, existsSameKind, existsDifferentKind) with proposed_kind/live_kind, plus drift_count/collision_count/new_count and a policy explanation. Drift triggers a 'Drift detected against live schema' preamble in the assistant transcript so the user sees the conflict before approving. System prompt instructs the agent to inspect the verification block after every proposal. Tests in SchemaEvolutionToolsTests cover the pure verifier (new/sameKind/differentKind) and an integration path against the gist fixture asserting drift surfaces in the tool result and transcript. Source-of-truth distinction: memory remains precedent (search_ontology_memory), live schema verification is now structurally enforced at proposal time.

title: Expose Lingo ontology memory retrieval
description: Add a Lingo tool that searches the Ontology-owned Wax corpus and returns ontology context with provenance for schema-design conversations.
design: Create a SwarmAgent-compatible tool such as search_ontology_memory or recall_ontology_context in the Ontology plugin. The tool should query the Wax ontology corpus, return concise ranked context, and include provenance metadata for package, version/revision, source path, type label, domain/module, and whether the result came from schema, TypeDoc, domain, or view content. The tool belongs to Lingo/Ontology, not Muse. Muse only supplies shared runtime/memory plumbing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lingo sessions register the ontology memory retrieval tool when the corpus is available
- Tool output is structured enough for transcript diagnostics and future generative UI rendering
- Missing or stale Wax stores degrade gracefully with a clear message
- The Lingo prompt instructs the agent to use ontology memory for design precedent and to cite/surface provenance
- Tests prove the tool returns relevant fixture ontology context
close_reason: Already implemented. SearchOntologyMemoryTool (OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/OntologyMemoryTools.swift) is registered in LingoAgent.makeTools and emits structured query/index/results/verification/source_of_truth_policy output. Provenance dictionary surfaces package/version/git rev/source path/type label/domain/view key/installed_database. Verification block compares each result's typeLabel against currentSchemaLabelKinds. Prompt instructs use (LingoSystemPrompt.swift lines 42, 49, 66). Graceful failure via OntologyMemoryError.museUnavailable. Substrate covered by OntologyMemoryCorpusTests; LingoAgentTests asserts tool registration. Tighter agent-flow assertions remain part of 15.38 + 15.20.

title: Index ontology packages into Wax
description: Build the Ontology-owned Wax corpus that ingests resolved ontology package source and documentation for fast repeated semantic discovery by Lingo.
design: Implement an Ontology-side indexing service that reads resolved packages from PackageManager, loads raw TypeQL through SchemaLoader, loads TypeDoc/domain/schema-view documentation through StaticSchemaProvider, and writes searchable chunks to a Wax .mv2s store. Prefer Wax text search/BM25 initially so the corpus works without embedding setup; leave vector embeddings optional/configurable through Muse plumbing. Store enough metadata on every chunk to report provenance and support stale-index detection. Do not index hard-coded modeling concepts outside package content.
acceptance_criteria:
- Resolved ontology package schemas and docs can be ingested into a local Wax store
- Indexing is repeatable and idempotent for unchanged package/version/revision/checksum inputs
- Updated package versions or git commits cause stale entries to be superseded or rebuilt
- The index includes provenance sufficient to open or report source package/file/type context
- Tests cover fixture packages without mocks
close_reason: Already implemented. OntologyMemoryCorpus (OneApps/Ontology/Backend/OntologyMemoryCorpus.swift) builds a Wax-backed MuseTextMemoryStore from PackageManager.resolveLoadOrder, SchemaLoader, and StaticSchemaProvider, with TypeQLParser per-type records. Fingerprint-keyed manifest gives idempotent rebuilds across version/git-rev/checksum changes. Provenance captured per record. OntologyMemoryPackageFilter restricts to installed-and-matching packages (per 15.52). OntologyMemoryCorpusTests exercises fixture packages with the real DefaultMuseRuntime (no mocks). title: Define ontology memory corpus sources

title: Detect and flag untracked changes on sandbox reopen
description: If Lingo crashes mid-write or a sandbox is edited directly via TypeQL outside the paired-write path, reopening it flags the orphaned schema atoms as untracked ChangeIntents — one per atom. Subsequent reopens of the same sandbox do not re-detect the same orphans (convergence). The intent log is always an honest account of sandbox state.
design:
The design has three components that together guarantee convergence.

1. Atom model: the unit of drift.
   A schema "atom" is the smallest change we track. Atom kinds are:
     - entity: an entity type declaration (targetLabel = entity name)
     - attribute: an attribute type declaration (targetLabel = attribute name)
     - relation: a relation type declaration (targetLabel = relation name)
     - role: a role on a relation (targetLabel = "<relation>.<role>")
     - owns: an attribute ownership (targetLabel = "<owner>.<attribute>")
     - sub: a parent-type declaration (targetLabel = "<type>.sub")
     - function: a function declaration (targetLabel = function name — simple identifier, no delimiter)
   Each atom is uniquely identifiable by (kind, label).

   Function body changes are NOT atoms in v1. Atoms track presence only. A function present in the sandbox but absent from the accepted set produces one drift atom with AtomKind.function. If the function is present in both sides but its body drifted (someone edited it out-of-band), that is NOT detected as an atom — drift detection in v1 is presence-only for functions. This is a known v1 limitation; body-drift detection can be added post-v1 if it becomes important.

2. Accepted-atoms set: what the sandbox knows about.
   When computing drift on reopen, the "accepted" schema state is:
     - For non-untracked intents: atoms derived by parsing the reference-DB schema after replay
     - For untracked intents (action = "untracked"): add (kind, label) directly to accepted atoms, bypassing any TypeQL replay

   Accepted atoms = replay atoms ∪ untracked atoms.

3. Drift atoms = real schema atoms − accepted atoms.
   Parse the real sandbox's typeSchema() into atoms. Anything in real-atoms but not in accepted-atoms is drift. For each drift atom, synthesize one untracked ChangeIntent with targetKind and targetLabel set to the atom's fields.

Convergence guarantee:
  After reopen N: drift atoms are detected and written as untracked intents.
  Before reopen N+1: untracked intents contribute their (kind, label) to accepted atoms.
  During reopen N+1: previously-orphaned atoms are in accepted atoms; real atoms still include them; no drift. Convergent.

Requirements on other features:
  - SandboxMeta.sourceName must be reliably populated for every sandbox (one-2xg.3.3).
  - Non-untracked intents' forwardTypeql must be well-formed and replayable.
  - ChangeIntent schema does NOT need new attributes — targetKind and targetLabel carry the atom identity.
  - Parser upgrade (one-2xg.5.9) must be landed — function atoms come from parsing the upgraded ParsedFunction.
acceptance_criteria:
- Drift is modeled as atoms with (kind, label) identity
- AtomKind covers: entity, attribute, relation, role, owns, sub, function
- v1 limitation documented: function body drift is NOT detected (presence-only)
- Accepted atoms = replay atoms ∪ untracked atoms
- Drift atoms = real atoms − accepted; each produces one untracked ChangeIntent
- Subsequent reopens produce no new untracked intents (convergence tested in 6.3)
- Sandbox provenance comes from SandboxMeta.sourceName (one-2xg.3.3 dependency)
- Parser upgrade (one-2xg.5.9) dependency — needed to extract function atoms
- All L4 tests pass
close_reason: all child tasks closed; drift detection + untracked-intent synthesis with convergence proven

title: Compute a human-readable diff between two ontologies
description: Given any two TypeDB databases, a pure function returns a structured, human-inspectable diff covering: added/removed entities, relations, attributes, and roles; added/removed owns clauses (with the owning type); cardinality changes on existing owns clauses; sub (inheritance) changes; and added / removed / body-changed functions. Inheritance is correctly accounted for — inherited members on subtypes are not double-counted.
design:
The diff's first-class output categories (frozen contract):

1. Type-level adds/removes:
   - addedEntities / removedEntities
   - addedRelations / removedRelations
   - addedAttributes / removedAttributes
   - addedRoles / removedRoles

2. Owns-clause adds/removes (scoped to the owning type):
   - addedOwnsClauses: [(owner: String, attribute: String)]
   - removedOwnsClauses: [(owner: String, attribute: String)]

3. Cardinality changes:
   - cardinalityChanges: [(owner, attribute, from, to)]

4. Sub (inheritance) changes:
   - subChanges: [(type, from, to)]

5. Function changes:
   - addedFunctions: [ParsedFunction]
   - removedFunctions: [ParsedFunction]
   - functionBodyChanges: [(name, fromBody, toBody)]

Rename handling: explicitly NOT detected by the diff. A rename applied as undefine+define surfaces as one removal + one addition. Rename-ness lives in the ChangeIntent log (one-2xg.4); MigrationAuthor (one-2xg.7) uses the log to reconstruct renames when authoring TypeQL output.

Function body changes: a function present in both sides with the same name but a different body emits exactly one functionBodyChanges entry — not a remove+add pair. Body equality is TEXTUAL equality after a lightweight normalization (trim leading/trailing whitespace, collapse internal whitespace runs to single spaces, strip comments). Semantically-equivalent bodies with different text are treated as different; Lingo does not attempt semantic equivalence.

Inheritance: inherited members on subtypes are NOT counted as adds/removes on the subtype unless the subtype itself declares them directly.

Prerequisite: the parser upgrade task (one-2xg.5.9) must land first — SchemaDiff consumes ParsedRole, ParsedOwns, Cardinality, ParsedFunction, and related fields.

No reliance on ChangeIntentWriter or any mutable state — SchemaDiff is pure.
acceptance_criteria:
- SchemaDiff pure function exists with all contract categories above
- Type-level adds/removes covered for entities, relations, attributes, roles
- Owns clauses reported with the owning type (scoped adds/removes)
- Cardinality changes reported as structured CardinalityChange entries
- Sub-inheritance changes reported as structured SubChange entries
- addedFunctions, removedFunctions reported as [ParsedFunction]
- functionBodyChanges reported with name + fromBody + toBody
- Same-name different-body functions emit one functionBodyChanges entry (NOT remove+add)
- Body equality uses documented normalization (whitespace + comment strip)
- Inheritance: inherited members NOT double-counted on subtypes
- Rename NOT detected — surfaces as delete+add (reconstruction in one-2xg.7)
- All child tests pass against the upgraded parser
- Parser upgrade task (one-2xg.5.9) lands BEFORE 5.1 starts
close_reason: all child tasks closed; SchemaDiff stack with parser upgrade covers every diff category from contract

title: Atomically record every schema change with its motivation
description: Every schema change in a sandbox is recorded together with its motivation — either both land or neither does. You can query the ordered history of any sandbox and see N changes chain correctly through the changeSequence relation, grouped by concept via changeConcept.
design:
TypeDB 3.x requires separate transaction types for schema changes and data writes. A schema transaction and a data transaction cannot be atomically combined into a single commit. The ChangeIntentWriter owns a compensating-transaction pattern: apply the schema change and commit; write the intent record and commit; if the second commit fails, run a compensating schema transaction that reverses the first. Residual failure mode — the process dies between the two commits — handled by drift reconciliation in one-2xg.6.

ChangeIntentReader queries the intent log via TypeQL against the sandbox itself:
  - ordered by changeSequence chain
  - grouped by changeConcept concept
  - filtered by session / time window

Relation names come from the meta-schema in one-2xg.3:
  - changeSequence (roles earlier, later) — was originally named "precedes" in early drafts; renamed to avoid collision with gist's own precedes relation
  - changeConcept (roles intent, concept) — was originally named "groupedUnder"; renamed for clarity and collision-safety

L2 tests inject an intent-write failure and assert the compensating rollback restores pre-call state. N-apply tests assert correct changeSequence chaining.
acceptance_criteria:
- ChangeIntentWriter.applySchemaDelta(..., motivation:, groupTag:) writes both the schema change and the matching ChangeIntent instance
- Injected intent-write failure triggers compensating schema reversal; sandbox returns to pre-call state
- ChangeIntentReader returns N applied intents in correct changeSequence order
- ChangeIntentReader filters by changeConcept concept and by time window
- All L2 tests pass in OntologyTests
- No references to precedes or groupedUnder remain in any task design under this feature
close_reason: all child tasks closed; L2 integration tests cover the writer + reader behavior end-to-end

title: Bootstrap every sandbox with a change-log schema
description:
Every new sandbox boots with the ChangeIntent entity, the SandboxMeta entity, the changeSequence relation, and the changeConcept relation already loaded alongside the base schema — visible in the TypeDB console, ready for intent writes and metadata reads. The meta-schema is source-agnostic: it works whether the sandbox's base contains gist, some other upper ontology, or nothing at all.

Change-log scope includes every TypeDB 3.x schema object: entities, relations, attributes, roles, owns clauses, sub declarations, AND functions. A user evolving an ontology through Lingo can add, remove, or modify any of these; the intent log captures the change with the appropriate targetKind.
acceptance_criteria:
- ChangeIntent, SandboxMeta entities and changeSequence, changeConcept relations exist in every newly created sandbox
- Fragment is fully self-contained: no references to gist, vibemachine, or any other upper ontology (verified by grep)
- Naming does not collide with gist's existing types and relations (verified by grep)
- targetKind enum values documented: entity, attribute, relation, role, owns, sub, function
- Bundled as a Swift string constant, not a file resource

- SandboxMeta instance written at create time carries correct sandbox name, source name, createdAt, and creatorVersion

title: Create and manage throwaway ontology sandboxes
description: Code that creates a sandbox TypeDB database from any existing source DB (e.g., knowledge), lists sandboxes, drops them, and reopens them. You can quit OneApp, come back, and the sandbox's schema and data are exactly as you left them.
design:
SandboxManager lives in OneApps/Ontology/ alongside the existing OntologyTypeDBClient. It exposes create(from:), drop, list, and reopen, built on the TypeDBSwift primitives proven in F1 — exportRecords from source, importFromRecords into a freshly-created knowledge-sandbox-{uuid} database. Sandboxes persist via TypeDB's on-disk storage; no extra plumbing needed for restart survival.

L1 tests in OntologyTests assert:
- clone fidelity (sandbox's typeSchema() and record set match source)
- additive meta-schema (the ChangeIntent fragment from F3 applies without conflicting with the self-describing schema already loaded)
- process-restart persistence (tear down the driver, rebuild, query the sandbox — state intact)
acceptance_criteria:
- SandboxManager.create(from: "knowledge") produces a sandbox whose schema + records match the source
- list() enumerates existing sandboxes
- drop(id:) removes a sandbox and leaves all others untouched
- reopen(id:) returns a working handle to a pre-existing sandbox
- L1 test: process-restart with driver teardown + rebuild preserves sandbox state
- L1 test: additive meta-schema loads cleanly on a cloned sandbox
close_reason: All code-visible acceptance criteria met: SandboxManager.create/list/drop/reopen implemented (2.1, 2.2, 2.7), clone fidelity test (2.3) + ChangeIntent meta-schema test (2.4) + driver-teardown persistence test (2.5) all passing against live gamma-typedb. 2.6 remains open as a human-verify gate and is tracked independently.

title: Prove the TypeDB driver can clone, evolve, and isolate databases
description: A green test suite in OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/ that pins down exactly what the TypeDBSwift driver guarantees — the floor every later layer stands on. Specifically: exportRecords + importRecords round-trips a populated database faithfully; schema transactions (define / undefine) become visible in subsequent typeSchema() calls; deleting one database never affects any other. Any driver-level wrinkles are discovered and documented here, before we build anything on top.
design:
Tests live in OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/ and run against a real gamma-typedb workload (no mocks, per project policy). Fixtures build a non-trivial schema with at least one entity, one relation, one attribute with cardinality, and instances exercising all three — enough surface to catch serialization edge cases in the round-trip. Schema-transaction tests use TypeDBDriver.query(_, database:, transactionType: .schema) to confirm in-process define/undefine apply without shell-out to the CLI. Delete-isolation tests create two sibling databases, delete one, assert the other is untouched via listing and schema readback.

No new production code is introduced in this feature — only tests and minimal fixture helpers. If a genuine driver gap surfaces (e.g., a round-trip fidelity bug), it's captured as a discovered-from follow-up issue rather than worked around in fixtures.
acceptance_criteria:
- Export/import round-trip: imported DB's typeSchema() and instance set are indistinguishable from source
- Schema transaction: define adds a type visible in subsequent typeSchema(); undefine removes it
- Delete isolation: deleting DB A does not alter DB B's schema or instance set
- All three tests pass against gamma-typedb workload
- Any driver wrinkles logged as follow-up issues linked via discovered-from
close_reason: All four children closed: 1.1 round-trip test, 1.2 schema-transaction test, 1.3 delete-isolation test, 1.4 human-verify. Driver floor proven green against the live gamma-typedb workload.

title: Lingo — AI-Assisted Ontology Evolution (v1)
description: A user opens OneApp, describes a concept they want in their ontology, and has a conversation that ends with the concept permanently part of the shared ontology. They never leave the app and never touch git. Starting a brand-new ontology works the same way — same conversation, beginning from a blank template instead of an existing one. The experience works whether the user is adding one concept in a minute or thousands of concepts over days. Power users get the same capability from a `brew install`-able CLI. Continuous integration gates every pull request with the same tool. External agents — Claude Code, Codex — can drive the same primitives over MCP.
design:
The experience is built on three substrates:

1. A Rust core library (rust/ontology-core/) that owns schema validation, migration contracts, package validators, semver logic, and migration authoring. It is the single source of truth for every consumer. Rust because the CLI runs on Linux CI, and Rust's C ABI lets the Swift app consume the same code without duplication.

2. A Homebrew-distributed CLI called `ontology` that wraps the Rust core. Power users run `ontology validate`, `ontology new`, `ontology release` from a terminal. GitHub Actions invokes the same binary to gate PRs.

3. A Lingo experience inside the Ontology plugin — conversational exploration with an AI agent, sandbox-backed schema evolution, intent-logged history, and a codification path that turns a finished exploration into a real pull request on the ontology-* repo, tracks CI status in-chat, merges on user confirmation, and refreshes the local knowledge database automatically. The plugin links the Rust core via C ABI.

All schema continues to live in git repositories under the existing versioned package contract. The migration triple (preflight / migration / verify) format stays. What changes is that the Node.js tooling is replaced with Rust, and a new GUI path makes the entire PR lifecycle drivable from chat.

Out of v1 scope (deferred): merge-conflict resolution between concurrent users; bulk-loading ontologies from external formats (Excel, SysML); scale-specific UI virtualization. These are future concerns — call them out when they bite.
acceptance_criteria:
- All child features closed (F1–F27, minus F25 which was explicitly scoped out)
- A user can add a new concept to vibe-machine via conversation: talk it through, confirm gist placement, watch it codify into a PR, see green CI, and watch the concept appear in their local knowledge DB on merge
- A user can start a brand-new ontology from scratch via the same conversational flow, ending with a new ontology-* repo on GitHub with its first version tagged
- A power user can do both flows from the command line via `brew install`-able `ontology` CLI
- GitHub Actions gates PRs against ontology-* repos with the Rust validator
- External agents (Claude Code, Codex) can drive the exploration via MCP
- Sandboxes survive quit and relaunch with intent log intact
- GammaAgent settings supports ZAI / OpenRouter / Anthropic / OpenAI with hand-entered models and custom endpoints
- The user never has to open git, Xcode, or a terminal to complete the core experience

title: UI Testing Autmation
description: Automate the AI bug-fix loop for UI issues: create repro test first, reproduce failure, iterate code/test until stable pass, and provide journey-proof evidence.
design:
## Objective
Create a production workflow where an AI coding agent can fix UI bugs end-to-end without manual UI verification or manual Instruments setup.

## Execution Model
- Real XCUIAutomation (XCTest UI tests driving the real app).
- Makefile-first command surface for all workflows.
- Real backend first test mode.
- Test-first rule for UI bugs.

## Agent Workflow to Support
1. Human reports a bug journey.
2. Agent checks whether a UI test already covers this journey.
3. If not, agent adds a repro UI test first.
4. Agent proves repro test fails.
5. Agent iterates fix + tests until pass.
6. Agent requires 3-run stability before claiming done.
7. Agent reports journey-proof evidence.

## Constraints
- Must run via make targets.
- Must not require manual Instruments configuration.
- Deterministic selectors via accessibility identifiers.
acceptance_criteria:

- Each child bead includes complete design + testable acceptance criteria.
- Existing overlapping UI testing feature (one-6te) is linked for traceability.
- Resulting workflow is executable by AI agents without manual test-driving.
