title: Build ontology corpus lab vertical slice
description: Add the first executable ontology corpus workflow: bootstrap an ontology package into TypeDB, load corpus fixture data, run curated TypeQL examples, and export prompt-ready examples for Lingo.
design:
## Scope
Implement the first corpus-lab slice for the Rust ontology-core direction. This slice proves the end-to-end developer workflow before the full Node.js port is complete: load an ontology package, apply corpus fixtures, run known-good TypeQL examples, and export prompt-ready examples for Lingo.

The corpus source of truth lives in ontology repos. Start with `/Users/kenpo/SoftwareProjects/collection-vibe-machine/ontology-gist` because GIST is the base ontology every domain assistant must understand. Shared runner logic belongs in the Rust workspace in OneWorkspace. Thin mise tasks in ontology-gist delegate to the shared binary/API rather than reimplementing package bootstrap or query execution.

## Rust Workspace Shape
Use a crate layout that can grow into the general Vibe Machine CLI/TUI foundation while keeping the corpus slice focused.

```
rust/
  Cargo.toml
  crates/
    ontology-core/
      Cargo.toml
      src/
        lib.rs
        error.rs
        corpus/
          mod.rs
          model.rs
          discover.rs
          validate.rs
          run.rs
          export.rs
        package/
          mod.rs
          executable.rs
    ontology-cli/
      Cargo.toml
      src/
        lib.rs
        args.rs
        commands/
          mod.rs
          corpus.rs
          version.rs
        format/
          mod.rs
          json.rs
          text.rs
        logging.rs
    ontology-tui/
      Cargo.toml
      src/
        lib.rs
        app.rs
        event.rs
        terminal.rs
        panic.rs
        view/
          mod.rs
  bin/
    ontology/
      Cargo.toml
      src/main.rs
```

Dependency direction is one-way:

```
ontology bin -> ontology-cli -> ontology-core
             -> ontology-tui -> ontology-core
```

`ontology-cli` and `ontology-tui` must not depend on each other. They communicate only through `ontology-core`. The binary chooses the execution mode.

For this bead, implement the scripted corpus path fully. The TUI crate may be a compile-clean scaffold with terminal lifecycle primitives, but no corpus-specific interactive UI is required for acceptance.

## Workspace Dependencies And Lints
At the Rust workspace root, declare shared dependency versions and forbid unsafe code:

```toml
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"
```

Expected dependency families:
- CLI: `clap` with derive/env/wrap_help, `clap_complete`, `clap_mangen`
- TUI foundation: `ratatui`, `crossterm`
- async/cancellation: `tokio`, `tokio-stream`, `futures`, `tokio-util`
- errors: `thiserror` in ontology-core, `anyhow` at CLI/TUI/bin boundaries
- logging: `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber`, `tracing-appender`
- output/data: `serde`, `serde_json`, optionally `serde_yaml`, `tabled`, `anstream`
- tests: `assert_cmd`, `predicates`, and snapshot tooling if introduced

Pin concrete minor versions when implementing. Check current crate versions at implementation time rather than copying stale versions blindly.

## Binary Mode Selection
`rust/bin/ontology/src/main.rs` should stay small: parse args, initialize logging, choose mode, dispatch.

Mode-selection precedence:
1. If a subcommand is present, run scripted mode regardless of TTY.
2. If `--no-tui` or `--format=<x>` is set, do not launch the TUI.
3. If stdout is not a TTY, do not launch the TUI.
4. If `CI` or `ONTOLOGY_NO_TUI` is set, do not launch the TUI.
5. Otherwise interactive TUI is allowed.

For this bead, `ontology corpus ...` commands are the important path. Agents and mise tasks must never accidentally land in a TUI.

## ontology-core: Corpus Domain API
`ontology-core` is the domain layer. It must not expose `clap`, `ratatui`, or `crossterm` types in public APIs. It must not print. It returns typed `thiserror` errors.

Minimum corpus model:

```rust
pub mod corpus {
    pub struct Corpus {
        pub repo_path: PathBuf,
        pub manifest: CorpusManifest,
        pub items: Vec<CorpusItem>,
    }

    pub struct CorpusManifest {
        pub version: u32,
        pub ontology_package: String,
        pub fixtures: Vec<Fixture>,
    }

    pub struct CorpusItem {
        pub id: String,
        pub title: String,
        pub natural_language_intent: String,
        pub query_kind: QueryKind,
        pub ontology_tags: Vec<String>,
        pub fixtures: Vec<String>,
        pub typeql: String,
        pub expected: ExpectedResult,
        pub prompt_export: PromptExport,
        pub provenance: Option<String>,
    }

    pub enum QueryKind { Schema, Read, Write, Fetch, Reduce }
    pub enum ExpectedResult { RowCount(u64), NonEmpty, Empty, JsonShape(serde_json::Value) }
    pub enum PromptExport { Include, Exclude, BadToGood }
}
```

Minimum public functions:

```rust
pub fn discover_corpus(repo_path: &Path) -> Result<Corpus, Error>;
pub fn validate_corpus_manifest(corpus: &Corpus) -> Result<(), Error>;
pub async fn validate_corpus(request: CorpusRunRequest) -> Result<CorpusReport, Error>;
pub fn export_prompt_examples(request: PromptExportRequest) -> Result<PromptExportReport, Error>;
```

`validate_corpus` should use a real TypeDB database. During the transition it may call existing Node.js package tooling to bootstrap the package, but Rust owns corpus parsing, validation model, filtering, reporting, and export shape.

Long-running operations should be async and accept `tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken` once the operation surface requires it. Do not add callbacks; streaming status can be represented later as `Stream<Item = Result<CorpusEvent, Error>>`.

## ontology-cli: Scripted Corpus Surface
Add global args:
- `--no-tui`
- `--format json|text`
- `-v/--verbose`
- `--quiet`
- optional `--config`

Add scripted commands:

```text
ontology corpus test --repo <path> [--tag <tag>] [--item <id>] [--database <name>] [--keep-db] [--format json|text]
ontology corpus export --repo <path> [--tag <tag>] [--output <path>] [--format json|text]
ontology version [--format json|text]
ontology completions <shell>
```

Output discipline:
- stdout is data only.
- stderr is progress/logging only.
- `--format json` emits a single JSON value to stdout and a trailing newline.
- mise tasks should use explicit subcommands and should be safe in non-TTY/CI contexts.

## ontology-tui: Foundation Boundary
If implemented in this bead, keep it skeletal and correct:
- `TerminalSession` owns raw mode + alternate screen and restores on drop.
- panic hook restores terminal before delegating to original hook.
- event loop unifies key/mouse/resize/tick/signal/domain messages.
- `q`, Esc, Ctrl-C, SIGINT, and SIGTERM all take the same graceful-exit path.

Do not build corpus-specific TUI screens in this bead unless the scripted path is already complete.

## Corpus File Shape In ontology-gist
Use a plain, reviewable format under `ontology-gist/corpus/`. JSON is preferred for v0 because Rust can parse it with `serde_json` without adding YAML ambiguity.

Expected layout:

```
ontology-gist/
  corpus/
    manifest.json
    fixtures/
      meeting-decisions-schema.tql
      meeting-decisions-data.tql
    queries/
      meeting-decisions.json
    negative/
      typedb2-get.json
      missing-relation-roles.json
```

Each query item carries:
- `id`
- `title`
- `natural_language_intent`
- `query_kind`: `schema`, `read`, `write`, `fetch`, or `reduce`
- `ontology_tags`, e.g. `gist`, `activity`, `content`, `agreement`, `magnitude`, `unit`
- `fixtures` required
- `typeql`
- `expected`
- `prompt_export`: `include`, `exclude`, or `bad_to_good`
- `provenance`

Negative or repair examples are useful, but keep them separated from known-good prompt examples. They should not be exported into generation prompts unless explicitly requested as bad-to-good guidance.

## Initial GIST Corpus
Create a minimal GIST-grounded corpus that exercises the patterns Lingo has already failed around:
- Meeting/Activity modeling against GIST roots
- Decision/Content modeling so decisions are not incorrectly made Activities
- a relation with explicit roles between an Activity-like thing and Content-like thing
- a read query that answers which meetings produced decisions
- at least one fetch or select example suitable for prompt export

If GIST does not already contain exact domain-specific labels for Meeting/Decision, fixture schema overlays may define domain subtypes grounded in GIST. The goal is to validate GIST-grounded modeling, not to pretend all domain terms are already in the upper ontology.

## Mise Surface
Add repo-local tasks to ontology-gist:

```bash
mise run corpus:test
mise run corpus:export
```

The tasks delegate to the Rust binary/API. They must be deterministic and must not call an LLM.

Optional live generation/lab mode should be explicit and should not run as part of normal tests. If included later, call it `corpus:lab-live` or similar so provider usage is impossible to trigger accidentally.

## OneWorkspace Integration
Do not wire the Ontology plugin to live TypeDB corpus execution in this bead. Instead, produce a stable generated artifact that one-537.13 can consume when improving `TypeQL3PromptGuide` and prompt fixtures. Document the artifact path and format, e.g.:

```
ontology-gist/generated/corpus/typeql-prompt-examples.json
```

## Testing Strategy
- `ontology-core`: pure unit tests for corpus parsing/filtering/export shape; integration test for real TypeDB corpus validation.
- `ontology-cli`: argument parsing tests and command tests with `assert_cmd` where practical.
- `ontology-tui`: only if scaffolded; use `ratatui::backend::TestBackend` for render/update tests and no real TTY dependency.
- End-to-end verification: `mise run corpus:test` from ontology-gist validates the Meeting/Activity + Decision/Content corpus against real TypeDB.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rust workspace exists under `rust/` with compile-clean crates for `ontology-core`, `ontology-cli`, and the `ontology` binary; `ontology-tui` exists as either a compile-clean scaffold or a deliberately deferred follow-up bead
- Cargo workspace forbids unsafe code and builds with `cargo build --workspace`
- `ontology-core` owns corpus model parsing, manifest validation, filtering, reporting, and prompt-example export types without depending on clap/ratatui/crossterm
- Scripted commands exist for `ontology corpus test`, `ontology corpus export`, `ontology version`, and `ontology completions`
- CLI output discipline is enforced: data on stdout, progress/logs/errors on stderr, and `--format json` emits one JSON value to stdout
- ontology-gist contains a `corpus/` directory with at least one fixture and multiple GIST-grounded query items
- `mise run corpus:test` from ontology-gist validates the checked-in corpus against a real TypeDB database without using an LLM
- `mise run corpus:export` from ontology-gist produces a deterministic prompt-example artifact from passing, export-eligible corpus items
- Rust code owns corpus item parsing/validation/reporting, even if package bootstrap temporarily shells out to existing Node.js tooling
- The initial corpus includes a Meeting/Activity + Decision/Content example and a query answering which meetings produced decisions
- Negative/repair examples are represented separately from known-good prompt examples
- The exported artifact format is documented well enough for one-537.13 to consume it without reverse engineering
- Normal test tasks do not call a live LLM; any live lab mode is isolated behind an explicit mise task
notes:
Direction relocated 2026-05-04: the durable Rust workspace lives in `ontology-tooling/` (not under OneWorkspace). It exposes the `vibe-ontology` library (embeddable in OneApp / Lingo / other products) and the `ont` CLI/TUI binary. v0 of `ont corpus list` and `ont corpus validate` shipped under ontool-a29; follow-ups: ontool-0l0 (corpus export), ontool-2wj (TypeDB executor), ontool-t16 (corpus generate), ontool-0zf (TUI corpus browser).

This bead's design currently scopes the workspace under OneWorkspace's `rust/` tree — that section is superseded. The corpus-lab vertical-slice acceptance criteria (Meeting/Activity + Decision/Content example, real TypeDB validation, deterministic prompt artifact) still apply, but should be satisfied by changes in ontology-tooling + ontology-gist rather than OneWorkspace. Consider splitting this bead into a "consume vibe-ontology from OneWorkspace plugins" piece + closing the workspace-creation piece against ontool-a29.

title: Rejected alternatives feed future synthesis
description: Persist rejected schema alternatives, judge reasons, user decisions, GIST choices, and pattern choices so future synthesis becomes accretive.
design:
## Implementation Shape
Extend synthesis memory so every non-trivial modeling turn leaves reusable traces: accepted deltas, rejected deltas, judge rejection reasons, user clarification answers, confirmed or rejected GIST anchors, pattern candidates used or discarded, and migration ambiguity decisions.

Future context assembly should retrieve these traces to avoid repeated bad proposals and preserve user modeling intent across sessions.

This should integrate with the existing ChangeIntent / CompetencyQuestion / ConversationTurn model rather than introducing an unrelated store.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rejected proposals and judge reasons are persisted as first-class synthesis history.
- User-confirmed modeling decisions are retrievable in later turns.
- Context assembly includes relevant prior rejections and decisions.
- Tests show that a repeated prompt can see a prior rejection/decision in its synthesis context.
notes:
## Validation Matrix
Fast required tests: synthesis-history persistence tests for rejected deltas, judge reasons, user decisions, confirmed/rejected GIST anchors, pattern choices, and migration ambiguity decisions.
Integration checkpoint tests: context assembly retrieves prior rejection/decision traces and downstream synthesis avoids repeating a rejected modeling choice.
Epic close tests: full Ontology test target plus opt-in live-LLM smoke over a repeated prompt that should use prior synthesis memory.

title: Accretive GIST conformance and pattern library
description: Turn GIST expertise and reusable ontology patterns into explicit inspectable assets rather than relying on prompt instructions and weak vector memory.
design:
## Feature Scope
Create an authored ontology pattern substrate for synthesis. Each reusable pattern should pair natural-language intent, GIST anchor rationale, TypeQL snippets, examples, anti-patterns, and conformance checks. Pattern retrieval should search this authored content rather than raw TypeQL alone.

Expand GIST conformance beyond shallow hardcoded checks. The rule set should encode modeling expectations such as required grounding, relation role-player declarations, measurement/unit patterns where applicable, naming consistency, and other conventions that survive the OWL-to-TypeQL projection.

The library should be inspectable and versioned so the system becomes more expert over time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pattern records include natural-language descriptions, TypeQL fragments, examples, anti-patterns, and GIST alignment rationale.
- Pattern retrieval quality can be tested with representative ontology-design prompts.
- GIST conformance checks are represented as explicit reusable rules or validators, not only prompt text.
- Judge results cite the specific pattern or conformance rule behind accept/reject guidance where applicable.
notes:
## Validation Matrix
Fast required tests: pattern retrieval and GIST conformance unit/integration tests with representative ontology-design prompts and authored pattern fixtures; assert retrieved patterns are relevant and conformance failures cite explicit rules.
Integration checkpoint tests: run Judge semantic/conformance slices using the authored rule/pattern library and verify generator context includes pattern rationales.
Epic close tests: full Ontology test target plus opt-in live-LLM smoke showing the agent uses GIST/pattern guidance in a real proposal.

title: Color Lingo Browser type labels by defining ontology
description: When the Lingo Browser displays a type reference, the referenced type text should use the color associated with the ontology where that type is defined, such as using the gist color for `thing` in `sub Thing`.
design:
## User Impact
Ontology provenance is critical during schema review. Today, type references can look visually homogeneous or inherit the selected row kind color, so users cannot quickly tell whether a parent, attribute, relation, or role comes from gist, a domain ontology, live sandbox schema, or the current proposal.

## Current Code
`LingoExplorerRowView` colors icons through `OntologyTypePalette`. Detail views use colors based on the selected type domain, for example `LingoEntityDetailView.entityColor` and relation/attribute equivalents. Parent links like `sub <parent>` are colored with the current selected type color, not necessarily the ontology/domain that defines the referenced parent.

## Design
Add a lookup on `OntologyViewModel` that resolves a type name to its defining domain/ontology across proposal and live schema collections. It should distinguish proposal-domain definitions from live package definitions and prefer exact live definitions for external parents not declared in the proposal. Use existing `currentDomains`, parsed schema `domain`, and `OntologyTypePalette` to convert that defining domain to a color.

Apply the lookup to displayed type reference text in browser detail views:
- Entity parent links such as `sub Thing` should color `Thing` by the ontology/domain defining `Thing`.
- Relation parent links, role player type links, owned attribute links, and attribute parent links should use the referenced type's defining ontology color.
- Row labels in the sidebar can continue using kind/domain palette, but type references inside detail content should communicate the referenced ontology.

If a type cannot be resolved, fall back to the selected type's current color and expose no noisy UI warning.

## Tests / Verification
Add unit tests for the resolver: proposal-defined type, live gist-defined parent, live domain-defined type, duplicate proposal/live name precedence, and unresolved fallback. Manual verification: for a proposal containing `sub Thing`, the displayed `Thing` reference uses the gist/domain color while the proposed child uses the proposal color.
acceptance_criteria:
- A view-model helper resolves a type name to the ontology/domain where it is defined.
- Browser detail links color referenced type text by the referenced type's defining ontology/domain, not by the currently selected type.
- `sub Thing` displays `Thing` using the gist-associated color when `Thing` is defined in gist/live schema.
- Proposal-defined types still use the proposal-domain color.
- Tests cover live, proposal, duplicate, and unresolved type resolution.
close_reason: Added defining-domain resolution and applied ontology-domain coloring to type references in Lingo Browser detail views with resolver coverage.

title: Remove proposal revision and summary card from Lingo Browser sidebar
description: The Lingo Browser sidebar currently includes a proposal banner row with revision, status, and summary text. Remove that entire sidebar element so the sidebar focuses on navigable schema structure.
design:
## User Impact
The sidebar banner consumes high-value navigation space with metadata that is already available elsewhere. As proposals grow, the browser sidebar should remain a compact type tree, not a mixed metadata and navigation surface.

## Current Code
`visibleLingoExplorerRows` in `OneApps/Ontology/ViewModels/OntologyViewModel+LingoExplorer.swift` prepends `.proposalBanner(proposal)` rows for each proposal. `LingoExplorerRowView` has a `proposalBanner(_:)` rendering path showing `rev`, summary, and status/review badges. This is the UI element to remove.

## Design
Stop adding proposal banner rows to `visibleLingoExplorerRows`. Remove or deprecate the `.proposalBanner` render path if no other UI uses it. If the enum case is still useful for proposal overview selection, keep the model case but do not surface it in the sidebar.

Proposal metadata should move to the browser detail header or overview area only when no type is selected. The sidebar should start with the Proposal domain and live ontology domains/sections. Selection behavior should continue to choose the first proposal type via `selectFirstLingoProposalType()`.

Update previews in `LingoExplorerRowView` and `LingoExplorerView` so they no longer showcase a proposal banner as a sidebar row.

## Tests / Verification
Add or update a view-model test for `visibleLingoExplorerRows` asserting no `.proposalBanner` node is returned. Manual verification: opening the Lingo Browser shows domain/type rows only in the sidebar, with no revision/summary card at the top.
acceptance_criteria:
- `visibleLingoExplorerRows` no longer inserts proposal revision/summary banner rows.
- Lingo Browser sidebar contains only navigable domain, section, and type rows.
- Existing proposal selection/open behavior still selects the first proposal type when the browser opens.
- Previews/tests no longer rely on `.proposalBanner` sidebar rendering.
- Proposal metadata remains available outside the sidebar where appropriate.
close_reason: Removed proposal banner rows from the Lingo Browser sidebar and updated tests/previews around schema-only navigation.

title: Show inheritance, attributes, roles, and relations for proposed types in Lingo Browser detail
description: The Lingo Browser detail area should expose the same structural facts for proposed schema types that it exposes for live types, including inheritance, owned attributes, roles, played roles, relations, and related documentation.
design:
## User Impact
Users reviewing a proposal need to understand what each proposed type inherits, owns, relates, and plays before applying schema changes. If detail panels omit those facts for proposed types, users must read raw TypeQL or guess from the tree, which is error-prone.

## Current Code
Explorer detail views already exist: `LingoEntityDetailView`, `LingoRelationDetailView`, and `LingoAttributeDetailView`. They call view-model helpers such as `lingoAncestors`, `lingoChildren`, `lingoInheritedOwns`, `lingoInheritedPlayedRoles`, and `lingoInheritedRoles`. Proposed types come from `proposalLingoEntities`, `proposalLingoRelations`, and `proposalLingoAttributes`, derived through `currentProposalSchemaModel` and `SchemaModel+ParsedSchema.swift`.

The likely failure point is the proposal parsing/model conversion path or missing parent/domain linkage: proposed rows may not carry enough `declaredOwns`, `declaredPlays`, `declaredRelates`, supertype, role player, or annotation data for the detail helpers to render sections.

## Design
Audit proposal TypeQL parsing into `EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart.schemaModel` and the `SchemaModel+ParsedSchema` conversion layer. Ensure proposed entities preserve:
- `supertype` / parent entity.
- `declaredOwns` with cardinality annotations.
- `declaredPlays` role references.
- documentation annotations.

Ensure proposed relations preserve:
- parent relation.
- declared roles, overridden roles, and role player type information where available.
- owned attributes and annotations.

Ensure proposed attributes preserve:
- parent attribute.
- value type and annotations.

Update detail views if they are filtering out proposal-domain data unintentionally. Cross-domain links from proposal types to live gist/base types should navigate to the live type when the parent is not present in the proposal domain. The detail panel should prefer structured sections over raw TypeQL for review.

## Tests / Verification
Add tests with a proposal TypeQL fixture containing an entity subtype, owned attribute, played role, relation with roles, relation owns, and attribute subtype/value. Assert that the generated Lingo schema models and detail helper outputs include inheritance, owns, plays, roles, and owners for proposal-domain selections. Manual verification: open a proposal and select an entity/relation/attribute; structural sections appear without requiring the raw TypeQL pop-up.
acceptance_criteria:
- Proposed entity detail shows inheritance, owned attributes, played roles, children/parents, and documentation when present.
- Proposed relation detail shows inheritance, roles, owned attributes, role players where available, and documentation when present.
- Proposed attribute detail shows inheritance, value type, owning entities/relations, and documentation when present.
- Cross-domain parent links from proposal to live ontology types navigate correctly.
- Tests cover a proposal fixture with inheritance, owns, plays, relation roles, and attribute value/subtyping.
close_reason: Exposed proposed type inheritance, owns, roles, relation players, attribute parents, and documentation through browser detail helpers and tests.

title: Move pending proposal TypeQL into a read-only inspector pop-up
description: The inspector overview currently embeds proposed TypeQL inline under Pending proposal. Replace the inline code block with a pop-up/sheet that shows selectable, non-editable proposal text for large proposals.
design:
## User Impact
Large TypeQL proposals will overwhelm the inspector overview. Inline code consumes vertical space, makes other inspector state harder to scan, and will not scale when proposals contain many types or functions.

## Current Code
`LingoInspectorOverviewView` in `OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo/LingoRootView.swift` renders `snapshot.pendingProposalTypeQL` directly as a monospaced `Text` with `.textSelection(.enabled)`, `.lineLimit(16)`, and a tinted background inside the `Pending proposal` section.

## Design
Remove the inline TypeQL block from the overview. Keep the proposal summary, then add a compact `View TypeQL` or `View Proposed Schema` button with a document/code icon. The action presents a popover or sheet from the inspector. The pop-up content should contain:
- Title: Proposed Schema or Proposal TypeQL.
- Read-only selectable monospaced text with the full `pendingProposalTypeQL`.
- Optional copy button using `NSPasteboard`, matching existing copy affordances.
- Close button or standard popover dismissal.

The text must be selectable but not editable. A SwiftUI `Text` in a `ScrollView` with `.textSelection(.enabled)` is acceptable; if using AppKit for better large-text performance, wrap `NSTextView` with `isEditable = false`, `isSelectable = true`, and theme-aware colors.

Do not remove proposal summary or the ability to inspect/copy TypeQL elsewhere. This change is only about moving the large raw payload out of the always-visible overview.

## Tests / Verification
Add UI state preview for inspector with a very long proposal. If an AppKit read-only text component is introduced, add a focused test or documented preview verifying non-editable/selectable configuration. Manual verification: inspector overview remains compact, the button opens the full proposal, the text can be selected/copied, and it cannot be edited.
acceptance_criteria:
- `LingoInspectorOverviewView` no longer renders full TypeQL inline under Pending proposal.
- A button opens a pop-up/sheet displaying the full proposed schema/TypeQL.
- Pop-up text is selectable and read-only/non-editable.
- Very large proposal text scrolls inside the pop-up without resizing the inspector overview.
- Existing copy/review workflows for TypeQL remain available.
close_reason: Moved pending proposal TypeQL out of the inspector overview into a read-only selectable popover with copy support.

title: Make Lingo intents and proposal documentation visible in inspector and browser
description: The inspector Intents tab is often empty, proposal types lack useful documentation, and the Lingo Browser does not expose docs consistently. Investigate the intent write/read flow and wire documentation into proposal review surfaces.
design:
## User Impact
The inspector has an Intents tab that appears to promise a history of modeling decisions, but users see nothing there. Proposal types also often show generic fallback text instead of meaningful documentation. This undermines trust because users cannot tell why a proposed type exists, what decision created it, or how it should be interpreted in the browser.

## Current Code
`IntentTimelineView` reads `viewModel.intentLog` and `viewModel.intentGroups`. `LingoInspectorSnapshot.intentCount` is derived from `intentLog.count`. Proposal application writes `ChangeIntentRecord` in `OntologyViewModel+Lingo.swift`, but pre-apply proposals may only carry `proposal.changeIntents`. `LingoTypeEditorModel` synthesizes fallback documentation for proposal rows, while explorer detail views try `annotations["doc"]` and `viewModel.typeDoc(for:)`.

## Design
First determine the intended lifecycle:
- Pre-apply proposal intent metadata should be visible as pending/proposed intents even before a schema write.
- Applied schema changes should appear as committed intent history from `intentLog`.
- Missing documentation should be surfaced as a real missing-doc state, not hidden behind vague generated text.

Implementation should add a presentation adapter that merges pending `EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart.changeIntents` with persisted `ChangeIntentRecord` entries for inspector display. Pending entries should be visually distinct and should not be written as committed intent records until apply.

For documentation, map proposal docs from TypeQL annotations and/or proposal metadata into `LingoSchemaEntity`, `LingoSchemaRelation`, and `LingoSchemaAttribute` detail sections. When no doc exists, show a concise missing-doc message and include that gap in the proposal review surface so users know documentation needs to be added before applying. The Lingo Browser detail views should expose docs for proposal and live types consistently.

Add tests around the adapter: no intents, pending-only proposal intents, committed-only intents, and mixed pending/committed history. Include a fixture where proposal type docs are present and absent.
acceptance_criteria:
- The Intents tab shows pending proposal intents from the active proposal before apply.
- The Intents tab still shows committed `ChangeIntentRecord` history after apply.
- Pending and committed intents are visually distinguishable.
- Lingo Browser detail views show proposal/live type documentation when available.
- Missing proposal documentation is visible as an explicit review gap instead of only generic filler text.
- Tests cover pending-only, committed-only, mixed, and no-intent states.
close_reason: Merged pending proposal intents with committed intent history, surfaced pending state, and made documentation/missing-doc states visible in browser detail surfaces.

title: Use transparent backgrounds for non-user Lingo chat messages
description: Only user-authored chat input should render with a colored message background. Assistant, tool, status, and error rows should sit on the transcript background with theme-aware text.
design:
## User Impact
`LingoChatTranscriptRow` currently assigns a colored fill to every message kind: blue for users, purple for assistant messages, orange for tools, red for errors, and gray for status. This makes the transcript visually noisy and causes non-user content to look like equal-weight bubbles instead of system output. In light theme it also risks low contrast if system foreground defaults interact poorly with tinted backgrounds.

## Current Code
`OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo/LingoChatView.swift` defines `LingoChatTranscriptRow.backgroundColor` and applies `.background(backgroundColor)` plus rounded clipping to every row. Assistant markdown uses `LingoAssistantMessageText`; non-assistant rows use plain `Text`.

## Design
Change `LingoChatTranscriptRow` so only `.user` rows receive the colored bubble/background. Non-user rows should have `Color.clear` background and no bubble-like clip unless a child widget intentionally has its own card surface. Use GammaTheme text tokens so regular transcript text is `theme.primaryText`, metadata/timestamps are `theme.secondaryText`, and muted helper text is `theme.tertiaryText`.

For error rows, preserve urgency through icon/status color and optional leading accent, not a filled red background. For tool/status rows, preserve scanability through icon color, monospaced text where currently used, and spacing. Keep user row max width and trailing alignment as-is so user input remains visually distinct.

## Tests / Verification
If the row background logic is extracted into a pure helper, add tests asserting `.user` is the only filled row kind. Otherwise add/update previews for transcript rows in light and dark theme. Manual verification: send user, assistant, tool, status, and error transcript items; only the user message has a colored bubble while all other text remains readable in both themes.
acceptance_criteria:
- In `LingoChatTranscriptRow`, `.user` is the only message kind with a colored filled background.
- Assistant, tool, status, and error rows render on transparent transcript background with theme-aware primary text.
- Error/tool/status rows still communicate state through icons or accent text without full-row colored fill.
- Light theme uses dark text for non-user rows; VibeMachine theme uses light text for non-user rows.
- A focused test or preview verifies all transcript item kinds.
close_reason: Restricted filled transcript backgrounds to user messages and moved non-user rows to theme-aware transparent rendering; added row presentation coverage.

title: Add chat-panel control to open the Lingo Browser
description: The Lingo Browser/Explorer can be opened from proposal cards or programmatic flows, but the chat panel needs an always-visible button that opens or displays it when a proposal exists.
design:
## User Impact
Users can miss the Lingo Browser because it appears only after proposal-specific interactions. That makes structured review feel hidden and pushes users back into the transcript, which is a poor surface for navigating schema proposals.

## Current Code
`LingoChatView` renders a header with font-size controls and conditionally displays `LingoExplorerView` when `viewModel.isLingoExplorerPresented` and `viewModel.currentLingoProposal != nil`. `OntologyViewModel+LingoExplorer.swift` already exposes `openLingoExplorer()` and `closeLingoExplorer()`.

## Design
Add a compact icon button to the `LingoChatView.header` near the existing transcript controls. Use a browser/explorer-appropriate SF Symbol such as `sidebar.left` or `rectangle.split.2x1`, with help text like `Show Lingo Browser`. The button should call `viewModel.openLingoExplorer()` when a current proposal exists, and toggle close/minimize if the browser is already visible.

Disabled state: if `viewModel.currentLingoProposal == nil`, disable the button and use help text that explains a schema proposal is needed first. Avoid visible instructional copy in the main UI.

The button should not replace the proposal-card `Open in Lingo Explorer` action; both should route to the same view model method. The browser should remain embedded in the chat panel below the transcript as it does today.

## Tests / Verification
Add a view-model-level test if a toggle helper is introduced. Otherwise add preview states for no proposal, hidden browser with proposal, and visible browser. Manual verification: after generating a proposal, clicking the header button opens the browser; clicking it again minimizes or hides it; before a proposal exists, the disabled state is clear via tooltip/help.
acceptance_criteria:
- `LingoChatView` header includes a button that opens/displays the Lingo Browser when a current proposal exists.
- The button uses existing `openLingoExplorer()` / close behavior rather than duplicating browser state logic.
- The button is disabled when no proposal exists and has appropriate help text.
- Existing proposal-card browser action still works.
- Browser visibility can be manually toggled from the chat panel without sending a chat message.
close_reason: Added chat header toggle for the Lingo Browser with proposal-aware disabled state and view-model toggle coverage.

title: Make Lingo views consume GammaCore themes
description: Lingo currently mixes hard-coded SwiftUI colors with the host theme. Adopt GammaCore's theme facility across the Lingo chat, inspector, browser, composer-adjacent widgets, and proposal cards so light and dark themes render consistently.
design:
## User Impact
When the app switches from the default dark VibeMachine theme to the light theme, Lingo still contains many hard-coded colors and system defaults. The result is inconsistent contrast, status colors that do not match the shell, and surfaces that can look visually detached from the rest of OneApp.

## Existing Facilities
GammaCore already exposes `GammaTheme` in `OneApp/GammaCore/Theme/GammaTheme.swift`, `ThemeName`, `EnvironmentValues.gammaTheme` in `OneApp/GammaCore/Theme/ThemeKey.swift`, and `.gammaPaneBackground()`. `OneApp/OneApp/OneAppApp.swift` injects the resolved theme at the app root. Settings writes `ui.theme` through `OneApp/OneApp/Views/Settings/OneSettingsView.swift`.

## Design
Add `@Environment(\.gammaTheme) private var theme` to Lingo views that render durable surfaces or semantic colors, especially `OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo/LingoChatView.swift`, `LingoRootView.swift`, `IntentTimelineView.swift`, `LingoToolTraceCard.swift`, `CandidateSchemaView.swift`, `SandboxSelectorView.swift`, and explorer views under `OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo/Explorer/`.

Replace hard-coded neutral colors with semantic theme tokens:
- Page/pane backgrounds use `.gammaPaneBackground()` or `theme.solidBackground`/`theme.background` as appropriate.
- Text uses `theme.primaryText`, `theme.secondaryText`, or `theme.tertiaryText` instead of `.primary`, `.secondary`, and `.tertiary` where contrast must be explicit.
- Card borders and neutral fills use `theme.cardBorder`, `theme.surfaceCard`, `theme.surfaceHover`, or `theme.badgeBackground`.
- Status colors use `theme.success`, `theme.warning`, `theme.error`, and `theme.accent` where the meaning is application status rather than ontology identity.

Keep ontology/domain colors delegated to `OntologyTypePalette` so ontology provenance remains separate from host theme. Do not create a parallel Lingo theme struct.

## Tests / Verification
Add focused Swift tests where a pure helper is introduced for color/style mapping. For view-only changes, add or update previews with both `.environment(\.gammaTheme, .vibemachine)` and `.environment(\.gammaTheme, .light)` for the changed Lingo root/browser surfaces. Manual verification should switch Appearance in Settings and confirm Lingo remains readable in both themes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lingo root, chat transcript rows, inspector sections, browser/explorer surfaces, intent rows, tool trace cards, and proposal cards read `@Environment(\.gammaTheme)` or inherit it cleanly.
- Hard-coded neutral foreground/background colors in Lingo are replaced with GammaTheme tokens where contrast/readability depends on theme.
- Existing ontology/domain colors continue to use `OntologyTypePalette`.
- Light theme shows black/dark primary text on light surfaces; VibeMachine theme shows white/light primary text on dark surfaces.
- Relevant Lingo previews or tests cover both `.vibemachine` and `.light` theme injection.
close_reason: Implemented GammaCore theme adoption across Lingo chat, inspector, browser, timeline, tool trace, candidate schema, and sandbox selector surfaces; added explicit light and VibeMachine preview coverage.

title: Lingo UI theme and proposal browser polish
description: Organize follow-up work from the Lingo UI review: theme adoption, chat readability, proposal browser access, inspector scalability, intent/documentation visibility, and ontology-aware type coloring.
design:
## UX Problem
Lingo has the right core workflow for schema proposal review, but several surfaces still behave like prototype UI: hard-coded colors, colored chat backgrounds for every system message, a hidden browser affordance, inline TypeQL that cannot scale, empty intent surfaces, sidebar proposal metadata noise, incomplete proposal detail rendering, and type labels that do not communicate ontology provenance.

## Design Direction
Treat Lingo as a theme-aware ontology workbench. Chat should emphasize conversational content and reserve colored fill only for user-authored input. The Lingo Browser/Explorer should be discoverable from chat, focused on navigable schema structure rather than proposal metadata cards, and able to show documentation, inheritance, attributes, relations, roles, and provenance for both live and proposed types. Large proposal TypeQL should move into a read-only selectable pop-up. Intent and documentation surfaces should become meaningful review aids instead of empty placeholders.

## Boundaries
Implementation work should stay under OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo, OneApps/Ontology/ViewModels, OneApps/Ontology/Models, and OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests unless a shared GammaCore theme helper is required. GammaCore already provides GammaTheme, ThemeName, the gammaTheme environment key, and gammaPaneBackground; Lingo should consume those instead of introducing a separate theme system.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each reviewed bullet has a child bead with user impact, implementation design, and testable acceptance criteria.
- Child beads reference the relevant Lingo/GammaCore files and use GammaTheme/GammaCore terminology where applicable.
- Dependency ordering captures work that depends on theme adoption before theme-sensitive visual fixes.
close_reason: Implemented and verified all child tasks/bugs one-ovq.11.1 through one-ovq.11.8; focused Lingo tests, Ontology build, and full Ontology suite pass.

title: Lingo should clean up unused development sandboxes
description: The transcript created knowledge-sandbox-4ed5a744-de47-4867-beab-3a9eec9c6d31 and never dropped it. Lingo sessions can leave disposable development databases behind.
design: Define and implement a Lingo sandbox lifecycle policy. At minimum, expose deterministic cleanup for abandoned or failed proposal sandboxes and record the cleanup in the transcript/diagnostic log. The policy must not drop sandboxes with accepted/applied work or user-selected sandboxes without explicit confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: A focused test covers an unused Lingo-created sandbox becoming eligible for cleanup and verifies drop_sandbox or equivalent cleanup removes it. A second test verifies a sandbox with accepted/applied work is not dropped automatically. Diagnostic transcript records cleanup decisions.
close_reason: Implemented cleanup_unused_sandboxes with transcript reporting; inactive development sandboxes are removed and active/applied sandboxes are skipped by default.

title: Enrich core ontology slices with scoped concept documentation
description: Add a semantic documentation overlay to CoreOntologySlice so synthesis agents receive bounded concept docs for labels already in scope, especially rich GIST definitions and modeling guidance.
design:
CoreOntologySlice is intentionally structural in one-2xg.38.4.12: it is pure over SchemaModel + CQ refs and does not do I/O. Before SchemaGenerator/Judge prompts rely on the slice heavily, add a separate semantic overlay keyed by TypeLabel.

Recommended shape:
- TypeDocumentationRef: label, summary, definition, examples, synonyms, modelingNotes, sourcePackage/sourceFile.
- CoreOntologySliceSemanticOverlay or an optional [TypeLabel: TypeDocumentationRef] input to rendering.
- Keep selection bounded: include docs only for labels in slice.scopeLabels and gistAnchors.gistRoot/immediateSubtypes. Never dump the full docs corpus.
- Source docs from existing ontology memory/package documentation services in the workflow layer, not inside SchemaModel. SchemaModel may continue to expose only schema-native @doc annotations.
- renderForGenerator() or a sibling renderer should add a section such as '== Semantic documentation in scope ==' after structural types.

This should be implemented before or alongside SchemaGeneratorAgent prompt integration so generation/judging can distinguish GIST semantics such as part/member, activity/event, category/type, etc.
acceptance_criteria:
- Slice prompt rendering can include bounded semantic docs for scoped labels and GIST anchors.
- SchemaModel remains structural; rich docs are passed as an overlay, not stored inside SchemaModel.
- Overlay selection is deterministic and capped.
- Tests prove unrelated docs are excluded and scoped docs appear in stable order.
- SchemaGeneratorAgent/JudgeStep designs or prompts are updated to consume the semantic-doc section.
close_reason: Added CoreOntologySliceSemanticOverlay and TypeDocumentationRef as a pure, bounded semantic documentation layer over structural slices. Overlay selection is deterministic over slice scope labels plus GIST anchor labels, renderForGenerator(documentationOverlay:) emits a Semantic documentation section, and tests prove unrelated docs are excluded while scoped docs render in stable order. Added notes to SchemaGenerator and Judge beads so their prompt/context assembly consumes the semantic-doc section.

title: Integrate Lingo transcript segment rendering
description: Wire accepted Lingo transcript segments and action surfaces into LingoChatView/Lingo message rows.
design:
Modify existing file: `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/ChatMessageView.swift`.

Changes:

1. Replace the current single `Text(message.content)` body with a per-segment renderer. Compute:
   ```swift
   let segments = ChatTranscriptContentClassifier.segments(from: message.content)
   ```
   For each segment render the appropriate view:
   - `.plainText(let s)` -> `Text(s)`
   - `.codeBlock(let lang, let body)` -> `CodeBlockAttachmentView(language: lang, body: body)`
   - `.markdownTable(let headers, let rows)` -> `MarkdownTableAttachmentView(headers: headers, rows: rows)`

   Stack the segment views in a leading-aligned `VStack`.

2. Wrap the segment list in `CollapsibleContentAttachmentView`. Estimate line count as `message.content.split(separator: "\n").count` (or equivalent newline-count based estimate) and pass it as `lineCount`:
   ```swift
   CollapsibleContentAttachmentView(lineCount: lineCount) {
     VStack(alignment: .leading) { /* segment views */ }
   }
   ```

3. Below the body, when `message.role == .assistant` (or whatever the assistant case is named on `ChatMessage`), render `ResultActionAttachmentView(messageBody: message.content)`. User-message branch does NOT render the result-action row.

Depends on tasks 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 — this task is the integration that consumes their output.
acceptance_criteria: Lingo transcript renders prose, TypeQL/code, diagnostics, and proposal actions coherently with focused tests and Ontology build pass.

title: Collapsible Lingo diagnostics and tool payloads
description: Collapse long validation errors, tool payloads, or diagnostic blocks in the Lingo transcript while preserving copy/access to the full content.
design:
File: `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Transcript/CollapsibleContentAttachmentView.swift`

SwiftUI View wrapping arbitrary content via `@ViewBuilder`. Stored properties:
- `let lineCount: Int` (estimated by caller, typically `body.split(separator: "\n").count`)
- `@ViewBuilder content: () -> Content` (generic over `Content: View`)

Local state:
- `@State private var isExpanded: Bool = false`

Behavior:
- If `lineCount <= 30`: render `content()` directly with no wrapper UI.
- If `lineCount > 30`:
  - When `isExpanded == false`: wrap `content()` in a clipped frame approximately 8 lines tall (e.g. fixed height around 8 * line height, or a `.frame(maxHeight:)` clipping). Below the clipped frame render a `Button("Show more") { isExpanded = true }`.
  - When `isExpanded == true`: render `content()` unbounded with a `Button("Show less") { isExpanded = false }` beneath.

Buttons should use `.buttonStyle(.borderless)` for a subtle inline appearance.
acceptance_criteria: Long diagnostics show a concise preview with show more/less and copy/full-content access.

title: LingoMentionPickerPopover for ontology context references
description: Build the @ mention popover for Lingo context references such as proposals, packages/types, sandboxes, transcripts, and supported files.
design:
Two file deltas:

## 1. Extend `FakeComposerPickerData.swift` (from F4)

Add a new option type and a static fake list with 8–12 plausible entries:

```swift
struct FileMentionOption: ComposerPickerOption, Identifiable {
    let id: String                  // stable, e.g. path + filename
    let title: String               // filename
    let subtitle: String            // directory path
    let systemImage: String         // "doc.text"
}

extension FakeComposerPickerData {
    static let mentionFiles: [FileMentionOption] = [
        FileMentionOption(id: "OneApp/OneApp/Views/ContentView.swift",
                          title: "ContentView.swift",
                          subtitle: "OneApp/OneApp/Views/",
                          systemImage: "doc.text"),
        FileMentionOption(id: "OneApps/VibeMachine/.../DesignChatSession.swift",
                          title: "DesignChatSession.swift",
                          subtitle: "OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/",
                          systemImage: "doc.text"),
        FileMentionOption(id: "OneApps/VibeMachine/.../ChatPanelView.swift",
                          title: "ChatPanelView.swift",
                          subtitle: "OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/",
                          systemImage: "doc.text"),
        // ... 5–9 additional plausible entries spanning OneApp/, OneApps/VibeMachine/, LocalPackages/, Vendor/.
    ]
}
```

Aim for 8–12 total entries; mix filenames so filter tests have substring overlap (e.g. multiple `*View.swift` files).

`FileMentionOption` MUST conform to F4's `ComposerPickerOption`.

## 2. New file `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/Pickers/FileMentionPickerPopover.swift`

```swift
import SwiftUI

struct FileMentionPickerPopover: View {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    let query: String
    let triggerRange: NSRange         // from MentionTrigger.mention(query:range:)
    let coordinator: PromptTextViewCoordinator

    var body: some View {
        ComposerPickerPopover<FileMentionOption>(
            options: filtered,
            emptyStateText: "No files found",
            onSelect: { option in
                insert(option)
                isPresented = false
            }
        )
    }

    private var filtered: [FileMentionOption] { ... }
    private func insert(_ option: FileMentionOption) { ... }
}
```

## Filter logic
- If `query.isEmpty`, return the full list.
- Otherwise filter on case-insensitive substring against `title` (filename) and `subtitle` (directory path).
- Empty filtered set renders the empty-state row.

## Selection write-back
On `onSelect`:
1. Call coordinator to replace text in `triggerRange` with `"@\(option.title)"` (e.g. `"@ContentView.swift"`).
2. Update `selectedRange` to sit immediately after the inserted token.
3. Set `isPresented = false`.

Use the same coordinator helper introduced in F5 task 3 (`replace(range:with:)`).

## Esc dismissal
Esc dismissal is the SwiftUI popover default — when the popover loses focus, `isPresented` flips to `false` and the caller's `MentionTriggerObserver`-derived binding resets `trigger` to `.none`. No special insertion happens on dismiss.

## Caller integration
`ChatComposerView` presents this in `.popover(isPresented: mentionPresented, attachmentAnchor: .rect(.bounds), arrowEdge: .bottom) { FileMentionPickerPopover(isPresented: mentionPresented, query: extractedQuery, triggerRange: extractedRange, coordinator: coordinator) }`. The `extractedRange` comes from the `.mention(query:range:)` payload on the observer.
acceptance_criteria: Mention rows are Lingo-specific, filtering works, empty state is clear, and selecting a mention replaces the @ token with the selected reference.
close_reason: Added Lingo mention option model and @ context picker with token replacement

title: Evaluate whether Lingo needs markdown table rendering

design:
File: `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Transcript/MarkdownTableAttachmentView.swift`

SwiftUI View accepting:
- `let headers: [String]`
- `let rows: [[String]]`

Render via `Grid` (or `LazyVGrid` if simpler) with bordered cells. Each cell:

title: Responsive toolbar collapse with displayMode breakpoints (full / compact / tight)
design:
Inside OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/ChatComposerToolbar.swift, add a private enum DisplayMode { case full, compact, tight } plus a helper that maps a measured width to a DisplayMode using:
- width >= 320 -> .full
- 240 <= width < 320 -> .compact
- width < 240 -> .tight

Measure the toolbar's available width using either GeometryReader or .onGeometryChange(for: CGSize.self) { ... } and stash the measured width in @State, derive displayMode from it.

Visibility rules:
- .full: all nine slots visible inline.
- .compact: Model picker and Reasoning Effort picker collapse into an overflow Menu (use ChatComposerMenuButton). Send, Accept Edits, Share Active Doc, Apply Last Reply, Add Context, Tools, Operating Mode remain inline.
- .tight: Share Active Doc, Apply Last Reply, Add Context, Tools, Operating Mode picker also collapse into the overflow Menu. Only Send and Accept Edits remain inline.

The overflow Menu lists the collapsed items with their titles and (for picker-backed entries) the current selection as a trailing checkmark or subtitle. Tapping a collapsed picker entry opens its popover via the same ComposerPickerButton path (or a Menu of the dataset directly — implementer's choice; document the choice in the file header).
acceptance_criteria:
- ChatComposerToolbar declares a private DisplayMode enum with cases .full, .compact, .tight and computes it from measured width using the documented breakpoints (>=320, 240-319, <240).

title: Lingo transcript content classifier
description: Pure classifier for Lingo transcript segments: prose, TypeQL/code block, TypeDB error, tool trace, proposal reference, and long diagnostic content.
design:
File: `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Transcript/ChatTranscriptContentClassifier.swift`

Pure-logic content classifier that splits a chat message body into ordered segments. No SwiftUI, no I/O — must be unit-testable in isolation.

```swift
enum TranscriptSegment: Equatable {
  case plainText(String)
  case codeBlock(language: String?, body: String)
  case markdownTable(headers: [String], rows: [[String]])
}

enum ChatTranscriptContentClassifier {
  static func segments(from message: String) -> [TranscriptSegment]
}
```

Detection rules:
- Triple-backtick fences ``` open/close a `.codeBlock`. The opening fence may carry an optional language identifier on the same line (e.g. ```swift). Body is the verbatim content between fences (newline trimmed at edges only).
- Pipe-table syntax: a sequence of lines starting and ending with `|`, where the second line is a header separator row composed of dashes (e.g. `|---|---|`). The first line is the header row, subsequent rows are body rows. Cells are split on `|` and trimmed.
- Anything else collapses into a `.plainText` segment containing the verbatim text (preserve newlines).

The function is the single integration point used by `ChatMessageView` (task 7) to render rich segments.
acceptance_criteria: Classifier tests cover Lingo segment types and ignore unsupported generic transcript widgets.

## 2. New file `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/Pickers/SlashCommandsPickerPopover.swift`

```swift
import SwiftUI

struct SlashCommandsPickerPopover: View {
    @Binding var isPresented: Bool
    let query: String
    let coordinator: PromptTextViewCoordinator

    var body: some View {
        ComposerPickerPopover<SlashCommandOption>(
            options: filtered,
            emptyStateText: "No commands found",
            onSelect: { option in
                insert(option)
                isPresented = false
            }
        )
    }

    private var filtered: [SlashCommandOption] { ... }
    private func insert(_ option: SlashCommandOption) { ... }
}
```

## Filter logic
- If `query.isEmpty`, return the full list.
- Otherwise return options whose `title` OR `subtitle` contains `query` (case-insensitive substring, e.g. `localizedCaseInsensitiveContains`).
- If filtered set is empty, the wrapped `ComposerPickerPopover` shows the `emptyStateText` row ("No commands found"). (Reuses F4's empty-state row chrome.)

## Selection write-back
On `onSelect`:
1. Call into `coordinator` to mutate `currentText` and `selectedRange`:
   - Strip the leading `/<query>` token (the slash and everything up to the caret) from the text.
   - Insert the placeholder marker `[command: <option.title>]` at the caret position.
   - Update `selectedRange` to sit immediately after the inserted marker.
2. Set `isPresented = false` so the caller's `MentionTriggerObserver`-derived binding flips to `false` and resets `trigger` to `.none`.

The write-back goes through the same coordinator seam F2 introduced — do NOT poke `NSTextView` directly here. If a small `func replace(range: NSRange, with: String)` helper does not yet exist on `PromptTextViewCoordinator`, add it as part of this task.

## Caller integration
`ChatComposerView` instantiates this view inside its `.popover(isPresented: slashPresented, attachmentAnchor: .rect(.bounds), arrowEdge: .bottom) { SlashCommandsPickerPopover(isPresented: slashPresented, query: extractedQuery, coordinator: coordinator) }`.

title: Wire LingoMentionTriggerObserver to LingoPromptTextViewCoordinator
description: Observe LingoPromptTextViewCoordinator.currentText and selectedRange, publish the active LingoMentionTrigger, and expose enough state for Lingo composer popovers to present/dismiss.
design:
Add a new file `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/Pickers/MentionTriggerObserver.swift`. This is the Combine glue between F2's `PromptTextViewCoordinator` and the popovers from F5 tasks 3 and 4.

## Type shape
```swift
import Combine
import Foundation
import SwiftUI

@MainActor
final class MentionTriggerObserver: ObservableObject {
    @Published private(set) var trigger: MentionTrigger = .none

    init(coordinator: PromptTextViewCoordinator)
    deinit
}
```

## Behavior
- On `init`, subscribe (via `Combine`) to `coordinator.$currentText` and `coordinator.$selectedRange` (both already published by F2 — task 5 may need to nudge F2 to ensure they are `@Published`).
- Use `Publishers.CombineLatest` (or `MergeMany` then a manual recomputation closure) to recompute `MentionTrigger.detect(text: <currentText>, caretLocation: <selectedRange.location>)` on every change.
- Apply a `~50ms debounce` (`.debounce(for: .milliseconds(50), scheduler: DispatchQueue.main)`) to suppress per-keystroke flicker. The debounce window is small enough not to be perceptible but coalesces fast multi-char input.
- Assign the result to `self.trigger` on the main queue.
- Cancellables stored in a `private var cancellables = Set<AnyCancellable>()`.
- `deinit` lets the cancellables drop naturally.

## Owner / integration
- `ChatComposerView` (or a small helper view inside it) constructs the observer with its existing `PromptTextViewCoordinator` and stores it as `@StateObject`.
- The composer view derives two `Binding<Bool>` values from `observer.trigger`:
  - `slashPresented = trigger is .slash` → drives `SlashCommandsPickerPopover`.
  - `mentionPresented = trigger is .mention` → drives `FileMentionPickerPopover`.
- Each binding's setter, when set to `false` by the popover system (Esc / outside click), should reset `trigger` to `.none` (via a method `func dismiss()` on the observer or by writing `trigger = .none` directly through a small writable surface — pick whichever keeps the API tight).
- Popovers are anchored on the prompt editor with `.popover(isPresented: <binding>, attachmentAnchor: .rect(.bounds), arrowEdge: .bottom)`. Anchor is the prompt editor's bounds for v1; if narrow widths look bad, anchor to the composer shell instead.

## F2 dependency note
F5 task 2 assumes F2 (`one-ovq.2`) exposes `currentText: String` and `selectedRange: NSRange` as `@Published`. If F2's current implementation does not yet publish these, this task includes the small extension to do so. Do NOT change F2's other behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Observer updates on text and selection changes, clears when trigger boundaries break, and has focused tests without AppKit window dependencies.

title: PromptTextViewCoordinator unit tests for send predicate, newline modifiers, and reentrancy guard
design:
Create `OneApps/VibeMachine/VibeMachineTests/Chat/Composer/PromptTextViewCoordinatorTests.swift`.

## Framework
Swift Testing (`@Test` / `#expect`) — match existing VibeMachineTests style. No XCTest unless the surrounding test target is XCTest-only; in that case mirror sibling files in `VibeMachineTests/`.

## No mocks
Use a real `PromptTextViewCoordinator` instance. The pure-logic methods (`shouldSubmit`, `shouldInsertNewline`) take primitives and require no NSWindow, NSTextView, or run loop. The reentrancy test instantiates a real `NSTextView` and sets it as the coordinator's text view reference, then invokes `textDidChange(_:)` directly — still no mocks, just real AppKit.

## Test cases

### 1. shouldSubmit for `insertNewline:` selector
- Empty text → false (regardless of streaming/IME).
- Whitespace-only text → false (trimmed empty).
- Non-empty text + not streaming + not IME composing → true.
- Non-empty text + streaming → false.
- Non-empty text + IME composing → false.

### 2. shouldSubmit for `noop:` (Cmd-Return)
- Empty text → false (don't submit empty even on Cmd-Return).
- Non-empty text + streaming + IME composing → true (Cmd-Return forces through, per design "Cmd-Return always submits").
- Confirm Cmd-Return path is NOT gated by `isStreaming` or IME composition.

### 3. shouldSubmit for unknown selector
- Any other selector (e.g. `#selector(NSResponder.moveDown(_:))`) → false.

### 4. shouldInsertNewline modifiers
- `insertNewline:` + `.shift` → true.
- `insertNewline:` + `.option` → true.
- `insertNewline:` + `.shift.union(.option)` → true.
- `insertNewline:` + no modifiers → false.
- `insertNewline:` + `.command` → false (Cmd-Return is the submit path, not newline).
- Non-`insertNewline:` selector + any modifiers → false.

### 5. isUpdatingFromSwiftUI guard prevents binding feedback
- Construct a real `NSTextView` (no window required).
- Wire it as the coordinator's text view; install a closure on the coordinator that records calls (`var bindingUpdates: [String] = []` captured by `coordinator.onTextChange = { bindingUpdates.append($0) }`).
- Set `coordinator.isUpdatingFromSwiftUI = true`.
- Mutate `textView.string = "hello"`, then post `NSText.didChangeNotification` (or directly call `coordinator.textDidChange(Notification(name: NSText.didChangeNotification, object: textView))`).
- `#expect(bindingUpdates.isEmpty)`.
- Then set the guard to `false`, repeat the change, `#expect(bindingUpdates == ["hello"])`.

## Test target
Place under `OneApps/VibeMachine/VibeMachineTests/Chat/Composer/` (create directory). Add file membership to the VibeMachineTests target in `OneApps/VibeMachine/VibeMachine.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` if Xcode does not auto-add.

## Reference
- `testing-guidelines` skill (no-mocks policy, xcsift build flow).
acceptance_criteria:
- File `OneApps/VibeMachine/VibeMachineTests/Chat/Composer/PromptTextViewCoordinatorTests.swift` exists and is a member of the VibeMachineTests target.
- Tests cover `shouldSubmit` for the `insertNewline:` selector across the matrix: empty / whitespace / non-empty × streaming on/off × IME on/off (assertions match the predicate semantics in F2-task-2).

title: MentionTrigger pure-logic detection function
design:
Add a new file `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/Pickers/MentionTrigger.swift` containing a pure-logic enum and detection function used by the trigger observer (F5 task 2) and unit tests.

## Type shape
```swift
import Foundation

enum MentionTrigger: Equatable {
    case none
    case slash(query: String)
    case mention(query: String, range: NSRange)

    static func detect(text: String, caretLocation: Int) -> MentionTrigger
}
```

## Detection rules
- `.slash(query)` when `text` begins with `/` AND `caretLocation > 0`. The `query` is the substring from index 1 up to `caretLocation`. If the query contains a whitespace character, return `.none` (typing a space after `/` cancels the trigger).
- `.mention(query, range)` when the substring immediately preceding the caret matches the regex `(?:^|\s)@(\S*)`. The `query` is the captured group (everything after `@` up to the caret, no whitespace). The `range` (an `NSRange`) covers the entire `@<query>` token in the original `text` so the popover selection callback can replace it.
- `.none` otherwise.

## Implementation notes
- Pure function, no AppKit/SwiftUI imports. `Foundation` only.
- Use `NSRegularExpression` or manual scanning over `text.utf16` for caret-aligned bounds; choose whichever keeps the `NSRange` math precise.
- Guard against `caretLocation` outside `0...text.utf16.count`.
- Treat `text` empty / `caretLocation == 0` as `.none`.

## Pure-function seam
This file contains zero Combine, zero SwiftUI. F5 task 2 (`MentionTriggerObserver`) imports `MentionTrigger` and calls `MentionTrigger.detect(...)` from a Combine subscription on `PromptTextViewCoordinator.$currentText` and `$selectedRange`.

- `MentionTrigger.detect(text:caretLocation:)` is a `static func` with the exact signature above.
- File contains no SwiftUI or Combine imports — `Foundation` only.
- Unit tests exist (in the VibeMachine test target) covering at minimum:
  - leading-slash: `text = "/exp"`, caret at end → `.slash(query: "exp")`.
  - mid-prompt mention: `text = "hello @foo"`, caret at end → `.mention(query: "foo", range: <NSRange covering "@foo">)`.
  - mention-after-space: `text = "a @b"`, caret at end → `.mention(query: "b", ...)`.
  - mention-after-non-space: `text = "abc@foo"`, caret at end → `.none`.
  - space-after-slash: `text = "/foo bar"`, caret at end → `.none`.
  - backspace past trigger: `text = ""`, caret 0 → `.none`; `text = "/"`, caret 0 → `.none`.
- Tests pass via xcsift.

title: Classify pasted Lingo context
description: Add pure paste/context classification for Lingo prompt input: ordinary text, TypeDB error, TypeQL snippet, transcript path/excerpt, package/schema path, and oversized text.
design:
Extend the F2 (`one-ovq.2`) AppKit bridge so the composer can intercept and classify paste events without changing the bridge's text-editing semantics for normal paste. No file I/O, no real image decoding.

## Files (extending one-ovq.2)

### `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/PromptTextView.swift` (subclass of `NSTextView`)

Add ivar:

```swift
var pasteHandler: ((NSPasteboard) -> Bool)?
```

Override `paste(_:)`:

```swift
override func paste(_ sender: Any?) {
    let pb = NSPasteboard.general
    if pasteHandler?(pb) == true { return }
    super.paste(sender)
}
```

Override `readablePasteboardTypes` to extend the default text types with image + file URL:

```swift
override var readablePasteboardTypes: [NSPasteboard.PasteboardType] {
    super.readablePasteboardTypes + [.tiff, .png, .fileURL]
}
```

### `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/PromptTextViewCoordinator.swift`

Add nested `enum PasteOutcome { case insertPlain, snippet, image, file, ignore }` and a static threshold:

```swift
static let largePasteThreshold = 2000
```

Add a pure function (testable, no `NSPasteboard` argument):

```swift
func classifyPaste(types: Set<NSPasteboard.PasteboardType>, plainTextLength: Int) -> PasteOutcome
```

Decision rules (evaluated in order):
1. If `types` contains `.tiff` or `.png` → `.image`.
2. Else if `types` contains `.fileURL` → `.file`.
3. Else if `types` contains a string type AND `plainTextLength > 0`:
   - If `plainTextLength <= largePasteThreshold` → `.insertPlain`.
   - Else → `.snippet`.
4. Else → `.ignore`.

(Order matters when a pasteboard advertises multiple types — image/file beats string.)

### Composer shell wiring (`ChatComposerView` or its bridging container)

In the `updateNSView` (or equivalent) path of the bridge, set `pasteHandler` on the `PromptTextView` to a closure that:

1. Reads `pb.types` and the plain-text string (if any) from the pasteboard.
2. Calls `coordinator.classifyPaste(types: Set(types ?? []), plainTextLength: plainText?.count ?? 0)`.
3. Switches on the outcome and mutates the composer's `@State var attachments: [ComposerAttachment]`:
   - `.insertPlain` → return `false` (let `super.paste` run).
   - `.snippet` → append a `.textSnippet(title: nextSnippetTitle(in: attachments), charCount: plainText.count, body: plainText)` and return `true`.
   - `.image` → append `.image(thumbnailName: "photo")` and return `true`.
   - `.file` → for each `URL` decoded from `pb.readObjects(forClasses: [NSURL.self])`, append `.file(name: url.lastPathComponent, path: url.path, sizeString: "—")` and return `true`.
   - `.ignore` → return `false`.

The composer holds the `@State var attachments` itself; F3 task 3 renders the strip.

## Test hook

`classifyPaste` should be invocable from `OneApps/VibeMachine/VibeMachineTests/` with synthetic `Set<NSPasteboard.PasteboardType>` inputs to cover:

- 0-char + string types → `.ignore`
- 100-char string → `.insertPlain`
- 2000-char string (boundary) → `.insertPlain`
- 2001-char string → `.snippet`
- `.png` only → `.image`
- `.tiff` + string → `.image` (image wins)
- `.fileURL` only → `.file`
- empty set → `.ignore`
acceptance_criteria: Pure logic tests cover each context class and ordinary small text still inserts normally.

description: When a streamed reply is in progress and the composer's height changes (e.g. the user starts typing a follow-up while a reply is still arriving), re-run the existing scheduleScrollToBottom so the latest streamed token is never hidden behind a growing composer. title: PromptTextViewCoordinator with binding sync and keyboard semantics
design:
Create `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/PromptTextViewCoordinator.swift`.

## Type
`final class PromptTextViewCoordinator: NSObject, NSTextViewDelegate, ObservableObject`

## Stored / published properties
- `@Published var currentText: String = ""`
- `@Published var selectedRange: NSRange = NSRange(location: 0, length: 0)` (consumed by F5 slash/mention triggers later)
- `var isUpdatingFromSwiftUI: Bool = false` — reentrancy guard (set by representable's `updateNSView` before mutating `textView.string`, cleared after).
- Held closures injected by representable: `var onTextChange: ((String) -> Void)?`, `var onSubmit: (() -> Void)?`
- `var isStreamingProvider: (() -> Bool)?` — read-only accessor so the coordinator can ask the representable for the current `isStreaming` value at keypress time without storing stale state.

## Pure-logic decision seams (unit-testable, no NSWindow required)
```swift
func shouldSubmit(
    forSelector selector: Selector,
    currentText: String,
    isStreaming: Bool,
    isComposingIME: Bool
) -> Bool

func shouldInsertNewline(
    forSelector selector: Selector,
    modifierFlags: NSEvent.ModifierFlags
) -> Bool
```

### shouldSubmit semantics
- `selector == #selector(NSResponder.insertNewline(_:))`:
  return `!currentText.trimmed.isEmpty && !isStreaming && !isComposingIME`.
- `selector == #selector(NSResponder.noop(_:))` (Cmd-Return path — system maps Cmd-Return to noop:): return `true` regardless (force-submit even when empty/streaming guard is bypassed by user intent? — match design: Cmd-Return always submits when text is non-empty; for safety return `!currentText.trimmed.isEmpty`).
- All other selectors: `false`.

### shouldInsertNewline semantics
- `selector == #selector(NSResponder.insertNewline(_:))` AND
  `modifierFlags.contains(.shift) || modifierFlags.contains(.option)`:
  return `true`.
- Else: `false`.

## NSTextViewDelegate methods
- `textDidChange(_:)`:
  - If `isUpdatingFromSwiftUI` → return.
  - Read `textView.string`, assign to `currentText`, fire `onTextChange?(currentText)`.
  - Toggle placeholder visibility (placeholder NSTextField stored on the representable's coordinator-accessible context — see F2-task-3).
- `textViewDidChangeSelection(_:)`: capture `textView.selectedRange()` into `selectedRange`.
- `textView(_:doCommandBy:)`: implement keyboard routing:
  - Compute `isComposingIME = textView.hasMarkedText()`.
  - For `cancelOperation:` (Esc) → `textView.window?.makeFirstResponder(nil)`; return `true`.
  - For `insertNewline:` with Shift/Option (consult `NSApp.currentEvent?.modifierFlags ?? []` via `shouldInsertNewline`) → return `false` so default newline insertion runs.
  - For `noop:` (Cmd-Return) → if text non-empty, fire `onSubmit?()` and return `true`; else return `false`.
  - For `insertNewline:` plain → consult `shouldSubmit(forSelector:currentText:isStreaming:isComposingIME:)`; if true fire `onSubmit?()` and return `true`; else return `false`.
  - All other selectors: return `false`.

## Reference patterns
- `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Editor/DesignSourceEditorView.swift` — for the larger AppKit-bridge coordinator pattern (vendored CodeEditSourceEditorFork wrapping).

This file contains no `NSViewRepresentable`; that's task 3.
acceptance_criteria:
- File `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/PromptTextViewCoordinator.swift` exists with `final class PromptTextViewCoordinator: NSObject, NSTextViewDelegate, ObservableObject`.
- `@Published var currentText: String` and `@Published var selectedRange: NSRange` declared.
- `var isUpdatingFromSwiftUI: Bool` reentrancy guard exists; `textDidChange` early-returns when set.
- Pure-logic methods `shouldSubmit(forSelector:currentText:isStreaming:isComposingIME:)` and `shouldInsertNewline(forSelector:modifierFlags:)` exist with the signatures above and no UI-thread or NSWindow dependencies.
- `shouldSubmit` for `insertNewline:` returns true iff text non-empty, not streaming, not IME-composing.
- `shouldInsertNewline` returns true for `insertNewline:` selector when modifierFlags contain `.shift` or `.option`.
- `textView(_:doCommandBy:)` handles `cancelOperation:` (Esc → resign first responder), `noop:` (Cmd-Return submit when non-empty), `insertNewline:` (route through predicate, optionally invoking `onSubmit`).

title: PromptTextView NSTextView subclass with intrinsic content size
design:
Create `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/Composer/PromptTextView.swift`.

## Type
`final class PromptTextView: NSTextView` (Composer/ subdirectory is new — create it).

## Stored properties
- `var minHeight: CGFloat = 32`
- `var maxHeight: CGFloat = 120` (~5 lines)

## Override: intrinsicContentSize
Compute height from layout:
```
guard let layoutManager = layoutManager, let textContainer = textContainer else {
    return super.intrinsicContentSize
}
layoutManager.ensureLayout(for: textContainer)
let used = layoutManager.usedRect(for: textContainer)
let inset = textContainerInset
let rawHeight = ceil(used.height) + inset.height * 2
let clamped = min(max(rawHeight, minHeight), maxHeight)
return NSSize(width: NSView.noIntrinsicMetric, height: clamped)
```

## Override: didChangeText
```
override func didChangeText() {
    super.didChangeText()
    invalidateIntrinsicContentSize()
}
```

## Configuration defaults (set in init or via configure())
- `isRichText = false`
- `importsGraphics = false`
- `allowsUndo = true`
- `isAutomaticQuoteSubstitutionEnabled = false`
- `isAutomaticDashSubstitutionEnabled = false`
- `usesFindBar = false`
- `textContainerInset = NSSize(width: 4, height: 6)`
- `isVerticallyResizable = true`, `isHorizontallyResizable = false`
- `textContainer?.widthTracksTextView = true`

When height exceeds `maxHeight`, the enclosing NSScrollView (constructed in F2-task-3) handles internal scrolling — this view does NOT cap the text content itself, only its intrinsic size report.

## Reference patterns
- `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Components/VisualEffectView.swift` — minimal NSViewRepresentable shape (companion file).
- `OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Editor/DesignSourceEditorView.swift` — for the larger AppKit-bridge wrapping pattern (relevant in sibling tasks).

No coordinator wiring in this file — just the view subclass.
