title: Implement core ontology slice computation (pure function over SchemaModel)
description: Pure deterministic function that computes a focused subset of the schema for input to the Generator and Judge. No I/O. Bounded. Renders to multi-section LLM-input format.
design:
A pure deterministic function that computes a focused subset of the current schema for input to the Schema Generator and Judge. Same inputs → same output; no side effects; no I/O.

File: OneApps/Ontology/Schema/CoreOntologySlice.swift (new file in Schema/ alongside TypeQLParser.swift / SchemaContractValidator.swift)

Depends on: 38.1 — specifically 38.1.4 (inheritance resolver) so the slice can include inherited capabilities.

Types:

```swift
struct CoreOntologySlice: Sendable {
  let scopeLabels: Set<String>            // the labels included in the slice
  let types: [SchemaModelType]            // restricted to scopeLabels
  let functions: [FunctionDeclaration]    // those whose body references any scopeLabel
  let gistAnchors: [GistAnchorContext]    // gist roots reachable from scope, with one level of subtypes
  let nearbyCQs: [CompetencyQuestionRef]  // CQs whose nlForm or typeqlForm mentions any scopeLabel

  func renderForGenerator() -> String {
    // produces the multi-section LLM input format documented below
  }
}

struct GistAnchorContext: Sendable {
  let gistRoot: String                    // e.g. "gist:Activity"
  let immediateSubtypes: [String]         // first-level children
}

struct CompetencyQuestionRef: Sendable {
  let cqId: String
  let nlForm: String
  let typeqlForm: String?
  let cqStatus: String
}

enum CoreOntologySliceComputer {
  static func compute(
    seedLabels: Set<String>,
    schemaModel: SchemaModel,
    cqRegistry: [CompetencyQuestionRef],
    config: SliceConfig = .default
  ) -> CoreOntologySlice
}

struct SliceConfig: Sendable {
  let maxTypes: Int = 50
  let maxSubtypesPerType: Int = 10
  let maxFunctionsKept: Int = 20
  let maxHops: Int = 2
}
```

Algorithm (deterministic):

```
function compute(seedLabels, schemaModel, cqRegistry, config):
  scope = ∅
  frontier = seedLabels

  for hop in 1..config.maxHops:
    next_frontier = ∅
    for label in frontier:
      type = schemaModel.lookup(label)
      if type == nil: continue                      # new concept; Generator will introduce it
      if label in scope: continue
      scope.add(label)

      # Direct supertype
      if type.supertype != nil: next_frontier.add(type.supertype)

      # Direct subtypes (capped)
      for subtype in type.directSubtypes.prefix(config.maxSubtypesPerType):
        next_frontier.add(subtype.label)

      # Owned attribute types
      for owns in type.declaredOwns + type.inheritedOwns:
        next_frontier.add(owns.attributeLabel)

      # Played roles' enclosing relations
      for plays in type.declaredPlays + type.inheritedPlays:
        next_frontier.add(plays.relationLabel)

      # For relations: types that play any of this relation's roles
      if type is RelationType:
        for role in type.relates:
          for playerLabel in schemaModel.typesPlaying(relation: type.label, role: role.name):
            next_frontier.add(playerLabel)

    frontier = next_frontier - scope

  # Functions whose body references any scope label
  functionsKept = schemaModel.functions
    .filter { fn in fn.referencedTypeLabels.intersection(scope).isNotEmpty }
    .prefix(config.maxFunctionsKept)

  # GIST anchor context: for each scope type, walk its supertype chain to a GIST root.
  # Then for each GIST root reached, include its first-level subtypes.
  gistRoots = scope.compactMap { schemaModel.gistRoot(for: $0) }.unique()
  gistAnchors = gistRoots.map { root in
    GistAnchorContext(
      gistRoot: root,
      immediateSubtypes: schemaModel.directSubtypes(of: root).map(\.label)
    )
  }

  # Nearby CQs: any CQ whose nlForm or typeqlForm mentions any scope label
  nearbyCQs = cqRegistry.filter { cq in
    scope.contains(where: { label in
      cq.nlForm.contains(label) || (cq.typeqlForm?.contains(label) ?? false)
    })
  }

  # Cap total types
  if scope.size > config.maxTypes:
    drop = scope.size - config.maxTypes
    # Drop subtypes first, then types not directly seeded
    scope = trimByPriority(scope, dropCount: drop, seedLabels)

  return CoreOntologySlice(
    scopeLabels: scope,
    types: schemaModel.types.filter { scope.contains($0.label) },
    functions: functionsKept,
    gistAnchors: gistAnchors,
    nearbyCQs: nearbyCQs
  )
```

renderForGenerator() output format (multi-section text):

```
== GIST anchors in scope ==
gist:Activity (subtypes: Event, Task, Process, ...)
gist:Category (subtypes: Type, Kind, ...)

== User-extended types in scope ==
<focused TypeQL fragment for the slice types, with inherited capabilities annotated as comments>

== Functions in scope ==
<function declarations from the slice's functions>

== Relevant CQs ==
[unanswered] cq-abc-123: "How many meetings did Alice attend last quarter?"
[partial]    cq-def-456: "Which features depend on which releases?"

== Pattern Library suggestions ==
<this section is filled by the synthesis workflow before passing to the Generator,
 not by this slice computation. Slice produces sections 1-4; workflow appends 5.>
```

Constraints:
- Pure function. No I/O, no side effects.
- Deterministic: identical inputs (seedLabels, schemaModel state, cqRegistry, config) produce identical output, including ordering. Use deterministic sort orders (alphabetical by label).
- Bounds enforced strictly. No silent overflows.

Test fixtures:
- small synthetic SchemaModel (e.g., gist subset + a few user types)
- expected slices for representative seed sets
- assert exact output (label set, capability lists, render output)

Used by: SchemaGeneratorAgent (38.4.13), JudgeStep (38.4.14), MigratorAgent (38.4.15) — all consume the slice as their schema-context input.

title: Adopt APM for centralized agent skill management
description:
Replace the current relative-symlink approach to skill sharing (which assumes both collection-one and collection-vibe-machine sit as siblings under ~/SoftwareProjects/) with Microsoft's APM (Agent Package Manager). Skills will live in a private GitHub repo, declared as dependencies in each consumer repo's apm.yml, and installed via 'apm install' into the locations Claude Code and Codex expect.

Why APM: (1) current symlinks break on CI machines that only clone one of the two collections; (2) directory-layout assumption is fragile if anyone reorganizes; (3) no integrity verification or version pinning; (4) all skills must be private — no public marketplace. APM solves all four with a manifest + lockfile model and supports private GitHub repos via the user's existing credentials.

Risks: (1) APM is a recent project (Sep 2025) — bus factor and maturity; (2) Codex compatibility is claimed but unverified for our setup; (3) Unicode hijack scanner may false-positive on Greek letters in swift-concurrency typing rules; (4) one-time migration cost across 8 repos.
design: Pilot in OneWorkspace + ontology-gist before rolling out to the other 6 repos. Decommission only after rollout is verified. Use the user's existing GitHub credentials and the vibe-machine org (or kenpo personal) for the private skills repo — final naming is a sub-decision.

(2) OneWorkspace and all 7 ontology-* repos consume skills via apm install (apm.yml + apm.lock committed in each). (3) Claude Code and Codex both find every migrated skill in every consumer repo. (4) Old relative symlinks are removed. (5) Root CLAUDE.md documents APM as the skill management approach with a brief maintenance workflow.

title: AI tools to focus proposal in explorer or editor
description: Add two new dispatch-only AI tools (focus_proposal_in_explorer, focus_proposal_in_editor) so the assistant can flip between the two views on user request. Update propose_schema_change to auto-open the Lingo Explorer instead of the Type Editor as the default landing surface.
design:
New tools in Agent/Tools/SchemaEvolutionTools.swift (or new file Agent/Tools/LingoUITools.swift):

struct FocusProposalInExplorerTool: OneTool, @unchecked Sendable {
  let name = 'focus_proposal_in_explorer'
  let description = 'Open the Lingo Explorer panel to review the current schema proposal. Closes the Lingo Type Editor if open.'
  parameters: [] (no args in V1; V2 adds optional proposal_id)
  execute: viewModel.openLingoExplorer(); return .dictionary(['opened': .bool(true)])
}

struct FocusProposalInEditorTool: OneTool, @unchecked Sendable {
  let name = 'focus_proposal_in_editor'
  let description = 'Open the Lingo Type Editor panel for tabular review of the current schema proposal. Closes the Lingo Explorer if open.'
  parameters: [] 
  execute: viewModel.openLingoTypeEditor(); return .dictionary(['opened': .bool(true)])
}

Tool registration: add to SchemaEvolutionTools.makeTools (or a new makeTools alongside).

ProposeSchemaChangeTool change: in execute(), replace the call to viewModel.openLingoTypeEditor() with viewModel.openLingoExplorer(). Update transcript message from 'I opened it in the Lingo Type Editor for review.' to 'I opened it in the Lingo Explorer for review. You can switch to the Lingo Type Editor if you prefer the table view.'

Soft-error contract: if no current proposal exists when focus_proposal_in_explorer is called, return a friendly message ('No active proposal — ask me to propose a schema change first.') rather than throwing.
acceptance_criteria:
- AI can call focus_proposal_in_explorer → explorer panel opens, editor closes.
- AI can call focus_proposal_in_editor → editor panel opens, explorer closes.

title: End-to-end smoke test of Lingo Explorer V1
