title: Lingo Explorer: schema proposal browser parallel to the entity explorer
description: A new browser-style widget for reviewing and (eventually) editing Lingo schema proposals. Renders the proposal as a synthetic top-of-sidebar section above the live ontology, fully self-contained inside the chat's panel area. Lives parallel to the Lingo Type Editor — same chat panel slot, different widget — so the user (and the AI on their behalf) can flip between them. Built as a parallel implementation to the existing entity browser (copy SwiftUI views; share TypeQLParser, Parsed* models, and LingoProposalVerifier) so the two views can evolve independently before being refactored to a shared foundation once the patterns settle.
design:
Architectural decisions:
- Self-contained widget. All cross-references (e.g., a proposed type's parent in vibemachine, an owned attribute, a played role) resolve INSIDE the Lingo Explorer panel — clicking never navigates the user out to the standalone entity browser route. The widget contains its own 3-pane layout: sidebar tree | detail panel | inspector.
- Lives in the same chat panel area as the Lingo Type Editor. Only one of {Type Editor, Lingo Explorer} is visible at a time. AI tools swap between them.
- Single source of truth, live binding. Both Type Editor and Lingo Explorer read from the same OntologyViewModel proposal state. When the conversation revises the proposal, both reflect it instantly.
- Copy-don't-reuse for SwiftUI. Lingo Explorer SwiftUI files are copied from Views/Entities/* into Views/Lingo/Explorer/* (LingoExplorerView, LingoExplorerTreeView, LingoExplorerRowView, LingoEntityDetailView, LingoRelationDetailView, LingoAttributeDetailView, LingoTypeInspectorView). The two view stacks are allowed to diverge under different pressure (live explorer optimizes for filter/search/perf-at-scale; Lingo Explorer optimizes for diff badges, edit affordances, multi-proposal). Shared (NOT copied): TypeQLParser, ParsedEntity/Relation/Attribute, LingoProposalVerifier — pure types and pure logic, no UI churn risk.
- Phased rollout. V1 ships view-only single-proposal mechanics fast so the visual concept is real and we can iterate. V2 adds multi-proposal management. V3 promotes the proposal data model to structural source of truth and adds in-widget editing with TypeQL serialization. V4 looks back at V1+V3 and refactors duplication between the two explorers into a shared foundation — only after the patterns have settled with real use.
- Eventual consistency: V4's refactor pass is explicit. The cost of letting the two explorers drift in V1-V3 is paid back by extracting a battle-tested shared abstraction in V4 instead of guessing one upfront.
acceptance_criteria:
All five features delivered. End-to-end loop works:
- Assistant proposes schema change via propose_schema_change → Lingo Explorer panel opens automatically with the proposal section visible.
- User reviews proposal in the explorer (navigates inheritance, reads docs, sees diff vs. live).
- User asks the assistant to revise; the proposal updates and both Lingo Explorer + Lingo Type Editor reflect the change.
- User can edit the proposal directly in the explorer (rename a type, change a parent, etc.) and the change round-trips through TypeQL.
- User clicks Apply → entire proposal applies atomically.
Multi-proposal supported. Live cross-references pinned to the active sandbox's installed package versions. Both explorers (live entity + Lingo) eventually share a refactored foundation with proposal-specific UI living in the Lingo layer.

title: getParsedSchema must expose relation roles, not just relation names
description: OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/SchemaIntrospectionTools.swift returns relationNames as a flat array of relation labels, with no role information. The agent has no way to learn what roles a relation declares — and run_read_query is forbidden by system prompt for schema metadata. Result: when constructing TypeQL like 'X plays Y:Z', the agent guesses Z from system-prompt knowledge or memory and is wrong whenever the live schema's role names diverge from canonical. Confirmed failure mode in user session: agent emitted plays isDirectPartOf:part (canonical role is directPart) and TypeDB rejected the apply with [SYR9] role type not found. Fix: replace relationNames with relations: [{ name, roles: [...] }]. Maintain relationNames for backward-compat if any tool tests depend on it, or update tests.
acceptance_criteria: getParsedSchema response includes relation role names per relation. Agent receiving the response can construct correct plays declarations against the live schema's actual role names. Tests cover: (a) relations array carries each relation with its declared roles in stable order; (b) result handles relations with multiple roles; (c) parser-to-tool round trip preserves role labels.
close_reason: getParsedSchema now returns a relations: [{ name, roles: [...] }] field in addition to the existing relationNames flat array. Each relation entry carries the actual declared role names from the parsed live schema. SchemaIntrospectionTools.swift constructs RelationDescriptor from ParsedRelation.roles.map(\.roleName); the agent reading the response can construct correct 'X plays Y:Z' declarations against the live schema's actual role names rather than guessing canonical names. System prompt updated to require reading the roles array before any plays declaration. Tests in LingoAgentTests cover (a) per-relation roles array population for multi-role relations like isPartOf and (b) single-role relations. Combined with one-wcv (memory live-schema fallback), the agent now has two independent paths to discover correct role names: search_ontology_memory for package precedent, and getParsedSchema for live-schema ground truth.

title: Bound TypeDBService.checkReachable so an unresponsive candidate cannot stall 30s
description: When the Knowledge view first opens, OntologyViewModel.refreshTypeDBState calls TypeDBService.connect, which iterates connection candidates. The current checkReachable uses Darwin.connect() with only SO_SNDTIMEO set, which does not bound connect() itself. On 2026-04-30, candidate #2 hung for exactly 30s before failing while EuroRack was still booting the typedb container. Fix the timeout so an unresponsive endpoint fails fast.
design:
## Evidence
From PID 91891:
  11:45:37.944  [ontology:TypeDBService] TypeDB connect candidates: <list>
  11:45:37.945  [ontology:TypeDBService] TypeDB connect attempt failed [candidate #1]
  ... 30s hang on candidate #2 ...
  11:46:07.946  [ontology:TypeDBService] TypeDB connect attempt failed [candidate #2]
  11:46:07.946  [ontology:TypeDBService] Health check failed
  11:46:07.946  [ontology:TypeDB] TypeDB refresh failed

Meanwhile EuroRack finishes booting typedb at 11:46:02 and a fresh connect at 11:46:04 succeeds.

## Files to modify
- OneApps/Ontology/Backend/TypeDBServiceProvider.swift
  - `checkReachable(address:)` at line 378
  - The blocking `Darwin.connect()` at line 415 with `SO_SNDTIMEO` (line 412-413)

## Approach
SO_SNDTIMEO does not bound connect(). Switch to a non-blocking probe:
1. Set the socket non-blocking with `fcntl(sock, F_SETFL, O_NONBLOCK)`.
2. Call `Darwin.connect()`. Expect EINPROGRESS.
3. Use `poll()` or `select()` with a 1500ms timeout on POLLOUT.
4. If poll signals writable, check SO_ERROR via getsockopt to confirm connect succeeded.
5. If poll times out, close the socket and treat as UNREACHABLE.

Per-candidate ceiling: 1500ms. With 2-3 candidates, worst case is ~4.5s instead of 30s+.

## Additional consideration
Ontology activate() registers the TypeDB workload contribution but does NOT trigger connect; connect happens later from refreshTypeDBState() when a Knowledge view first appears. So this fix improves first-view-open responsiveness, not pure plugin activation. Keep this scope tight - do not add reconnect-on-failure logic here, that is a separate concern.

## Reference
- Standard non-blocking connect pattern: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/connect.2.html (EINPROGRESS section)
- macOS getsockopt(SO_ERROR) for connect status check
acceptance_criteria: checkReachable returns within ~1.5s per candidate when an endpoint is unresponsive. The 30s stall on Knowledge view first-open with typedb still booting is gone. Existing TypeDB-related tests in OntologyTests still pass; add a unit test that checkReachable to a deliberately black-holed address (e.g., 10.255.255.1:1) returns within 2s.

title: Parallelize plugin activation in AppState
description: AppState activates plugins sequentially, so a single slow plugin (currently VibeMachine at 4.5s) blocks every plugin after it. Activate independent plugins concurrently so fast plugins can finish even when one is slow.
design:
## Evidence
In the 2026-04-30 launch:
  - 8 of 9 plugins activated in <80 ms each.
  - vibemachine (8th in order) took 4,484 ms.
  - producer (9th) was forced to wait until vibemachine finished, even though it activates in 5 ms.

If plugins had activated concurrently, total wall-clock time would have been bounded by the slowest plugin (still 4.5s until that's fixed) - but more importantly, this shape will keep plugin loading from regressing whenever any single plugin gets slow.

## Files to modify
- OneApp/OneApp/GammaShell/AppState.swift (the activation loop that emits "Activating plugin: ..." / "Plugin activated: ...")
- OneApp/OneApp/GammaShell/PluginLoader/PluginLoader.swift (if dependency-resolved phases need preserving)

## Approach
1. Read the current activation loop in AppState.
2. PluginLoader already groups plugins into role-based phases ("Phase: <role> (N plugins)" log). Keep phases sequential but activate plugins WITHIN a phase concurrently with TaskGroup.
3. Preserve ordering guarantees of any service registry the plugins write to during activate(). If services are MainActor-isolated and writes serialize naturally, concurrent activate() should be safe; if not, surface those constraints in the task notes and gate concurrency to phases where it's known safe.
4. Keep the per-plugin "Plugin activated" log so we still see each one's individual duration.

## Risks to evaluate
- Plugins that depend on a service registered by an earlier plugin in the same phase. Today the dependency resolution sort handles cross-plugin order, but within a phase the loader assumes "all peers in this phase are independent" - confirm.
- Service registry concurrency: GammaCore service container may not be set up for concurrent registration.
acceptance_criteria: Within each activation phase, plugins activate concurrently. Producer no longer waits on VibeMachine. Re-running the launch profile shows total activation wall-clock <= max(individual plugin activate times) + small overhead. Existing PluginLoaderEndToEndTests still pass.

title: Faster plugin activation and post-launch responsiveness
description: Bundle of work to reduce the ~4.6s plugin activation window and the ~30s TypeDB connect stall that delays Knowledge view first-open.
design:
## Scope
Three concrete child tasks rolled up here:
1. Investigate and fix VibeMachine activate() taking 4.5 s.
2. Parallelize plugin activation in AppState (or otherwise prevent one slow plugin from blocking the rest).
3. Bound TypeDBService.checkReachable so an unresponsive candidate cannot stall 30 s.

## Why one feature, not three independent epics
All three roll into the same user-visible symptom ("plugin loading is slow after launch"). Keeping them under one feature gives a single place to evaluate cumulative impact (re-run the launch profile and check the totals listed in the parent epic).

## Sequencing
- Investigation task (VibeMachine 4.5 s) is the gating piece. It will likely produce its own follow-ups.
- Parallel activation can land independently and benefits all plugins.
- TypeDB checkReachable fix is independent of the other two.
acceptance_criteria: All child tasks closed; baseline launch profile re-captured with the same  command in the epic; plugin activation total < 1s; no 30s stall on TypeDB connect.

title: OntologyMemoryPackageFilter false-skips packages whose schema is in knowledge but bootstrap registry is empty
description: OntologyMemoryPackageFilter.selectInstalledPackages decides 'installed' purely from PackageBootstrapRegistry .applied records for the database. Packages whose schema is functionally present in 'knowledge' (160 entities, 128 relations seen in the user's session — clearly gist+vibemachine+other content) but were applied through a different path (manual schema apply, bootstrap path that didn't write a record, drift cleanup) get skipped — and the user sees a misleading 'gist: not installed in knowledge' message. The current message has been silenced from the chat (logs to os.Logger only) but the underlying detection is wrong: search_ontology_memory now skips those packages even though their precedent should be searchable. Better signal: any package whose schema labels (entity/relation/attribute names from package prefix or parsed package files) intersect the live parsed schema labels in the database is functionally installed. Or fall back to: if registry has no records at all for the database, treat all loaded packages as candidates rather than skipping all.
acceptance_criteria: search_ontology_memory in a 'knowledge' database whose schema includes gist + vibemachine entity/relation/attribute labels selects those packages without skipping. The detection logic does not depend solely on PackageBootstrapRegistry for ground truth. Tests cover: (a) package whose entity name is present in live parsed schema is selected; (b) registry being empty-but-schema-present does not skip everything.
close_reason: OntologyMemoryPackageFilter now accepts a liveSchemaLabels Set<String> and falls back to label intersection when the bootstrap registry has no records for a package. If any of the package's declared labels (entities/relations/attributes from its bundled .tql files) appear in the live schema, the package is treated as functionally installed and gets selected for the memory corpus. OntologyViewModel+Memory.installedKnowledgeMemoryPackages now fetches typeSchema(database:) and parses the labels before invoking the filter; on any TypeDB failure the call falls back to registry-only behavior. Tests in OntologyMemoryCorpusTests cover: (a) registry empty + matching live labels selects; (b) registry empty + no matching live labels skips; (c) no live labels available falls back to strict registry behavior. Strict happy-path with version/checksum mismatch still skips correctly. Bundled gist (with isPartOf, Task, Collection, etc.) is now recoverable for search_ontology_memory even when the bootstrap registry is stale or empty.

title: Lingo Type Editor pane shows empty rows after a schema proposal lands
description: When the agent calls propose_schema_change, the pending proposal is set on viewModel.lingoEngineeringHierarchyProposal and openLingoTypeEditor() is called, but the user reports the editor pane appears not populated even though a schema change has been proposed. Possible causes: rows derived from LingoTypeEditorPresentation.rows(for:) returning empty for the current proposal shape; the editor is open but pinned to a stale proposal id after revision/supersession; UI refresh skipped when proposal changes in place via revision. Repro: ask Lingo to extend a hierarchy; observe whether the editor pane between transcript and input bar shows rows for proposed entities/relations/attributes.
acceptance_criteria: After propose_schema_change runs, the Lingo Type Editor pane (LingoTypeEditorView) displays a non-empty row list including the proposed entity/relation/attribute labels for the active revision. Re-revising via supersession refreshes the editor to the new revision's rows. Tests cover: (a) rows returned by LingoTypeEditorPresentation for the current proposal are non-empty; (b) a revision update changes the visible rows.

title: Make AllPlugins aggregate build path correct and clean
description: Get mise run build-aggregate working end-to-end by fixing the latent issues it surfaced, plus the smaller wins that ride along.
design:
Path A from build perf investigation:
1. Add EuroRackContracts as explicit framework dep on GhosttyTerminal.xcodeproj (it relied on auto-linking through GammaCore re-export)
2. Add flock to scripts/install-plugin-bundle.sh so parallel plugin builds don't race in the group container
3. Auto-generate One.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/xcschemes/AllPlugins.xcscheme from pbxproj files (drift hazard otherwise)
4. Smaller wins:
   - Drop redundant 'mise run install --all' from dev.sh (build phase already installs)
   - Change build_scheme default action from 'clean build' to 'build'
   - Gate resign_oneapp_nested_runtime on nested-helper mtime
5. Verify mise run build-aggregate completes successfully
acceptance_criteria: mise run build-aggregate succeeds on a hot incremental and is faster than mise run build --all
close_reason: mise run build-aggregate now succeeds end-to-end. Hot no-op: 24s vs 170s for build --all (~7× faster). All five Path A items landed: GhosttyTerminal pbxproj declares EuroRackContracts dep + invokes install-plugin-bundle.sh; install-plugin-bundle.sh has mkdir lock to serialize parallel installs; AllPlugins.xcscheme auto-generated from pbxproj files via scripts/generate-allplugins-scheme.sh (hooked into bootstrap); dev.sh drops redundant install --all; build_scheme default off 'clean build'; resign_oneapp_nested_runtime gated on mtime stamp.

title: Compact tool-use trace strip in Lingo chat
description: The Lingo chat surfaces every agent tool call as a full transcript row (start, complete, sometimes both, plus per-tool inline messages from tools themselves). For schema-design turns this swamps the chat. Replace per-call rows with a single in-line trace strip per assistant turn: small chips (toolName · duration · status), pair start/complete into one updating entry, suppress separate rows for read-only tools, and auto-expand failures with the error inline. Click any chip to reveal arguments + result preview. The chip data flows through a new LingoToolTracePart so the existing widget registry can render it. Tools and assistant prose stay legible; tool detail is one click away.
acceptance_criteria: Successful read-only tool calls (listDatabases, getParsedSchema, search_ontology_memory, run_read_query, query_intents) no longer produce standalone Tool started/completed transcript rows — they appear as chips in a per-turn trace strip. Failed tool calls are visually loud (red chip, expanded inline detail). Each tool call paired into one entry, not two rows. The trace strip is implemented as a registered LingoTranscriptPart so the widget registry resolves it. Tests cover: (a) consecutive tool starts/completions accumulate into a single trace item with one entry per call; (b) failure flips an entry to .failed and preserves the error; (c) assistant .completed/.failed/.cancelled closes the active trace so the next tool call starts a fresh one; (d) read-only tools do not produce separate row items.
close_reason: Replaced per-call Tool started/Tool completed transcript rows with a single per-turn LingoToolTracePart strip. New view-model methods recordToolCallStarted/Completed/Failed accumulate entries by callId and pair start/complete in place; closeActiveLingoToolTrace ends the strip when the assistant turn finishes. Read-only tools (LingoReadOnlyToolNames) are flagged in entries so the chip shows a 'read' badge and doesn't generate a separate row. Failures auto-promote a loud .error transcript row alongside the chip and the chip auto-expands to show args/result/error inline. LingoToolTraceCard widget is registered in the registry under shape 'ontology.toolTrace.v1'. OntologyAgentService.handleAgentEvent routes tool events through the new path. Diagnostic recorder captures the trace part. Tests in LingoToolTraceTests cover accumulation into a single item, failure promotion (both .toolCallFailed and non-success completion), turn-boundary trace closure, read-only flag propagation, and compact arguments preview.

title: Make Lingo schema proposals concise: cut compliance-form sections
description:
## Problem

Lingo's schema-change proposal output reads as a compliance form, not a conversation. The actual answer (often 2 lines of TypeQL) is buried under sections that mostly justify the assistant's process to itself. Users have called the output "overwhelming" and "overly verbose."

## Example

For "extend VibeEngineeringTask to support children", the assistant returned ~350 words across 9 headed sections — Verified live-schema facts, Gist/precedent reuse, Proposed TypeQL, Rollback, Rationale, Drift/collision check, Assumptions, Important note, follow-up options — when the useful content was ~80 words: the two `plays` constraints, one-line rationale, one-line next step.

## Desired behavior

The proposal output should default to:
1. Proposed TypeQL (lead with it, not bury it)
2. One-line rationale tying it to gist/precedent
3. One-line next step (apply in sandbox)

Other sections become **conditional** — shown only when they carry information:
- **Rollback** — only if reverting is non-trivial (data loss, dependent types). Mechanical `define`→`undefine` inversion is noise.
- **Drift / collision check** — only when non-zero. "0, 0" is meaningless surface.
- **Assumptions** — only when the user's intent was ambiguous and a load-bearing call was made. Filler assumptions ("no instance migration in this step") get cut.
- **Verified live-schema facts** — only when something *unexpected* turned up. Default-checked facts the user already assumes you checked are noise.
- **Important note / disclaimer** — already implied by the heading. Collapse "this is a proposal, not applied, sandbox needed" into one line, or fold into the next-step line.

Additionally: when the user asks a multi-part question, address all parts substantively. In the example, the user asked about both hierarchy *and* future top-level task collections — the assistant punted on the second half ("we can defer") instead of sketching the pattern (e.g., gist `Collection` ←`hasMember`→ task) in a single line.

## Out of scope

- Changing what gets *checked* during proposal generation (drift/collision detection, schema verification). Only what gets *surfaced* to the user.
- Changing apply_schema_delta or sandbox flow (covered by one-azz.5).

## Acceptance

- A schema proposal for a simple add (e.g., new `plays` constraints on an existing entity) renders in well under 100 words by default
- Rollback section absent unless the change is risky to revert
- Drift/collision section absent when both are zero
- Assumptions section absent unless an ambiguous-intent call was made
- Multi-part user requests get multi-part proposals (no silent deferral)
- Existing detection/verification logic unchanged — only output-rendering / prompt instructions change
design:
## Approach

The verbosity is a **prompt-shape problem**, not a tool-output problem. The assistant treats every section in its template as required output. Fix is to make sections conditional and reorder for lead-with-the-answer.

## Where the change lives

Likely in the OntologyAgentService prompt(s) that govern proposal rendering — specifically the system prompt section that instructs the model how to format `propose_schema_change` results. Need to locate the exact prompt file (search for terms like "Verified live-schema facts", "Drift / collision check", "Important note" in OneApps/Ontology).

If the rendering is split between prompt instructions and post-tool-call formatting code, both surfaces need updating.

## Prompt restructure (sketch)

Replace the always-render template with conditional instructions:

```
When presenting a schema proposal:
1. Lead with the proposed TypeQL.
2. Follow with one line of rationale tying the change to existing gist/precedent.
3. Close with one line on the next step (sandbox application).

Include the following sections ONLY when the named condition holds:
- Rollback: only when reverting is non-trivial (data loss possible, or dependent
  types need cleanup). Mechanical define→undefine inversion is not worth showing.
- Drift / collision check: only when either count is non-zero.
- Assumptions: only when the user's intent was ambiguous and you made a
  load-bearing interpretation. Do not list trivia like "no instance migration".
- Verified live-schema facts: only when verification turned up something
  unexpected (entity didn't exist, relation has different roles than assumed,
  etc.). Default verification is assumed by the user.

If the user asked a multi-part question, address every part with at least a
one-line concrete sketch. Never silently defer one half.

Keep the disclaimer ("proposal, not applied, sandbox required") to a single
line — fold it into the next-step line when possible.
```

## Verification

- Re-run the original "extend VibeEngineeringTask to support children" prompt and confirm the response is ≤100 words and addresses both parts (hierarchy + future top-level collections)
- Try a proposal that *does* warrant rollback (e.g., dropping a relation with instances) — confirm rollback section reappears
- Try a proposal where verification finds a mismatch (e.g., entity doesn't exist) — confirm "verified facts" section reappears with the surprise
- Try a proposal with a real collision — confirm collision section appears with the value

## Risks

- Going too terse loses safety affordances. Mitigation: keep the always-on next-step line as the load-bearing reminder that nothing has been applied yet.
- Conditional sections risk inconsistency across runs. Mitigation: prompt should give the model explicit thresholds ("non-zero", "non-trivial revert"), not vague guidance.

## Out of scope

- Changing the underlying detection/verification logic
- Changing apply_schema_delta or sandbox semantics (one-azz.5)
- Changing transcript token-usage rendering (one-azz.6)
close_reason: Prompt updated: lead with TypeQL, conditional sections (rollback/drift/assumptions/verified-facts/disclaimer), multi-part-question rule. 3 new prompt-content tests in LingoAgentTests cover the new shape and forbid the old always-render framing. Version bumped to one-xaf.

title: Legacy and self-describing TypeDoc parser drops fields after a semicolon inside quoted values
description: StaticSchemaProvider.parseLegacyTypeDocEntries splits content with components(separatedBy: ";") and parseSchemaResourceEntries uses non-greedy regex up to the first ";". Both break when a quoted attribute value contains a semicolon (e.g. usageNote "...generic work items; use Bead..."). The block is truncated mid-statement, causing every "has" clause that follows the offending field to be silently dropped — including sourceIRI, altLabel, editorialNote, etc. Discovered while working on one-9jl: scopeNotes for Task came out empty until the offending usageNote was reordered to the end of the statement.
design: Replace the naive ;-split with a quote-aware tokenizer that ignores ; inside double-quoted strings. Apply to both parseLegacyTypeDocEntries and parseSchemaResourceEntries. Also audit other regex-based parsers in StaticSchemaProvider that match up to the first ; (parseSchemaModuleEntries, parseSchemaViewEntries, parseSchemaGroupEntries, etc.) for the same bug.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test using a TypeDoc/SchemaResource fixture with a ; inside a quoted value asserts that all "has" attributes parse correctly regardless of their order in the statement. parseLegacyTypeDocEntries and parseSchemaResourceEntries both produce complete entries when values contain ;.
notes: Discovered while implementing one-9jl. Worked around by reordering the gist Task TypeDoc fixture so usageNote (which contains ;) comes last. The pre-existing scopeNotes-empty-for-Task issue likely went undetected because no test asserted it.
close_reason: Added quote-aware StaticSchemaProvider.splitTypeQLStatements helper that splits on ; only outside double-quoted values. Refactored parseLegacyTypeDocEntries, parseLegacyDomainEntries, parseSchemaModuleEntries, parseSchemaResourceEntries, parseSchemaViewEntries, parseSchemaGroupEntries, and parseVariableKeyMap to use the splitter instead of components(separatedBy: ';') / non-greedy regex up to first ;. Restored the natural attribute ordering in the gist Task TypeDoc fixture (usageNote with embedded ; is now in its original position) and confirmed all OntologyMemoryCorpusTests still pass — proving the parser handles ; inside quoted values end-to-end. Three new tests cover the splitter directly and a temporary fixture package whose TypeDoc has ; in both definition and usageNote.

title: Lift runOnce into BaseAgentService and clean up VibeMachine duplication
description: Three concrete duplications and one missing convenience were found while comparing VibeMachine's agent usage to Lingo's. (1) BaseAgentService should provide a runOnce(userTurn:) async throws -> OneAgentResult convenience that aggregates the per-call event stream into a single result — VibeMachine currently re-implements this aggregation in OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/AgentService.swift lines ~122-149. (2) VibeMachine duplicates provider-resolution fallback logic (re-instantiating AssistantConfigStore + ProviderResolver outside MuseRuntimeProviding when museRuntime is nil — lines ~86-100); should route through Muse. (3) VibeMachine carries a second legacy KeychainService at OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/KeychainService.swift, distinct from SwarmAgent.KeychainService — dead surface, should be removed. (4) VibeMachine.AgentService.startSession is monolithic (mixes prompt-building, tool construction, provider resolution); could adopt Lingo's split where a typed startConversation overload separates these concerns.
design:
Files: OneApp/SwarmAgent/AgentService.swift (BaseAgentService — add runOnce convenience); OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/AgentService.swift (consume the new runOnce, delete duplicated aggregation); OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/KeychainService.swift (delete); OneApps/VibeMachine/Views/Design/Workspace/Chat/DesignChatSession.swift (consumer — verify aggregation still works); OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/DesignAgent.swift (system-prompt builder — already collapsed in d4a0f17e); OneApps/Ontology/Agent/OntologyAgentService.swift (reference for the typed-startConversation pattern); OneApp/SwarmAgent/MuseRuntime.swift (the provider-resolution surface).

Approach (4 sub-changes):

A) BaseAgentService.runOnce convenience. Public nonisolated method on BaseAgentService (or add to the AgentService protocol):
   public nonisolated func runOnce(userTurn: String) async throws -> OneAgentResult { for try await event in run(userTurn: userTurn) { ... aggregate ... } }
   Aggregates .outputChunk/.outputToken into output text, .toolCallStarted/.toolCallCompleted into a tool-calls list, returns final OneAgentResult on .completed (or throws on .failed). Replaces VibeMachine's hand-rolled loop.

B) Remove VibeMachine provider-resolution fallback. Drop the if museRuntime != nil branch with the AssistantConfigStore/ProviderResolver fallback (AgentService.swift lines ~86-100). Either require museRuntime always (precondition fatalError) or surface a typed PluginContextRequiresMuse error. Muse is now always present at runtime; the fallback is dead code from the pre-facade era.

C) Delete OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/KeychainService.swift. Remove its references in VibeMachine.AgentService (the public getAPIKey/setAPIKey/deleteAPIKey API — lines ~162-183). Settings UI must already have moved to AssistantSettingsView under Muse; verify before deleting.

D) Split startSession(for:designState:toolsEnabled:). Adopt OntologyAgentService's pattern: a low-level startConversation(systemPrompt:tools:resolvedProvider:memoryConfig:) that takes the inputs prepared by the caller, plus a higher-level startSession that resolves the provider and constructs prompts/tools. The split makes testing easier (low-level can be exercised with a stub provider; high-level wraps the resolver glue).
acceptance_criteria: BaseAgentService.runOnce ships and is unit-tested in OneApp/SwarmAgentTests/AgentServiceTests.swift. VibeMachine.AgentService consumes runOnce instead of its hand-rolled aggregation loop. VibeMachine.AgentService.startSession requires museRuntime (no fallback) or surfaces a typed error. OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/KeychainService.swift deleted; settings UI continues working through AssistantSettingsView. VibeMachine startSession split into low-level + high-level forms matching OntologyAgentService's pattern. All VibeMachine tests still pass.

title: Map Conduit AIError into OneAgentError so UI shows actionable messages
description: Conduit ships rich error categorization on its AIError type (~/.cache/one-spm-packages/checkouts/Conduit/Sources/Conduit/Core/Errors/AIError.swift line ~429): isRetryable, category, recoverySuggestion, and structured cases including .rateLimited(retryAfter:), .billingError, .authenticationFailed, .tokenLimitExceeded. Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Providers/Conduit/ConduitInferenceProvider.swift currently rethrows the raw Error without unwrapping, so Swarm and the UI fall back to error.localizedDescription — losing actionable categorization. Map AIError cases into OneAgentError so OntologyAgentServiceError.userFacingMessage can show 'invalid API key' vs 'rate limited' vs 'token limit exceeded' with provider-specific recovery hints, and the agent loop can use isRetryable for selective retry rather than blanket retry.
design:
Files: Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Providers/Conduit/ConduitInferenceProvider.swift (the rethrow site at generate / generateWithToolCalls / streamWithToolCalls); ~/.cache/one-spm-packages/checkouts/Conduit/Sources/Conduit/Core/Errors/AIError.swift (read-only — the AIError shape); Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Core/AgentError.swift (target enum); OneApp/SwarmAgent/Adapters/AgentErrorBridge.swift (the bridge to OneAgentError); OneApps/Ontology/Agent/OntologyAgentService.swift (userFacingMessage — already has cases for rateLimitExceeded, modelNotAvailable, contextWindowExceeded, etc.); OneApp/SwarmAgent/Providers/ProviderResolver.swift (also bypasses ConduitProviderSelection factories — see secondary cleanup below).

Primary approach:
1. In ConduitInferenceProvider, wrap each provider call in a do/catch that pattern-matches AIError cases and rethrows as appropriate AgentError cases:
   - .authenticationFailed → AgentError.inferenceProviderUnavailable(reason: 'API key rejected')
   - .rateLimited(let retryAfter) → AgentError.rateLimitExceeded(retryAfter:)
   - .billingError → AgentError.inferenceProviderUnavailable(reason: 'billing')
   - .tokenLimitExceeded → AgentError.contextWindowExceeded
   - .modelNotFound → AgentError.modelNotAvailable(model: ...)
   - default → AgentError.generationFailed(reason: aiError.recoverySuggestion ?? aiError.localizedDescription)
2. AgentErrorBridge already maps AgentError → OneAgentError; verify the new shapes flow through cleanly.
3. OntologyAgentServiceError.userFacingMessage already handles most of these cases (rateLimitExceeded, modelNotAvailable, contextWindowExceeded); just verify the friendly messages match the new categorization. May need a new case for 'billing' since the existing 'inferenceProviderUnavailable' message is generic.

Secondary cleanup (optional, can defer to follow-up):
- ProviderResolver hand-rolls Conduit configuration construction (OpenAIConfiguration, AnthropicConfiguration) instead of using the existing Swarm-side Swarm.ConduitProviderSelection.openAI/.anthropic/.openRouter factories. Consider routing through those factories once the AIError path is in place.
- Conduit supports per-config retryConfig / timeout / maxRetries that are accepted as silent defaults today. Expose as user settings (e.g. fast for local Ollama, conservative for cloud) — separate UX task.
acceptance_criteria: Integration tests against ConduitInferenceProvider with stubbed Conduit failures: each AIError case produces the expected AgentError. OntologyAgentServiceError.userFacingMessage returns 'API key rejected' / 'rate limited' / 'token limit' / 'billing' messages for the corresponding paths. Manual verify: triggering an invalid API key shows the 'API key rejected, check OneApp Settings' message instead of the raw Conduit description.

title: Raise default maxIterations and add soft-limit warning hook
description: Swarm AgentConfiguration.maxIterations defaults to 10 (Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Core/AgentConfiguration.swift line 39, 182). At the cap, ReActAgent throws AgentError.maxIterationsExceeded — execution aborts and all turn output is lost (no graceful synthesis). Lingo's typical inspect→propose→validate→refine→apply flow eats 6-8+ tool calls (each tool call burns one ReAct iteration), so the default is too tight. Bump to 20-25 and install a RunHooks onIterationStart observer that emits a UI warning at 80% utilization so users know to wrap up before a hard throw.
design:
Files: Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Core/AgentConfiguration.swift (default value reference, read-only); Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Core/RunHooks.swift (onIterationStart hook contract); Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Agents/ReActAgent.swift (throw site at line ~394); OneApp/SwarmAgent/AgentService.swift (BaseAgentService.startConversation — passes AgentConfiguration to ReActAgent); OneApps/Ontology/Agent/OntologyAgentService.swift (handleAgentEvent — already shows max-iterations errors).

Approach:
1. Expose maxIterations on the SwarmAgent facade. Add a maxIterations parameter to BaseAgentService.startConversation (defaulting to 25) so plugins can tune per use case. Forward to AgentConfiguration.default.maxIterations(value).
2. In the new RunHooks adapter from one-azz.1, observe onIterationStart(number:). When number >= 0.8 * maxIterations, emit a transcript warning row 'Lingo is running low on reasoning steps (N of M used). Consider narrowing the request.'
3. Keep the existing maxIterationsExceeded error handling in OntologyAgentServiceError.userFacingMessage; just adjust the user-facing message to reflect the new default.

Depends on one-azz.1 (the RunHooks adapter is the cleanest place to install the soft-limit observer; if RunHooks lands first, this is a 30-line change).
acceptance_criteria: BaseAgentService accepts a maxIterations parameter; default raised to 25. RunHooks-based recorder emits a transcript warning when iteration usage crosses 80%. Integration test: agent that runs to iteration 20 emits the warning event; agent that runs to 25 throws the existing maxIterationsExceeded error. OntologyAgentService user-facing message text updated to reflect the new default.

title: Surface per-turn token usage in Lingo transcript
description: InferenceResponse.TokenUsage flows through onLLMEnd in the agent's hooks pipeline (see ReActAgent.swift line ~336). The diagnostic recorder ignores it; LingoTranscriptItem doesn't surface it to the chat UI. For a tool that calls LLMs aggressively, exposing per-turn token usage and cost in the transcript is a small change with real value — both for users tracking spend and for engineers debugging token-bloat issues.
design:
Files: Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Core/InferenceResponse.swift (TokenUsage shape); Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Core/RunHooks.swift (onLLMEnd usage parameter); OneApps/Ontology/Agent/LingoTranscriptItem.swift; OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo/LingoChatView.swift (the row rendering).

Approach (depends on Task 1 RunHooks landing):
1. In the new RunHooks-based recorder, capture TokenUsage from each onLLMEnd.
2. Aggregate per turn (a turn may make multiple LLM calls) into a per-turn total: prompt tokens, completion tokens, total tokens, model name.
3. Add a tokenUsage field to LingoTranscriptItem (or a new .usage transcript kind).
4. LingoChatView renders the usage as small dimmed text under each assistant turn ('123 in / 456 out · 579 total · gpt-5.4'). Cost requires per-model rates which are out of scope for this task — leave as a follow-up.
5. Also surface in the diagnostic JSONL trace.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end manual verify: send a Lingo turn, see the per-turn usage row appear under the assistant message. Snapshot test on LingoChatView for the usage row layout. Diagnostic JSONL trace contains usage records.

title: Replace prompt-only Lingo schema-change rules with output guardrails
description: LingoSystemPrompt enforces 'call propose_schema_change before any apply tool' and 'TypeQL must parse before being shown to the user' via natural-language instructions to the model. Models violate these instructions. Swarm.OutputGuardrail and per-tool preconditions enforce the same rules deterministically — failed turns return a structured error to the model rather than producing invalid state.
design:
Files: Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Guardrails/ (input/output guardrail protocols); OneApps/Ontology/Agent/LingoSystemPrompt.swift; OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/SchemaEvolutionTools.swift (apply_schema_delta, propose_schema_change); OneApp/SwarmAgent/AgentService.swift (constructor for ReActAgent — needs to forward guardrails).

Approach:
1. Add an outputGuardrails: [any OneAgentOutputGuardrail] = [] parameter to BaseAgentService.startConversation; forward to ReActAgent.
2. Author Lingo-specific guardrails:
   - ApplyRequiresPendingProposalGuardrail: if a turn ended with apply_schema_delta but viewModel.lingoEngineeringHierarchyProposal == nil, fail the turn with a structured error directing the model to call propose_schema_change first.
   - TypeQLMustParseGuardrail: any propose_schema_change argument must round-trip through TypeQLParser.parse(...) before the proposal is shown to the user; on failure, ask the model to retry with a corrected TypeQL block.
3. Move the corresponding system-prompt rules to comments referencing the guardrails (so future authors don't re-add the prompt-only enforcement).
4. Tools themselves should also do their own pre-condition checks — guardrails are for 'shape of the entire turn'; tool-level checks catch direct violations inside a single tool call.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test: agent that calls apply_schema_delta without a pending proposal is blocked by the guardrail and the failure is surfaced as a model-readable error. Test: malformed TypeQL in propose_schema_change fails the parse-before-show guardrail. The corresponding instructions in LingoSystemPrompt are removed; the comments reference the guardrail types.

title: Wrap OntologyMemoryCorpus as a Swarm.Memory and fix Wax round-tripping
description: OntologyMemoryCorpus is a hand-rolled retriever surfaced via the search_ontology_memory tool. The system prompt explicitly instructs the model to call the tool, which the model regularly forgets. Original plan was to migrate to Swarm.VectorMemory + HybridMemory, but research shows that's the wrong direction: Swarm.VectorMemory is in-memory only (no persistence, no metadata dict, no fingerprint/rebuild gating), and HybridMemory has no vector tier. The corpus already does Wax-backed persistence + provenance metadata + manifest fingerprinting, and tests lock those behaviors in. Right approach: wrap OntologyMemoryCorpus as a Swarm.Memory conformer so retrieval gets injected into the prompt's 'Relevant Context from Memory:' section automatically, drop the system-prompt instruction, and fix two Wax misuses while we're in there.
design:
Files: OneApps/Ontology/Backend/OntologyMemoryCorpus.swift, OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/OntologyMemoryTools.swift, OneApps/Ontology/Agent/LingoSystemPrompt.swift, OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/OntologyMemoryCorpusTests.swift, Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Memory/AgentMemory.swift (the Memory protocol), Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Integration/Wax/WaxMemory.swift, OneApp/SwarmAgent/MuseRuntime.swift (DefaultMuseTextMemoryStore.recall string-parse path), OneApp/SwarmAgent/Facade/OneAgentMemoryConfig.swift.

Approach (3 sub-parts):

A) Adapter-wrap the corpus as a Swarm.Memory conformer. New type OntologyCorpusMemory: Memory { context(for query: String, tokenLimit: Int) async -> String { ... corpus.search(...) ... format } }. Implement add/allMessages/clear as no-ops or minimal pass-throughs (the corpus is read-only at retrieval time; writes happen via the rebuild path).

B) Extend OneAgentMemoryConfig with a .ontologyHybrid(short: Int) case that returns HybridMemory(shortTerm: ConversationMemory(maxMessages: short), longTerm: OntologyCorpusMemory(corpus: ...)). Lingo opts in via the existing OntologyAgentService.startConversation(systemPrompt:tools:).

C) Drop the system-prompt instruction 'Call search_ontology_memory for relevant gist and installed-package modeling precedent' from LingoSystemPrompt.swift. The tool stays for explicit deep-dive queries the user asks for, but retrieval is now implicit through the Memory channel.

Wax misuses to fix in the same change:
- WaxMemory.context(for:tokenLimit:) currently serializes RAGContext.Item structures into a string '[kind frame:... score:... sources:...] text'; OntologyMemoryCorpus.provenance(from:) and DefaultMuseTextMemoryStore.recall then parse that string back into structured fields. Replace with structured access: WaxMemory should return a typed value (or keep the string for the Memory protocol surface, but expose a separate structured accessor that the Ontology corpus consumes directly without round-tripping).
- OntologyMemoryCorpus stores provenance as a JSON-encoded 'OntologyMemoryMetadata: {...}' line baked into the indexed body (OntologyMemoryCorpus.swift line ~288-303). Wax has a native metadata: [String: String] parameter on remember(_:metadata:) that is plumbed through. Migrate provenance into Wax's native metadata field; the indexed body becomes pure ontology text.

Load-bearing semantics that MUST be preserved (research-confirmed; tests lock these in):
- Provenance round-trip with all 13 fields (record_kind, package_name, package_version, source_url, git_commit, git_tag, schema_relative_path, checksum, type_label, kind, domain, view_key, installed_database).
- The verification block (cross-checking provenance.typeLabel against viewModel.currentSchemaLabelKinds()) and source_of_truth_policy string in the search_ontology_memory tool result.
- Fingerprint + manifest rebuild gating; the empty-recall self-heal force-rebuild path.
- OntologyMemoryPackageFilter (only-installed/version-matched packages get indexed).
- Per-type record granularity (entity/relation/attribute/function each its own record with typeLabel/kind/domain).
acceptance_criteria: Two-turn integration test: turn 1 asks about ontology X; the model receives X's package-provenance precedent in the prompt's 'Relevant Context from Memory:' section WITHOUT having explicitly called search_ontology_memory. The system prompt instruction telling the model to call search_ontology_memory has been removed. Existing OntologyMemoryCorpusTests still pass. Wax round-tripping replaced with structured access (no string-parse path remains in OntologyMemoryCorpus.provenance(from:) or DefaultMuseTextMemoryStore.recall). Provenance now uses Wax's native metadata field; indexed text bodies no longer contain the 'OntologyMemoryMetadata: {...}' JSON line. The 'design precedent vs live TypeDB drift' semantic distinction is preserved.

title: Persist Lingo conversation sessions across app restart
description: BaseAgentService.startConversation creates a new InMemorySession() on every call (OneApp/SwarmAgent/AgentService.swift line ~98). Closing Lingo loses the entire conversation history. For an ontology-modeling tool where sessions can span hours and multiple proposal-validate-apply cycles, persistence is a real UX gap.
design:
Files: Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Memory/PersistentSession.swift; Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Memory/SwiftDataMemory.swift; OneApp/SwarmAgent/AgentService.swift; OneApp/SwarmAgent/Facade/OneAgentMemoryConfig.swift.

Approach:
1. Extend OneAgentMemoryConfig with a .persistentConversation(maxMessages: Int, sessionID: String) case. Plugins that want fresh-each-time keep .conversation; Lingo opts into .persistentConversation.
2. In BaseAgentService.makeMemory and a new makeSession helper, branch on the config and construct PersistentSession backed by SwiftDataMemory under FileManager applicationSupportDirectory + plugin-specific subdir (e.g. Library/Application Support/com.gamma.ontology/lingo-sessions/<sessionID>.store).
3. Key the session ID off LingoDiagnosticSessionRecorder.sessionID so persistent session and JSONL trace co-locate.
4. UI: Lingo gets a 'resume previous conversation' affordance in LingoRootView (separate UX task; this task only delivers the storage layer + session restoration on startConversation).
5. Migration: first launch with no prior sessions — OK, empty store. Schema change in SwiftDataMemory — Swarm should provide a migration path; verify before shipping.
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start a Lingo session, send 3 turns, force-quit the app, relaunch with the same sessionID — turn-2 prompt to the model includes the prior 3 user/assistant pairs in Conversation History. Integration test: BaseAgentService persistence round-trip with a stub provider, asserting prompt content survives a service teardown + new service over the same store URL.

title: Wire Swarm OSLogTracer into BaseAgentService
description: BaseAgentService constructs ReActAgent without a tracer (OneApp/SwarmAgent/AgentService.swift line ~102). Swarm ships OSLogTracer (Apple-platforms-only, with privacy annotations). For Lingo's behaviorally rich agent runs the tracer would automatically log thoughts, action calls, observations, iterations, and errors to Console.app — observability we currently rely on transcript JSONL files for.
design:
Files: Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Observability/OSLogTracer.swift; Vendor/Swarm/Sources/Swarm/Observability/Tracer.swift (protocol); OneApp/SwarmAgent/AgentService.swift.

Approach:
1. Add a tracer parameter to BaseAgentService.startConversation as (any Tracer)? = nil — but expose via the facade as OneAgentTracer with a default OSLog-backed implementation behind #if canImport(os).
2. ReActAgent's existing tracing helper (TracingHelper) emits traceStart/traceThought/traceComplete/traceError. With OSLogTracer attached, each fires an os_log entry under the subsystem com.gamma.<plugin>.
3. Default-on for Lingo: OntologyAgentService passes a tracer with subsystem com.gamma.ontology category Lingo (matches the existing Logger).
4. Privacy: OSLogTracer must default user content to .private, tool names to .public, model names to .public, error reasons to .public — confirm this in OSLogTracer source first; if not the default, wrap it.
acceptance_criteria: mise run dev → Console.app shows agent thought/action/observation entries under com.gamma.ontology subsystem. Test asserts tracer is non-nil after startConversation when wired. Privacy annotations verified by reading os_log outputs in Console (no PII leaked).

title: Land Swarm/Wax framework usage upgrades for Lingo
description: Lingo currently uses BaseAgentService/ReActAgent through the SwarmAgent facade but bypasses or duplicates several Swarm features that would simplify the code and improve UX. This feature collects six targeted upgrades — each shipped as its own task — that bring Lingo onto the supported framework paths: hooks-based event recording, OSLogTracer, persistent sessions, Swarm VectorMemory in place of OntologyMemoryCorpus, output guardrails for the proposal-first workflow, and surfacing token-usage telemetry. Discovered while reviewing the conversation-memory regression (closed: one-0um). Items are ordered by leverage; each can ship independently.
design:
Parent epic: one-2xg.15. Each child task lives under this feature.

Guiding constraints:
- Plugins must continue to import only SwarmAgent (no direct Swarm/Conduit/Wax imports per one-2xg.31).
- BaseAgentService is the canonical default; changes that benefit other plugins (Muse, VibeMachine) belong there, not in OntologyAgentService.
- All changes are non-breaking to the AgentService protocol surface unless explicitly versioned.
- TDD: red-green for each task; integration tests live in OneApp/SwarmAgentTests/AgentServiceTests.swift for platform-layer changes and OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests for Lingo-specific behavior.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 child tasks closed. Lingo conversation flow validated end-to-end: tracing visible in Console.app, session persists across app restart, ontology-memory retrieval is implicit (no manual search_ontology_memory calls required for precedent surfacing), apply_schema_delta refuses without a pending proposal, transcript shows per-turn token usage.

title: OntologyTests: StickyEndpointTests fails when persisted port (e.g. 64156) is in use by a previous run or live MCP server
description:
OntologyTests/MCP/StickyEndpointTests.swift:8 'endpoint is persisted on first start and reused across restart' fails with .portConflict(port: 64156, reason: 'Address already in use'). The test by design exercises the sticky-endpoint behavior — the lifecycle persists a port on first start and rebinds the same port on restart. When that port is still bound by a prior leaked OntologyMCPServerLifecycle (or by an unrelated process happening to hold it), the test surfaces it as a real failure.

Two reasonable fixes:
1. Test isolation — give each StickyEndpointTests case a fresh, unique metadata URL (already done) AND an out-of-the-way port range that the test selects dynamically before persisting, so first-start picks a guaranteed-free port instead of whatever was last persisted.
2. Pre-test cleanup — kill any process bound to the persisted port before starting.

Hits intermittently when a developer is running the OneApp sandbox alongside tests, since the live OntologyMCPServer can be holding the persisted port. Reproduced 2026-04-29 with 'mise run dev --sandbox' running concurrently.
acceptance_criteria: StickyEndpointTests passes reliably when run alongside a live OneApp sandbox or another OntologyTests run that previously reserved the persisted port.
notes: Same flake also surfaces in OntologyPluginTests ('activate registers ontology UI without remote package bootstrap') and TypeDBSliceTests ('OntologyPlugin registers the TypeDB module without requiring a TypeDB service') when port 64057 is held by a running OneApp/MCP instance. The fix should generalize to any test that activates an OntologyPlugin while a sibling app holds the persisted MCP port.

title: OntologyTests: LiveTypeDBFixture trusts directory existence; corrupted clone yields misleading 'gh auth login' error
description:
OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/Support/LiveTypeDBFixture.swift:228 decides between 'fetch' and 'cold-clone' paths with a bare `fm.fileExists(atPath: url.path)` check. If the directory exists but the clone is half-complete (interrupted earlier run, stale TMPDIR cleanup), .git/HEAD and .git/config can be missing while .git/objects, .git/refs, etc. survive. `git fetch` then fails with 'fatal: not a git repository' (exit 128). The fixture's error handler at line 233-243 unconditionally surfaces 'Auth may have expired — run gh auth login' as the remediation, so 40+ tests fail with the wrong diagnosis. Real cause is repo corruption, not auth.

Reproduced on this machine: `gh auth status` returns OK; `/var/folders/.../one-ontology-test-repos/ontology-gist/.git/` is missing HEAD and config. `git -C ... fetch` exits 128 with 'fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git'.
acceptance_criteria: OntologyTests run cleanly without active gh auth. Either: skipped tests are clearly skipped (not reported as failing), OR a checked-in fixture path makes the gist clone work fully offline, OR the test bootstrap pre-warms a stable cache once and reuses it.
notes: Fix in commit (pending): validate the clone via `git -C path rev-parse --git-dir` before reusing; for fixture-owned paths, blow away corrupted directories and re-clone; for ONTOLOGY_*_REPO overrides refuse to rm -rf the developer's working tree and surface a clear repair message; tighten the fetch-failed error message so it lists likely causes (network, auth, deleted remote) instead of leading with auth.
close_reason: Fixed in 9f940c0d. LiveTypeDBFixture.refreshRepo now validates the clone via 'git -C path rev-parse --git-dir' before reusing; corrupted fixture-owned clones are wiped and re-cloned cleanly; developer ONTOLOGY_*_REPO overrides are protected with a 'repair manually' error rather than rm -rf; fetch-failed messages list real causes (network, auth, deleted remote) instead of leading with auth. Verified: post-fix Ontology test run went from 298 passing / 41 failing → 337 passing / 2 failing. Remaining failures are tracked separately as one-2xg.33 (MCP error code) and one-2xg.35 (sticky endpoint port collision).

title: EuroRack swift-nio explicit-modules cache reuses stale CNIOOpenBSD pcm after derived-data wipe
description: After a fresh derived-data wipe, building EuroRack via mise often fails with: error: missing required module 'CNIOOpenBSD'. EuroRackManagerKit imports NIO transitively via container-libs. Empirically the explicit-modules pcm cache for CNIOOpenBSD ends up referencing a stale or missing path. .mise/tasks/build.sh today papers over this with build_scheme_with_known_stale_module_retry, which clears Wax/NIO/CNIO* caches and retries once. one-2xg.32 originally hypothesized this was caused by SwiftPM-built Wax modules; with the SwarmAgent xcframework migration that hypothesis was tested and disproven — the fragility persists and is unrelated to Swarm/Wax. Root cause is in the EuroRack/swift-nio explicit-modules path. Fix the root cause and remove the retry helper from build.sh.
design: Investigate where the stale CNIOOpenBSD path comes from. Possible suspects: (1) module-cache.path values baked into NIOPosix/NIOCore swiftmodule files at SwiftPM build time, pinned to a specific derived-data subdirectory; (2) -fbuild-session-file conflict between EuroRack's xcodebuild invocation and prior session state; (3) ContainerLibs prebuilt artifact carrying a precompiled module reference. Reproduce on a fresh derived-data wipe with no other concurrent xcodebuild, capture which precompiled module file Clang is trying to read, and trace its path resolution. Once root cause is identified, remove build_scheme_with_known_stale_module_retry and clear_stale_swift_module_state from .mise/tasks/build.sh.
acceptance_criteria: mise run build app and mise run build EuroRack succeed from a clean derived-data wipe without the retry helper. build_scheme_with_known_stale_module_retry and clear_stale_swift_module_state are deleted from .mise/tasks/build.sh. The build_oneapp_with_eurorack flow uses plain build_scheme for EuroRack.

title: Lingo Type Editor arrow keys should move active row
design: Add keyboard handling to the fixed Lingo Type Editor table so up/down arrows select the previous/next selectable row and update the existing inspector selection. Avoid stealing arrow keys from the chat input when focus is in the input field.
acceptance_criteria: With focus in the Lingo Type Editor, Down selects the next row and Up selects the previous row. Selection updates the inspector. Chat input history behavior remains separate.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Lingo Type Editor duplicates Schema proposal rows
design: Remove the second non-actionable Schema proposal row from the generated Lingo Type Editor model. Keep at most one top-level proposal/root row if it helps orientation; otherwise start with concrete domains/types/relations. Ensure custom TypeQL fallback rows do not duplicate the root.
acceptance_criteria: A proposal with custom TypeQL renders no duplicate 'Schema proposal' entries. The row list contains useful schema nodes and sections only.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Inspector trace file value is hard to copy
design: Add an explicit copy action next to the diagnostic trace file path in the Lingo inspector. Use NSPasteboard or the project clipboard helper if one exists. Keep the visible path for inspection, but do not rely on text selection as the only copy path.
acceptance_criteria: When a trace file path exists, the inspector shows a copy control. Activating it places the exact path on the pasteboard. Missing trace file state remains readable and does not show a misleading copy action.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Lingo Type Editor shows unnecessary relationship toggles
design: Remove the owns/plays/relations toggle controls from the Lingo Type Editor toolbar. The editor should show the proposed schema shape directly without filter switches that do not materially help review. Keep the filter/search field if useful.
acceptance_criteria: The Lingo Type Editor toolbar no longer renders owns, plays, or relations toggles. The proposal rows still include relevant owns/plays/relates children where applicable. Existing row selection behavior remains intact.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Wire Muse memory plumbing for domain corpora
description: Expose shared Muse/Wax memory plumbing without moving ontology-specific corpus policy into Muse.
design: Extend Muse/SwarmAgent only enough for plugins to create or resolve Wax-backed memory stores in a consistent app storage location with shared provider/configuration behavior. Keep corpus ownership in domain plugins. Lingo owns ontology memory contents and retrieval policy; Producer can later own PRD/specification memory contents and retrieval policy. Avoid direct plugin imports of Wax; continue routing shared types through SwarmAgent.framework.
acceptance_criteria:
- Domain plugins can obtain or create a Wax-backed memory store through Muse/SwarmAgent without importing Wax directly
- Muse does not define ontology-specific tools, prompts, schemas, or chunking rules
- Lingo uses the shared plumbing for its Ontology-owned corpus
- Existing SwarmAgent.framework dependency rule remains intact
- Tests or build configuration checks prevent direct plugin dependency on Wax
close_reason: Already implemented. Shared plumbing lives at OneApp/SwarmAgent/MuseRuntime.swift: MuseRuntimeProviding protocol exposes openTextMemoryStore(named:reset:) returning any MuseTextMemoryStore. MusePlugin registers MusePlatformService as MuseRuntimeProviding and forwards to DefaultMuseRuntime. OntologyMemoryCorpus consumes 'any MuseRuntimeProviding'; no plugin in OneApps/ imports Wax directly (verified by grep). Muse defines no ontology-specific tools, prompts, schemas, or chunking — corpus content stays in Ontology. SwarmAgent.framework boundary intact.

title: Separate feedback diagnostics from internal thinking
description: Raw diagnostics record internal thinking content, which is useful for debugging but poor as a manual feedback artifact.
design: Keep raw trace capability if needed, but add the compact/manual feedback summary without internal thinking text. Mark thinking events as debug-only or omit them from summary output.
acceptance_criteria: The feedback summary artifact contains no internal thinking text while raw JSONL can still include debug trace if intentionally enabled.
close_reason: Fixed proposal refinement and diagnostics regressions: proposal tool now renders arguments, revised proposals replace pending UI state, pending proposals can be re-shown for approval, custom TypeQL is preserved and enriched with VibeEngineeringTask role declarations, diagnostics write plain JSON, and compact summaries omit debug token/thinking noise.

title: Keep sandbox requirement visible during schema evolution turns
description: The reviewed session ran with active_sandbox null while schema evolution discussion continued, making the proposal/apply path ambiguous.
design: When a pending schema evolution request exists and no sandbox is active, keep a visible create/select sandbox affordance in chat and inspector state. Allow conceptual discussion, but do not allow apply/proposal finalization until a sandbox exists.
acceptance_criteria: Starting the engineering hierarchy flow with no sandbox keeps the sandbox affordance visible across follow-up turns. Apply/confirm controls remain disabled until a sandbox is selected or created.
close_reason: Added isLingoSandboxAffordanceRequired and canConfirmLingoProposal derived properties to OntologyViewModel+Lingo.swift; LingoChatView shows a persistent sandbox affordance banner above the input bar across follow-up turns when no sandbox is active; LingoRootView Confirm button is disabled via canConfirmLingoProposal and shows a warning sub-label when affordance is required. Tests in LingoTranscriptTests.swift cover the persistent affordance state, confirm gating, and the apply-path refusal.

title: Flatten SendableValue fields in Lingo diagnostics JSON
description: Diagnostic fields are encoded as Swift enum payloads like {"string":{"_0":...}}, which makes manual review hard.
design: Before writing diagnostic fields, convert SendableValue values into primitive JSON dictionaries, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null. Preserve enough type information where needed in event names, not enum-wrapper payloads.
acceptance_criteria: New diagnostic JSONL events contain plain JSON fields. Existing recorder tests validate representative nested dictionaries and arrays.
close_reason: Fixed proposal refinement and diagnostics regressions: proposal tool now renders arguments, revised proposals replace pending UI state, pending proposals can be re-shown for approval, custom TypeQL is preserved and enriched with VibeEngineeringTask role declarations, diagnostics write plain JSON, and compact summaries omit debug token/thinking noise.

title: Write compact Lingo session summaries for manual feedback
description: The raw session trace is too noisy for manual feedback: 1768 lines, mostly output tokens and partial tool-call fragments.
design: Extend LingoDiagnosticSessionRecorder to write or derive a compact per-session summary containing user turns, generated UI parts, widget actions, tool calls, failures, final outputs, and improvement signals. Keep raw JSONL for deep debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Every Lingo session produces a compact summary artifact next to the JSONL or through a deterministic export command. The summary is readable without decoding token streams. Tests cover summary generation from a real JSONL fixture.
close_reason: Fixed proposal refinement and diagnostics regressions: proposal tool now renders arguments, revised proposals replace pending UI state, pending proposals can be re-shown for approval, custom TypeQL is preserved and enriched with VibeEngineeringTask role declarations, diagnostics write plain JSON, and compact summaries omit debug token/thinking noise.

title: Return graceful Lingo response when max iterations would be exceeded
description: The user-facing result of the failed final turn was only 'Agent exceeded maximum iterations (10)'.
design: Intercept AgentError.maxIterationsExceeded in LingoAgentService/ViewModel and render a structured error/partial-progress transcript item. Include tools attempted, last useful schema facts, and next manual action.
acceptance_criteria: Max-iteration failures produce a readable transcript item with partial progress and no raw internal error as the only response. Diagnostics still record the original error.
close_reason: Fixed in Lingo manual verification follow-up: registered propose_schema_change, stopped transcript scratchpad streaming, added useful max-iteration copy, and updated the hierarchy proposal to the structural VibeEngineeringTask model.

title: Extract Muse platform plugin
description: Extract the current shared GammaAgent framework capability into a Muse platform plugin that provides AI runtime services to domain assistant plugins while keeping ontology/document workflows plugin-owned.
design:
Design reference:
- planning-n-design/muse-lingo-generative-ui-architecture.md

Implementation approach:
- Treat Muse as a platform plugin analogous to EuroRack and GhosttyTerminal.
- GammaCore should contain only narrow service/protocol contracts needed for consumers to discover and use Muse.
- Muse owns provider/model configuration, key storage, Swarm integration, session lifecycle, memory plumbing, diagnostics/transcripts, and shared AI settings UI.
- Ontology continues to own Lingo, TypeQL tools, TypeQL proposal widgets, ontology memory, and sandbox/TypeDB workflows.
- Producer should later consume Muse for document/spec authoring assistants while owning document tools, rendered document UI, validators, and deconstruction into TypeDB.
- Preserve existing plugin consumers during migration; avoid forcing Lingo implementation to import broad Muse internals.
- Decide which current GammaAgent types remain in a framework for ABI sharing and which move behind Muse services.

Likely areas:
- OneApp/GammaAgent/
- OneApp/GammaCore/ service contracts
- new OneApps/Muse/ plugin
- OneApps/Ontology/Agent/
- OneApps/VibeMachine/Agent/
- OneApp/OneApp/Views/Settings/AssistantSettingsHostView.swift
acceptance_criteria:
- Muse platform plugin exists and activates through the normal Gamma plugin lifecycle.
- Shared AI provider/settings/session services are discoverable through GammaCore-level contracts or named services.
- Ontology/Lingo consumes Muse services without owning provider configuration implementation details.
- VibeMachine/Producer agent consumers have a migration path or compatibility adapter.
- GammaCore does not gain ontology- or document-specific workflow logic.
- Existing provider settings and Lingo sessions continue to work after migration.
- Tests cover Muse service registration, consumer lookup, and graceful behavior when Muse is unavailable.
notes:
Implemented first Muse refactor slice: added Muse platform plugin, GammaAgent Muse runtime contract/default runtime, moved assistant settings from host to Muse settings contribution, wired Ontology/Lingo and VibeMachine design chat to consume MuseRuntimeProviding with local fallback for tests/previews. Verified with mise run build Muse, mise run build Ontology, mise run build VibeMachine, and focused OneApp settings test.
Vendored Wax under Vendor/Wax as a git submodule at aeb28ac8e7386c42bb229d5a1d23aea245e5f7bb and updated Vendor/Swarm to resolve Wax via the local vendored path. Added MuseTests for Muse plugin activation/service/settings registration and wired mise run test Muse. Added EuroRack project Package.resolved so resolved-only xcodebuild paths can build host dependencies without drifting package resolution. Verified with mise run build Muse, mise run test Muse, mise run build Ontology, and mise run build VibeMachine. Current assessment: shared Swarm/Wax kits are not required for this slice, but remain the right escalation if plugin packaging later shows duplicated runtime symbols or Xcode lockfile friction.
Accounted for multi-plugin Swarm exposure now: documented GammaAgent.framework as the single shared Swarm/Conduit/Wax ABI carrier beneath Muse and added OneApp guardrail tests that fail if plugin projects link Vendor/Swarm, Vendor/Wax, Swarm, Wax, or Conduit directly, or if plugin Swift sources import Swarm/Wax/Conduit instead of GammaAgent. Verified with mise run build app and mise run test app after an initial Xcode explicit-module cache miss on CNIOOpenBSD during the first test prebuild.
Renamed the shared third-party agent-stack framework from GammaAgent.framework to SwarmAgent.framework to reflect that it wraps/re-exports vendored Swarm, Wax, Conduit, and related runtime types rather than One-owned Muse behavior. Updated host and plugin project links, Swift imports, tests, docs, and guardrail assertions. Muse remains the platform plugin/service layer on top of SwarmAgent. Preserved the old keychain service string com.oneapp.gamma-agent for saved provider-key compatibility. Verified with mise run build Muse, mise run test Muse, mise run test app, mise run build Ontology, and mise run build VibeMachine.
Updated assistant keychain namespace from the old GammaAgent service name to com.oneapp.muse. Producer remains aligned with the shared Muse assistant credential namespace; SwarmAgent remains the vendored runtime/framework boundary rather than the persisted product identity. Verified with mise run test app and mise run build Producer.

title: Update Lingo prompt for proposal-first TypeQL flow
description: Update LingoSystemPrompt so schema-design requests produce structured TypeQL proposals before apply, treat UI confirmation as the apply boundary, and understand the Muse/Lingo architecture decisions documented in planning-n-design/muse-lingo-generative-ui-architecture.md.
design:
Design reference:
- planning-n-design/muse-lingo-generative-ui-architecture.md

Implementation approach:
- Update OneApps/Ontology/Agent/LingoSystemPrompt.swift from version one-2xg.11 to a new version tied to this flow.
- Teach Lingo to call propose_schema_change for schema-design requests before applying any schema change.
- The proposal payload must include full TypeQL text as the canonical proposal, plus summary, affected labels, motivations, assumptions, and optional reverse TypeQL.
- Explicitly mention TypeQL functions and structs as first-class schema definables; Lingo must not reduce proposals to only entities/relations/attributes.
- Forbid apply_schema_delta until the user confirms the pending proposal through the UI.
- Treat ontology repo memory as canonical design precedent and TypeDB tools as current runtime state. If memory and live TypeDB disagree, surface drift.
- Add examples for the Engineering hierarchy request that show proposal-first behavior.

Relevant files likely involved:
- OneApps/Ontology/Agent/LingoSystemPrompt.swift
- OneApps/Ontology/Agent/Tools/SchemaEvolutionTools.swift once propose_schema_change exists
- OneApps/Ontology/OntologyTests/LingoAgentTests.swift or focused prompt contract tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- LingoSystemPrompt describes propose_schema_change and proposal-first schema-design behavior.
- Prompt explicitly forbids apply_schema_delta before UI confirmation.
- Prompt tells Lingo to propose full TypeQL, including functions/structs when needed.
- Prompt distinguishes ontology repo memory from live TypeDB runtime state.
- Tests or prompt-contract assertions cover the required instructions and Engineering hierarchy example.
close_reason: Updated LingoSystemPrompt for proposal-first schema evolution, full TypeQL payloads including functions and structs, UI-confirmation apply boundary, repo-memory versus live-TypeDB source-of-truth rules, and Engineering hierarchy example coverage.

title: Document Muse and Lingo generative UI architecture
description: Capture the Muse platform boundary, Lingo ownership model, TypeQL proposal contract, inspector split, prompt contract, transcript feedback loop, and implementation order in planning-n-design/muse-lingo-generative-ui-architecture.md.
design:
Document location:
- planning-n-design/muse-lingo-generative-ui-architecture.md

The document must record:
- Muse as the shared AI platform subsystem name.
- Muse as a future platform plugin, not a domain assistant.
- Lingo as the Ontology-owned assistant built on Muse.
- Producer/document assistants as Producer-owned domain assistants built on Muse.
- TypeQL proposal contract: propose_schema_change is Ontology-owned, canonical payload is full TypeQL text, Swift metadata extraction is best effort, TypeDB sandbox validation is authoritative until Rust parser support lands.

title: Lingo inspector mirrors EuroRack modules inspector pattern
description: Move cumulative Lingo state inspection into a native SwiftUI inspector panel following the EuroRack ModulesRootView/ModuleDetailView pattern: chat remains the conversation and proposal surface, while active sandbox, decided entities, schema state, intents, and validation state are reflected in an inspector.
design:
Implementation approach:
- Follow the EuroRack modules route pattern in OneApps/EuroRack/Sources/Views/Modules/ModulesRootView.swift and ModuleDetailView.swift. Use SwiftUI .inspector(isPresented:) on the Lingo root, a toolbar info.circle button, Cmd-I keyboard shortcut, and .inspectorColumnWidth with comparable min/ideal/max sizing.
- The inspector is the cumulative state surface. It should reflect concrete decisions as they happen: active sandbox/database, proposed/accepted ontology concepts, new entities/relations/attributes, pending proposal state, applied ChangeIntent records, validation status, and transcript diagnostic session ID/path when available.
- Chat remains the event/proposal/action surface. It should render request understanding, proposal review, confirm/apply progress, validation evidence, and revision events inline. Do not force long-lived schema/timeline inspection into transcript-only widgets.
- Reuse the existing CandidateSchemaView, IntentTimelineView, and SandboxSelectorView presentation logic where appropriate, but compose them as inspector sections/tabs instead of persistent side panes around chat.
- Inspector implementation should match EuroRack conventions: empty state when no selection/context exists, compact header, tab or section navigation, restrained card styling, route-active toolbar item only, and no nested card-heavy layout.
- The Lingo root should become a chat-first content area plus inspector, not a three-pane HSplitView.

Relevant files likely involved:
- OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo/LingoRootView.swift
- OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo/CandidateSchemaView.swift
- OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo/IntentTimelineView.swift
- OneApps/Ontology/Views/Lingo/SandboxSelectorView.swift

- OneApps/EuroRack/Sources/Views/Modules/ModuleDetailView.swift as the inspector reference.

- Lingo uses a native SwiftUI inspector panel rather than persistent side panes for cumulative state.
- The inspector can be toggled with the toolbar info.circle button and Cmd-I, following EuroRack ModulesRootView behavior.
- The inspector has bounded column width comparable to EuroRack modules inspector.
- Active sandbox/database, decided/proposed concepts, current schema snapshot, intent log, and validation status are visible in the inspector as state changes.
- Chat still contains event-shaped generative UI for proposals, apply progress, validation evidence, and revisions.
- Existing side-pane renderers are reused or adapted instead of duplicating schema/timeline logic in multiple places.
- Focused view/presentation tests or previews cover empty, active sandbox, proposal pending, and applied hierarchy inspector states.
notes: Design reference: planning-n-design/muse-lingo-generative-ui-architecture.md. Inspector follows EuroRack ModulesRootView/ModuleDetailView conventions and owns cumulative state inspection.
