title: Git-repo version resolver for ontology packages
description: Given (packageName, version), resolve the TypeQL contents from the corresponding git ref in the ontology source repo. The result is a ParsedSchema that the Lingo Explorer renders as a live section.
design:
New type: PackageVersionResolver

API:
@MainActor
func resolve(packageName: String, version: String) async throws -> ParsedSchema

Implementation strategy options (decision in task):
(a) git show approach: 'git show <ref>:<package>/package.json' to get manifest, then 'git show <ref>:<package>/<file>.tql' for each schema file. Concatenate, parse, return ParsedSchema. ref = tag like 'package-name-vX.Y.Z' or a content hash recorded in PackageBootstrapRegistry.
(b) Worktree cache: maintain .build/lingo-package-cache/<package>@<version>/ as a git worktree at the right ref; read files normally. Heavier setup but simpler subsequent reads.
(c) Hybrid: first call uses git show; cache parsed result in-memory + on-disk for subsequent calls.

Lean: (a) for V1 of this feature; (c) if profiling shows overhead.

Source repo location: the ontology git repo is checked out somewhere — verify location (likely Resources/Packages or a parallel sibling repo). PackageManager.OntologyPackage.source carries this info (.bundled vs .git).

Cache: in-memory map keyed by (packageName, version). Lifetime: process. Invalidate via explicit invalidate(packageName:version:) — useful if the user pulls upstream and wants Lingo Explorer to reflect.

Error path: if version isn't a known git ref, throw with a clear message ('No version tag/ref for <package>@<version>'); caller falls back to bundled or shows a missing badge.
acceptance_criteria:
- resolve('gist', '1.0.0') returns a ParsedSchema parsed from gist v1.0.0 .tql files.
- resolving a non-existent version throws with a useful error.
- Cache hit on repeated resolve of the same (package, version) — no second git call.
- Manual invalidate clears the cache and re-resolves.
- Result equals what TypeQLParser would produce on the on-disk version when versions match.
close_reason: Implemented sandbox installed-package introspection, loaded package-version resolution with mismatch fallback, sandbox-pinned Lingo Explorer live data, manual refresh, no-sandbox fallback, drift/error indicators, and focused tests.

title: Sandbox installed-packages introspection
description: Build the service that asks the active sandbox 'what ontology packages and versions are installed?' Source of truth for which live packages the Lingo Explorer should render in its sidebar.
design:
New service: SandboxInstalledPackagesService (or a method on existing OntologyTypeDBClient).

API:
struct InstalledPackage { let packageName: String; let version: String }
@MainActor
func installedPackages(in sandbox: SandboxHandle) async throws -> [InstalledPackage]

Implementation: PackageBootstrapRegistry already tracks bootstrap-unit application status per database, including checksums. Likely it knows which package@version was bootstrapped into each database. If yes: read from that registry. If no: query the sandbox's TypeDB metadata directly (each ontology package may store a marker entity like 'OntologyPackageMarker' with name + version attributes — verify pattern during implementation).

Caching: cache per sandbox-id with a short TTL (or invalidate on apply_schema_delta). Cache key: sandbox.name. Cache lives on OntologyViewModel to keep Observable propagation simple.

Edge cases:
- Sandbox has no installed packages: returns empty (rare; gist is required for the tool to work — but the call shouldn't fail).
- Sandbox is unreachable: throws; caller decides to use V1 fallback.
- Versions reported don't match what's on-disk: not this task's problem (drift indicator handled in T4.4).
acceptance_criteria:
- Calling installedPackages(in: sandbox) returns the correct list of (name, version) pairs.
- Result is cached per sandbox; clearing sandbox or applying a schema delta invalidates the cache.
- Unreachable sandbox throws cleanly; caller can detect.
- Tested against fixtures and at least one real sandbox during smoke test.
notes: Continuing after structural proposal editing. Starting with installed-package introspection as the source for sandbox-pinned live data.
close_reason: Implemented sandbox installed-package introspection, loaded package-version resolution with mismatch fallback, sandbox-pinned Lingo Explorer live data, manual refresh, no-sandbox fallback, drift/error indicators, and focused tests.

title: Editor and Explorer sync to shared structural state
description: With structural source of truth in place, ensure the Lingo Type Editor (table) and the Lingo Explorer (tree) both bind to the same proposal structure and reflect each other's edits in real time. Any drift between the two views indicates a bug — both should be wholly derived from the same Parsed* arrays on the proposal.
design:
Audit current sync mechanism:
- LingoTypeEditorPresentation.rows(for:) currently re-parses typeQL. After Feature 3's data refactor, the proposal's typeQL is computed; rows(for:) should bypass the parse and read parsedEntities/etc. directly.

Refactor:
- LingoTypeEditorPresentation reads from proposal.parsedEntities/relations/attributes — single source of truth.
- The Lingo Explorer's visibleLingoExplorerRows ALSO reads from proposal.parsedEntities — same source.
- @Observable propagation: changes to proposal (via applyLingoProposalEdit) trigger SwiftUI invalidation in both views simultaneously.

Live editing test:
- Open Lingo Type Editor and Lingo Explorer side-by-side (split-pane debug build, or sequential: open one, then switch — though they're mutex'd in the chat panel area, so 'side-by-side' may require special test scaffolding).
- Edit a type name in the explorer → switch to editor → verify table shows new name without manual refresh.
- Same for owns/plays/parent edits.

Editor-side editing (if the editor gains edit affordances in this work — verify scope with Feature 3.4-3.5 tasks): ensure editor edits also route through applyLingoProposalEdit, not direct typeQL string manipulation. Single edit pathway.

Tests: snapshot tests verifying both views render consistent representations of the same proposal after each edit op type.
acceptance_criteria:
- An edit made in the explorer is visible in the editor when the user flips to it (no stale typeQL parsed view).
- Conversely (when editor gains edit affordances): edits in the editor reflect in the explorer.
- No duplicate parsing: TypeQLParser is called once on proposal creation; subsequent reads use the structure.
- Both views reference proposal.parsedEntities directly (verified via code review).
- Snapshot tests confirm consistent rendering of both views post-edit.
close_reason: Added structural proposal edit API, Explorer edit controls for rename/parent/docs/remove/owns/plays, transcript edit events, and shared Parsed* state for Explorer and Type Editor.

title: Conversation event emission for widget edits
description: When the user edits a proposal directly in the widget, emit a structured transcript event so the assistant sees the edit on its next turn and can reason about it ('I see you renamed Collection to Aggregate — should I update the engages relation too?'). Without this, AI conversation context drifts as the user edits.
design:
Each LingoProposalEdit application records a transcript entry via existing recordLingoTranscript:

viewModel.recordLingoTranscript(
  kind: .userEdit,  // new kind, or reuse .status with a clear title
  title: 'Edited proposal',
  message: humanReadableSummary(of: edit),
  parts: [.userProposalEdit(LingoProposalEditEvent(proposalID:..., edit:..., timestamp:..., revisionAfter:...))]
)

humanReadableSummary examples:
- .renameType → 'Renamed Collection → Aggregate'
- .changeParent → 'Changed Aggregate parent: Concept → Set'
- .addOwns → 'Added owns: Aggregate has count : integer'
- .removeOwns → 'Removed owns: Aggregate.count'
- .addPlays → 'Added plays: Aggregate plays engages:participant'
- .removePlays → 'Removed plays: Aggregate plays engages:participant'
- .setAnnotation → 'Updated doc on Aggregate'
- .removeType → 'Removed Aggregate from proposal'

LingoProposalEditEvent: new transcript part. Sendable; carries the edit op + timestamp + revision-after. Has its own shape ('ontology.proposalEdit.v1') registered with a small renderer in LingoBuiltinWidgets — a slim card showing the human-readable summary + a 'view in proposal' link.

Agent context: the agent's history-loading code already reads .userEdit / status entries; verify it includes them in the prompt context. If not, extend the relevant context-builder.

Privacy: no edit content is sensitive; events are local-only (no telemetry).
acceptance_criteria:
- Each LingoProposalEdit application produces exactly one transcript event.
- Event is rendered in the chat as a small card with the human-readable summary.
- The assistant's next turn sees the edit in its conversation context (verified by inspecting the agent prompt).
- Multiple rapid edits each produce separate events (not coalesced — explicit history).
- Removing a proposal does not delete its edit history (transcript footprint preserved).
close_reason: Added structural proposal edit API, Explorer edit controls for rename/parent/docs/remove/owns/plays, transcript edit events, and shared Parsed* state for Explorer and Type Editor.

title: In-widget edit UI: rename, change parent, edit docs
description: Add the first tier of edit affordances to the Lingo Explorer's detail panel — type-level edits (rename, change parent, edit @doc annotation, remove type). These are the simplest visually (single-field interactions) and exercise the edit-op API end-to-end.
design:
LingoEntityDetailView (and Relation/Attribute equivalents) gain edit affordances when the type's domain is the proposal domain:

Header section:
- Type name renders as a click-to-edit text field. On commit (Enter / focus loss), validate name is unique within proposal; call applyLingoProposalEdit(.renameType(...)).
- Trash button (top-right) calls applyLingoProposalEdit(.removeType(...)) after confirmation.

Inheritance section (entities + relations only):
- Parent renders as a pill with a chevron. Click opens a picker showing eligible parent types: live entities of the same kind + already-proposed types. Selecting calls applyLingoProposalEdit(.changeParent(...)).
- 'Remove parent' option in the picker calls .changeParent(... newParent: nil).

Documentation section:
- @doc annotation renders as a click-to-edit text area. On commit, applyLingoProposalEdit(.setAnnotation(typeName:..., key: 'doc', value: text)).

Validation feedback:
- Inline error if rename clashes with an existing proposal name: red border + 'Name already exists in this proposal'.
- After successful edit: brief flash on the field (blue → fade) confirming.

Read-only types (live ontology, not proposal): edit affordances are absent. Only the proposal section's types get edit chrome.
acceptance_criteria:
- User clicks the type name → name becomes editable; edits and commits → type renames in the tree and detail view.
- Rename to colliding name shows inline error, leaves original name intact.
- Click parent → picker opens with live + proposed eligible parents; selecting changes parent; tree's inheritance reflects.
- 'Remove parent' option works for entities/relations.
- Edit @doc → annotation updates; detail panel shows new text immediately.
- Trash button → confirmation → type removed from proposal tree.
- Live entities show no edit chrome (verified).
close_reason: Added structural proposal edit API, Explorer edit controls for rename/parent/docs/remove/owns/plays, transcript edit events, and shared Parsed* state for Explorer and Type Editor.

title: In-widget edit UI: add/remove owns and plays
description: Add the second tier of edit affordances — owns and plays clause manipulation. More UI-rich than tier 1 (lists with insert/remove). Exercises the cascading-reference edge cases (e.g., adding an owns of an attribute that doesn't exist yet).
design:
In LingoEntityDetailView (and Relation):

Owns section:
- Each owns row has a trailing × button → applyLingoProposalEdit(.removeOwns(typeName, attribute)).
- '+ Add owns' affordance at the bottom of the section: opens a popover with two options:
  (a) Pick existing attribute: dropdown of attributes (from live ontology + proposal). Cardinality defaults to 1..1; user can edit before commit.
  (b) Create new attribute: prompts for name + valueType; on commit, the proposal gains a new ParsedAttribute and the owns clause referencing it (two structural edits or a compound op).

Plays section (entities + relations playing roles):
- Each plays row has a trailing × → applyLingoProposalEdit(.removePlays(...)).
- '+ Add plays' affordance: popover lets user pick (relation, role) from live + proposed relations.

Visual: minor differences in detail panel for proposal-domain types vs live (proposal types show edit chrome inline; live types don't).

Edge case handling:
- Adding owns of a non-existent attribute name (typed manually, not picked) → allowed; verifier will flag as 'attribute not found'.
- Removing the last plays of a type → no special UI; the section just shows '(none)' afterward.
- Cardinality editing: small inline @card editor (min..max with * support for unbounded).

Compound ops: 'create attribute + add owns' is two LingoProposalEdit calls or a new compound case. Decision deferred to task implementation.
acceptance_criteria:
- × button on an owns row removes the clause; serialized typeQL no longer includes it.
- '+ Add owns' with an existing attribute adds a clause; cardinality respected.
- '+ Add owns' with a new attribute name + valueType creates a new ParsedAttribute under the proposal AND adds the owns clause; both visible in the tree afterward.
- × button on a plays row removes the clause.
- '+ Add plays' opens a picker of live + proposed relations and roles; selection adds the clause.
- Serialized typeQL after edits re-parses to expected structure (round-trip safe).

title: TypeQL serializer with round-trip tests
description: Build TypeQLSerializer (Parsed* → TypeQL string), the inverse of TypeQLParser. Required because once the proposal is structurally canonical, edits regenerate TypeQL on demand. Round-trip tested: parse(serialize(parse(typeql))) must equal parse(typeql) for representative inputs. Whitespace and ordering may differ; structure must be identical.
design:
New file: OneApps/Ontology/Schema/TypeQLSerializer.swift

Surface:
struct TypeQLSerializer {
  func serialize(entities: [ParsedEntity], relations: [ParsedRelation], attributes: [ParsedAttribute]) -> String
}

Output format:
- Top-level 'define' keyword followed by clauses (matching what TypeQLParser accepts as input).
- Attributes first (no deps), entities next, relations last (cleaner read; still parser-accepted).
- Each entity: 'entity Name sub Parent;' followed by 'Name owns attr1 @card(min..max);' and 'Name plays Relation:role;' on subsequent lines.
- @doc('...') annotations rendered in their original form when present.
- Cardinality: omit when default (1..1); render @card(N..M) otherwise; render @card(min..*) for unbounded.

Edge cases:
- Empty proposal → 'define' (or empty string with a comment) — pick one in test design.
- Annotation with embedded quotes — escape correctly.
- Multi-line @doc — preserve newlines per parser's tolerance.

Round-trip test corpus:
- Hand-crafted minimal inputs (single entity, single relation with two roles, single attribute, doc annotations).
- Bundled package contents: gist, beads, vibemachine package .tql files.
- AI-generated proposals captured during V1 testing.
- Property-based test: random structural inputs → serialize → parse → assert structural equality.

Tolerated differences in round-trip:
- Whitespace, comment preservation (comments are stripped by parser anyway).
- Clause ordering within a type declaration (owns/plays order).
- Numeric formatting in @card.

Asserted equalities:
- Set of entities by name + each entity's parent + ownsClauses set + playedRoles set + annotations.
- Same for relations (with parsedRoles set + parentRelation).
- Same for attributes (valueType + annotations).
acceptance_criteria:
- Serializing minimal hand-crafted inputs and re-parsing produces identical Parsed* structures.
- Round-trip works for all bundled package .tql contents (vibemachine, beads, gist, gastown).
- Round-trip works for a captured corpus of 10+ AI-generated proposals from V1 testing.
- Property-based test passes 100+ random structural inputs.
- Output is human-readable (consistent indentation, one statement per line for type declarations) — verified by spot check.
notes: Starting with serializer because structural proposal storage needs a serializer before typeQL can safely become derived.
close_reason: Added TypeQLSerializer with round-trip coverage, taught parser keywordless TypeDB declarations, and made EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart store parsed schema structure with derived TypeQL.

title: Edit operation API on view model
description: Define a typed enum of proposal-edit operations and the OntologyViewModel method that applies them. Operations mutate the proposal's Parsed* structure, recompute typeQL via the serializer, regenerate revision diff against the prior version, and increment the revision counter.
design:
New type LingoProposalEdit:
enum LingoProposalEdit {
  case renameType(typeName: String, newName: String)
  case changeParent(typeName: String, newParent: String?)  // nil = remove sub
  case addOwns(typeName: String, attribute: String, cardinality: Cardinality)
  case removeOwns(typeName: String, attribute: String)
  case addPlays(typeName: String, relation: String, role: String)
  case removePlays(typeName: String, relation: String, role: String)
  case setAnnotation(typeName: String, key: String, value: String?)  // nil = remove
  case removeType(typeName: String)
}

Method on OntologyViewModel (or +Lingo extension):
@MainActor
func applyLingoProposalEdit(_ edit: LingoProposalEdit, to proposalID: String)

Implementation:
1. Look up the proposal by id; if missing, no-op.
2. Apply edit to Parsed* arrays:
   - Rename: scan all entities/relations/attributes for matches; update name, also update references to that name in others' parent/owns/plays where applicable.
   - ChangeParent: update entity.parent (or relation.parentRelation).
   - AddOwns: append a ParsedOwns to the matching entity/relation.
   - RemoveOwns: filter out matching attribute from ownsClauses + ownedAttributes.
   - AddPlays: append a 'plays Relation:role' clause; in the parsed structure, this lives on entity.playedRoles.
   - RemovePlays: filter out.
   - SetAnnotation: set/remove key in annotations dictionary.
   - RemoveType: drop from the appropriate array; also scrub references (other types' parents pointing to the removed name → set to nil, log a warning).
3. Compute new revision diff vs prior structure (LingoProposalRevisionDiff).
4. Increment revision counter; mark prior as superseded.
5. Re-trigger views that bind to the proposal (Observable change propagation).

Edge cases / validation:
- Renaming to a name that already exists in the proposal → return error; do not apply.
- Renaming a type referenced by an unedited type elsewhere → cascade: update that reference too.
- AddOwns of an attribute not declared anywhere → allowed (proposal can introduce attributes that don't yet exist; verifier flags as drift if needed).

Tests: each edit op has an apply-and-roundtrip test (apply edit → serialize → parse → verify expected structure).
acceptance_criteria:
- All 8 edit ops apply cleanly to a representative proposal and produce expected Parsed* structures.
- Cascading rename updates references on other types in the same proposal.
- Serializer output after each edit re-parses to the same structure (no drift).
- Revision diff after an edit accurately reports what changed (structurally).
- Errors return cleanly without partial state changes (e.g., rename to colliding name).
notes: Starting typed edit operation API after structural proposal storage landed.
close_reason: Added structural proposal edit API, Explorer edit controls for rename/parent/docs/remove/owns/plays, transcript edit events, and shared Parsed* state for Explorer and Type Editor.

title: Promote proposal to structural source of truth
description: Refactor EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart so its Parsed* arrays are canonical and typeQL becomes derived. Today the part stores typeQL: String as the source and concepts/relationships are derived from it. After this task: parsedEntities/parsedRelations/parsedAttributes are stored directly; typeQL is a computed property serialized via the new TypeQLSerializer (built in the next task). This is the data-model precondition for all in-widget editing.
design:
EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart shape change:
Before:
  let typeQL: String  // canonical
  let concepts: [...]   // derived in deriver
  let relationships: [...]  // derived in deriver

After:
  let parsedEntities: [ParsedEntity]  // canonical
  let parsedRelations: [ParsedRelation]  // canonical
  let parsedAttributes: [ParsedAttribute]  // canonical
  let annotations: [String: String]  // top-level proposal docs/annotations

  var typeQL: String { TypeQLSerializer().serialize(...) }  // derived
  var concepts: [...] { /* compute from parsedEntities */ }  // still exposed for backward compat
  var relationships: [...] { /* compute from parsedRelations */ }

Constructor variants:
- init(parsedEntities:, parsedRelations:, ...) — direct structural construction.
- static func make(typeQL: String, ...) — parses once via TypeQLParser, stores structure. (Existing call sites continue to work; AI tool flow unchanged.)

Verifier integration: LingoProposalVerifier already reads label kinds; it's agnostic to whether typeQL or structure is canonical. No change.

Revision diff (LingoProposalRevisionDiff): currently computed from typeQL deltas. Move to compute from structural deltas instead — cleaner and more precise (e.g., 'renamed X → Y' is one structural op vs. a textual diff).

Sendable / OneToolValue: sendableValue keeps typeQL field for tool-call wire compatibility; consumers that need structure read parsedEntities/etc.

Backward compatibility: any callers that read .typeQL still work (it's now computed). Callers that need structure read the new fields. Migration is mechanical: search for .concepts and .relationships in views and switch to .parsedEntities-derived where it makes sense.
acceptance_criteria:
- EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart stores Parsed* arrays directly; typeQL is computed.
- Existing make(typeQL:) constructor still works; parses once on construction.
- LingoProposalVerifier and LingoProposalRevisionDiff produce identical output before and after the refactor for representative inputs (regression-tested).
- AI tool flow (propose_schema_change → recordEngineeringHierarchyProposal → render in editor/explorer) produces identical UI output.
- All Lingo* tests pass.
close_reason: Added TypeQLSerializer with round-trip coverage, taught parser keywordless TypeDB declarations, and made EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart store parsed schema structure with derived TypeQL.

title: AI tool support for proposal_id parameter
description: Update focus_proposal_in_explorer and focus_proposal_in_editor to accept an optional proposal_id parameter. Without it: target the most-recently-revised proposal (current V1 behavior). With it: target that specific proposal — useful when the user says 'open the Collection proposal' and the AI knows which id to pass.
design:
Tool parameter additions:
- focus_proposal_in_explorer: optional proposal_id: String. If provided and matches a proposal in lingoProposals, sets selectedLingoProposalID to it and opens the explorer. If provided but no match, returns a soft error ('No proposal with id X — current proposals: [...]'). If omitted, falls through to most-recently-revised.
- focus_proposal_in_editor: same.
- delete_proposal: required proposal_id (no fallback — must be explicit).

Implementation in execute(): pull arguments['proposal_id']?.stringValue, pass to viewModel.openLingoExplorer(proposalID:) (new optional param) which handles selection.

Tool descriptions updated: examples in description so the AI knows when to use proposal_id vs not.

Soft-error format: '.dictionary(['error': .string('No proposal with id X. Active proposals: [id1, id2].')])' — includes the active list so the AI can self-correct on retry.
acceptance_criteria:
- focus_proposal_in_explorer with valid proposal_id selects that proposal and opens the explorer.
- focus_proposal_in_explorer without proposal_id selects the most-recently-revised proposal (V1 behavior).
- focus_proposal_in_explorer with invalid proposal_id returns a soft error including the active proposal id list.
- delete_proposal removes by id and surfaces a confirmation in the conversation transcript.
- Existing V1 single-proposal flows unaffected.
notes: Implementation landed and focused tests pass. Closure is intentionally deferred because these beads are blocked by open V1 smoke verification one-5s6.1.7 / parent one-5s6.1.

title: Stacked proposal banners in sidebar
description: Replace V1's single banner at top of sidebar with a stack of banners — one per proposal — and a selector that controls which proposal's tree section is expanded below. Default UX: stacked banners with the selected one visually highlighted; clicking a banner switches selection. Lean simple in V2; revisit if the stack gets unwieldy.
design:
Sidebar layout change in LingoExplorerView (or LingoExplorerTreeView):
- Banner area: VStack { ForEach(lingoProposals) { LingoExplorerBannerView(proposal: /bin/zsh, isSelected: /bin/zsh.id == selectedLingoProposalID) } }
- Each banner: summary, revision, status pill, [Apply], [Discard], [Delete] (new), [Select] (implicit on click).
- Selected banner has accent border / background tint to mark it as active.
- Below the banner stack: only the selected proposal's tree section appears (not all proposals' trees expanded — too much noise).

Banner selection: clicking a non-selected banner sets selectedLingoProposalID; tree section under refreshes; main-pane selection resets to the first type of the new proposal.

Tree assembly: visibleLingoExplorerRows now flattens [bannerRow ... ] + [proposal section for selected proposal] + [live package sections]. Non-selected proposals do NOT contribute tree rows.

Compact mode: if 4+ proposals, collapse banners into a horizontal tab strip (just summaries + revision badges, with a popover for full banner details on click). Decision: implement only stacked-banner mode in this task; tab-strip can be a follow-up if the stack feels crowded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two active proposals → two banners stacked at top of sidebar.
- Clicking a non-selected banner switches selection; tree section under updates; main pane resets to first type.
- Selected banner is visually distinct.
- Apply/Discard on a banner targets that specific proposal (not the selected one if it's different — though typically you'd select first).
- Tree shows only the selected proposal's section + live sections.
- Banner stack scrolls if it overflows vertically (responsibility on the panel area).
notes: Implementation landed and focused tests pass. Closure is intentionally deferred because these beads are blocked by open V1 smoke verification one-5s6.1.7 / parent one-5s6.1.

title: Per-proposal delete affordance
description: Add a [Delete] control on each banner that drops the proposal from the collection. Different from [Discard] in that Discard is the 'I reviewed this and reject it' user action; Delete is 'this is no longer relevant, just remove it' (e.g., the user moved on, or the AI created a stale duplicate). Confirmation prompt prevents accidental loss.
design:
UI: trash button on each LingoExplorerBannerView, separated from [Discard] by a small gap or different styling so users distinguish them.

Behavior on [Delete]:
1. Show a confirmation alert: 'Delete proposal X? This removes it from the conversation context and cannot be undone.'
2. On confirm: viewModel.removeLingoProposal(id: X).
3. removeLingoProposal:
   - Removes proposal from lingoProposals.
   - If selectedLingoProposalID == X: selects the most-recently-revised remaining proposal; if none, clears selection and closes the explorer panel.
   - Cleans verifier cache, expansion state for proposal-scoped node ids, etc.
4. Records a transcript event so the conversation history shows the deletion.

AI tool: new delete_proposal tool taking required proposal_id. Same backend path; bypasses confirmation (AI is acting on user's behalf).

Difference from Discard: Discard preserves the proposal's transcript footprint as 'rejected'; Delete removes the proposal entirely (transcript still shows the original creation message but no longer a banner).
acceptance_criteria:
- [Delete] button on each banner with a clear icon (trash).
- Clicking shows confirmation; cancel preserves state.
- Confirming removes the proposal; sidebar updates; selection moves or closes if none remain.
- delete_proposal AI tool removes a proposal by id with no UI prompt.
- Discard and Delete are visually and functionally distinct (verified in test plan).
notes: Implementation landed and focused tests pass. Closure is intentionally deferred because these beads are blocked by open V1 smoke verification one-5s6.1.7 / parent one-5s6.1.

title: Multi-proposal view-model state migration
description: Migrate OntologyViewModel from a single-optional proposal (lingoEngineeringHierarchyProposal: ...?) to a keyed collection (lingoProposals: [...]) plus a selection pointer. Update all call sites — recordEngineeringHierarchyProposal, openLingoTypeEditor, openLingoExplorer, the verifier integration, the editor presentation rows, the diff badges — to operate on the keyed collection.
design:
View-model changes:
- Replace lingoEngineeringHierarchyProposal: EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart? with lingoProposals: [EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart] (ordered by recency of last revision).
- Add selectedLingoProposalID: String? — the proposal currently shown in the explorer/editor.
- Add helpers:
  - currentLingoProposal: EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart? (computed from selectedLingoProposalID)
  - addLingoProposal(_:) — appends or replaces by id (when AI revises, supersedes existing).
  - removeLingoProposal(id:) — removes from collection; if it was selected, picks another or clears.
  - selectLingoProposal(id:) — sets selectedLingoProposalID and refreshes computed properties.

All existing computed properties (proposalParsedEntities, etc.) now operate on currentLingoProposal instead of the single field.

recordEngineeringHierarchyProposal updated: if a proposal with matching id exists, treat as revision (existing supersedes/revisionDiff path); otherwise append new. Auto-selects the just-recorded proposal.

Migration safety: callers that read lingoEngineeringHierarchyProposal directly are updated to read currentLingoProposal. Use a deprecated alias temporarily if needed to keep diff small, then remove.

Persistence (if any): existing transcripts that referenced the single proposal still resolve via proposal id.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two concurrent propose_schema_change calls produce two entries in lingoProposals.
- selectedLingoProposalID drives which proposal renders in the explorer and editor.
- removeLingoProposal cleans up state without leaving stale references in selection or expansion sets.
- Existing single-proposal flows still work as before (one proposal in the collection, auto-selected).
- All Lingo* tests pass after the migration.
notes:
Readiness review 2026-04-30: migration must preserve a compatibility path for existing tests/callers that directly read lingoEngineeringHierarchyProposal during the transition, or update those tests/callers in the same task. The selected/current proposal should remain the source for V1 explorer/editor computations.
Implementation landed and focused tests pass. Closure is intentionally deferred because these beads are blocked by open V1 smoke verification one-5s6.1.7 / parent one-5s6.1.

title: Direct editing of proposals from the explorer
description: V3 — promote the proposal data model to structural source of truth so the user can edit a proposal directly in the Lingo Explorer (rename a type, change a parent, add or remove owns/plays clauses, edit @doc annotations, remove a type from the proposal). TypeQL becomes a derived output, regenerated on each edit. Edits emit conversation events so the assistant sees what the user changed and can reason about it on the next turn. The Lingo Type Editor reflects the same edits — both views bind to one structural source.
design:
EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart refactor: parsedEntities: [ParsedEntity], parsedRelations: [ParsedRelation], parsedAttributes: [ParsedAttribute] become canonical fields. typeQL becomes a computed property that serializes the structure on read. Constructors that take typeQL now parse it once and store the structure.

New TypeQLSerializer (Parsed* → TypeQL string): correct ordering of clauses, owns annotations (@card), plays clauses, relates with role lists, attribute value-types, free-form @doc rendering. Round-trip-tested: parse(serialize(parse(typeql))) == parse(typeql) over a representative corpus including bundled package contents.

Edit operation API: typed enum LingoProposalEdit with cases:
- renameType(oldName, newName)
- changeParent(typeName, newParent)
- addOwns(typeName, attributeName, cardinality)
- removeOwns(typeName, attributeName)
- addPlays(typeName, relationName, roleName)
- removePlays(typeName, relationName, roleName)
- addAnnotation(typeName, key, value)
- removeAnnotation(typeName, key)
- removeType(typeName)

ViewModel exposes applyLingoProposalEdit(_ edit:to: proposalID:) which mutates the structure, recomputes typeQL via serializer, regenerates revision diff, increments revision.

UI affordances in the detail panel (LingoEntityDetailView etc.):
- Type name: inline-editable text field (rename)
- Parent: clickable chip → picker showing eligible parent types (live + already-proposed)
- Owns: each row has trailing × (remove); '+ Add' row at end opens attribute picker
- Plays: same pattern as owns
- @doc: inline text editor
- Trash button at top: removeType

Conversation event emission: each edit calls viewModel.recordLingoTranscript(kind: .userEdit, title: 'Edited proposal', message: 'Renamed Collection → Aggregate'). The assistant reads these on next turn and continues the conversation aware of the edit.

Editor↔Explorer sync: both views observe lingoProposals (or the single proposal post-V2). LingoTypeEditorPresentation.rows(for:) reads parsedEntities/etc. directly instead of re-parsing typeQL each render. No drift possible.
acceptance_criteria:
- User renames a type in the explorer → typeQL updates → editor table reflects new name → conversation log shows 'User renamed X → Y'.
- User adds an owns clause → editor + explorer both update; verifier output recomputes.
- User removes a type from the proposal → it disappears from explorer sidebar, editor table, and serialized typeQL.
- AI sees structured edit events on next conversation turn and can reference them ('I see you renamed Collection — should we also update the engages relation?').
- TypeQL serializer round-trips: for a corpus of representative inputs (bundled packages + AI-generated proposals), parse(serialize(parse(input))) produces the same Parsed* structure as parse(input).
- No drift between Type Editor and Lingo Explorer at any point during a multi-edit session.
notes: Starting with serializer because structural proposal storage needs a serializer before typeQL can safely become derived.
close_reason: Completed direct structural editing of Lingo proposals from the Explorer.

title: Version-pinned live cross-references
description: Replace V1's 'show all currently-loaded packages' with sandbox-aware version pinning. Query the active sandbox database for which ontology packages and versions are installed; render the live sidebar sections from those exact git-checked-out versions, not whatever happens to be loaded into PackageManager from Resources/Packages. This removes drift between what the Lingo Explorer presents as 'live' and what's actually deployed in the user's target database.
design:
New service SandboxInstalledPackages: queries the active sandbox for installed package list (name + version). Likely backed by a registry table the bootstrap planner already maintains (PackageBootstrapRegistry / typedb-package-bootstrap-registry.json — verify during task design).

Git-repo version resolver: given (packageName, version), resolves the TypeQL contents from the corresponding git ref. Implementation options to evaluate during task design:
(a) git show + git ls-tree against tracked package.json + .tql files
(b) Maintain a side-channel checkout under .build/lingo-package-cache/<package>@<version>/
(c) Rely on tags/branches in the source repo and check out a worktree

V1 fallback: when sandbox has nothing introspected (or there's no sandbox), fall back to PackageManager.packages (V1 behavior). Banner in the live section header explains the fallback.

Replace data feed: Lingo Explorer's live sections read from version-resolved cache keyed by (sandbox.id). Cache invalidates when sandbox installation state changes.

Drift indicator: when on-disk Resources/Packages version differs from sandbox-installed version for the same package, show a small badge on that package's section header ('on-disk vN, sandbox vM').

Out of scope for this feature: changing how the LIVE entity browser sources its data — that stays as it is. Only Lingo Explorer's live sections re-source.
acceptance_criteria:
- Switching active sandbox in OntologyViewModel re-renders Lingo Explorer's live sections from that sandbox's installed package versions.
- Installing gist 2.0 over gist 1.0 in a sandbox → Lingo Explorer's gist section reflects 2.0 schema (different types/owns), independent of what's checked out in Resources/Packages.
- No active sandbox → falls back to loaded packages with a banner; cross-references still work; user is told this is fallback mode.
- Drift badge appears when on-disk and sandbox-installed versions disagree.
- Live entity browser is unchanged by this work.
notes: Continuing after structural proposal editing. Starting with installed-package introspection as the source for sandbox-pinned live data.
close_reason: Completed version-pinned live cross-references for the Lingo Explorer.

title: Multi-proposal review queue
description: V2 — support multiple in-flight schema proposals concurrently. The user might have asked the assistant for two unrelated changes (e.g., 'add VibeEngineeringTask' and 'rename gist:Concept to gist:Idea') before applying either. Each proposal needs its own banner, its own tree section, and its own delete control. The view model migrates from a single-optional proposal to a keyed collection. AI tools learn an optional proposal_id parameter; without it they default to the most-recently-active proposal.
design:
View-model migration: lingoEngineeringHierarchyProposal: ...? becomes lingoProposals: [EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart] indexed by id, plus selectedLingoProposalID: String?. Existing call sites (recordEngineeringHierarchyProposal, openLingoTypeEditor, etc.) update to operate on the keyed collection.

Sidebar layout: stack of banners at the top, one per proposal, ordered by most-recently-revised. Each banner shows summary + revision + status + [Apply] + [Discard] + [Delete]. Below the stack, the SELECTED proposal's tree section appears (only one expanded at a time). Tabs at the top of the tree let the user pick which proposal's section is visible.

Decision deferred to task design: stacked-with-tab vs full switcher (one banner visible at a time, picker chooses). Lean stacked-with-tab as the first cut — fewer interactions for the common 'I have 2 active proposals' case.

Per-banner Delete: new viewModel.removeLingoProposal(id:) drops the proposal + revision diff history + clears verifier cache.

AI tool API: focus_proposal_in_explorer takes optional proposal_id (string). Without it: most-recently-revised proposal. With it: targets that exact proposal. New tool delete_proposal(proposal_id) for AI-driven cleanup.

propose_schema_change: when a proposal_id matches an existing proposal, treat as revision (existing supersedes mechanism). When it doesn't match, create a new proposal. Auto-select the just-created or revised proposal.

Editor still works on whichever proposal is selected; the editor's table view re-renders when selection changes.
acceptance_criteria:
- User issues two propose_schema_change requests in one conversation → both appear as banners stacked at top of explorer sidebar.
- Clicking a banner switches the active tree section to that proposal's types.
- Per-banner [Delete] removes that proposal cleanly; the other one stays.
- AI can target a specific proposal: 'show me proposal X in the explorer' → focus_proposal_in_explorer with proposal_id=X selects it.
- delete_proposal tool removes a proposal by id.
- Lingo Type Editor reflects the currently-selected proposal; flipping selection updates the editor table.
- No regression in single-proposal flow.
notes: Implementation landed and focused tests pass. Closure is intentionally deferred because these beads are blocked by open V1 smoke verification one-5s6.1.7 / parent one-5s6.1.

title: Lingo Type Editor has inert planning view picker
design: Remove the Engineering Planning View picker until multiple real views exist. If a future domain/ontology view selector is needed, reintroduce it with actual state and behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The Lingo Type Editor no longer shows a dropdown that does nothing. Layout remains balanced after removal.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Lingo Type Editor duplicates development database metadata
design: Remove the development database/sandbox metadata pill from the Lingo Type Editor because the inspector already owns that state. Keep target ontology and domain context in the editor if they are directly relevant to proposal review.
acceptance_criteria: The Lingo Type Editor does not repeat development database/sandbox information already shown in the inspector. The inspector remains the single visible place for that state.
close_reason: Implemented Lingo Type Editor and inspector fixes; focused Lingo transcript/editor tests pass.

title: Scaffold a new ontology from the terminal in one command
description: Power users run `ontology new <name>` and get a scaffolded ontology on their local disk ready to push. Same template as the GUI flow, same validation, no GUI required.
design:
Command: `ontology new <name> [--domain <domain>] [--path <path>] [--git] [--remote <url>]`

Behavior:
  - Creates a directory (default: ./<name>) with the ontology-template scaffolding
  - Package manifest initialized with <name>, version v0.1.0, domain description
  - Empty schema root with a validating package contract
  - Validating migration from an implicit empty baseline to v0.1.0

Flags:
  --domain  — domain description baked into the README and manifest
  --path    — override output location
  --git     — initialize as a git repo (default: true)
  --remote  — add and push to a GitHub remote (requires auth — uses `gh` env/config or GITHUB_TOKEN)

Shared code path with F26's GUI scaffolding — both call into ontology-core's scaffolding function.

Help text and examples documented in `ontology new --help` and in the CLI README section.
acceptance_criteria:
- `ontology new my-project` creates a valid ontology scaffolding in ./my-project
- Scaffolding matches the ontology-template shape and passes `ontology validate`
- Default includes git init; `--git=false` disables
- `--remote <url>` pushes first commit to the named GitHub remote
- `ontology new --help` is clear and lists all flags with examples
- Shares its scaffolding code path with F26 (one implementation, two surfaces)

title: Decide on apm-policy.yml for governance
description: APM supports policy enforcement (allowed sources, scopes, primitive types) at the org/repo level. For a solo / small-team setup this may be overkill, but it's a deliberate decision worth recording. Read the APM governance guide (https://microsoft.github.io/apm/enterprise/governance-guide/) and decide if any policy belongs in this setup.
acceptance_criteria: (1) Decision recorded: set up apm-policy.yml or skip it, with reasoning. (2) If set up: policy file committed; reasoning explains what it allows/blocks and why. (3) If skipped: reasoning explains the threat model that doesn't justify the overhead.

title: Migrate live entity explorer to shared foundation
description: Migrate the live entity browser to use the shared explorer foundation. Done first (before Lingo) because the live browser is on shipping data with established expectations — it's the higher-risk migration and we want it in production behavior unchanged before touching the proposal flow.
design:
OntologyViewModel conforms to ExplorerHostable for the live data path. Existing properties (visibleExplorerRows, expandedExplorerNodes, explorerSelection, searchText, currentDomains) become the conformance.

EntityExplorerView is rewritten as a thin wrapper around ExplorerHostView<OntologyViewModel> + live-specific banner/header/inspector. Most of the body code disappears.

Subview refactors:
- ExplorerTreeView → use ExplorerHostView's tree internally (or stays as a host-specific view if the audit says drift-by-design wins).
- ExplorerRowView → migrate to a generic over Host; shared base.
- EntityDetailView/RelationDetailView/AttributeDetailView → these probably stay where they are (detail content is more host-specific and the audit may classify as drift-by-design); the shared base hands off to a host-provided detail-renderer protocol.

Migration safety:
- Each commit is a 'before/after' snapshot. Before commit: capture screenshots of the live entity browser in 5+ states. After commit: capture again; visually compare.
- All existing entity-browser unit + UI tests run; any failures stop the migration.
- If a regression appears, revert the migration commit and adjust the shared protocol — do not band-aid in the live layer.

Out of scope: the Lingo Explorer (next task).
acceptance_criteria:
- EntityExplorerView and satellites are net-smaller after migration (LOC delta recorded).
- Visual regression check passes (screenshots before/after byte-identical or visually equivalent).
- All entity-browser tests pass.
- The shared foundation is exercised by a real consumer (the live explorer).

title: Migrate Lingo Explorer to shared foundation
description: Migrate the Lingo Explorer to the shared foundation. Done after the live migration so any protocol weaknesses surface against the live browser first. Proposal-specific UI (banner, diff badges, diff-vs-live footer, edit chrome) lives in the Lingo layer; the shared foundation has no proposal-awareness.
design:
Define a LingoExplorerHost: ExplorerHostable wrapper around OntologyViewModel that exposes the proposal-pinned data feed (proposalParsedEntities + pinnedLivePackagesBySandbox flattened, etc.) as the host's visibleRows source.

LingoExplorerView is rewritten as a thin wrapper:
- Banner at top (proposal-specific, layer-local)
- ExplorerHostView<LingoExplorerHost> as the main body, with closures injecting:
  - Diff-badge renderer (proposal-specific row decoration)
  - Detail-renderer protocol routing to LingoEntityDetailView/etc. (which keep diff-vs-live footer + edit chrome)
- LingoTypeInspectorView remains as inspector pane (or also migrates if it shares the shell with TypeInspectorView).

Strict separation: nothing in the shared foundation references EngineeringHierarchyProposalPart or any Lingo concept. All proposal awareness flows through:
- The host (which provides rows including the synthetic proposal domain)
- Layer-local view extensions (banner, diff badges, edit affordances)

Migration safety: same screenshot-before-after process as live migration. All Lingo Explorer tests pass.

Out of scope of this task: factoring the proposal-specific layer into something more abstract — it's a single consumer, no need to abstract.
acceptance_criteria:
- LingoExplorerView and satellites are net-smaller after migration.
- Visual regression: explorer renders identically before and after.
- All Lingo Explorer tests pass.
- Shared foundation has zero references to proposal/Lingo types (verified via grep for 'EngineeringHierarchy', 'Proposal', 'lingo' in the shared module).
- Both explorers can still ship layer-specific changes without touching the shared foundation.

title: Audit duplication between live and Lingo explorers
description: Step 1 of the refactor: a deliberate audit pass after V1 + V3 are live and exercised. Side-by-side diff the entity-browser and Lingo Explorer SwiftUI files, classify each piece as identical / accidental-drift / intentional-drift. Output is a written audit report (markdown in planning-n-design/) that drives the extract-and-migrate tasks.
design:
Files to compare (pairs):
- EntityExplorerView.swift ↔ LingoExplorerView.swift
- ExplorerTreeView.swift ↔ LingoExplorerTreeView.swift
- ExplorerRowView.swift ↔ LingoExplorerRowView.swift
- EntityDetailView.swift ↔ LingoEntityDetailView.swift
- RelationDetailView.swift ↔ LingoRelationDetailView.swift
- AttributeDetailView.swift ↔ LingoAttributeDetailView.swift
- TypeInspectorView.swift ↔ LingoTypeInspectorView.swift
- Models/ExplorerRow.swift ↔ Models/LingoExplorerRow.swift

For each pair, produce a section in the audit report:
- Diff stats (LOC added/removed/identical)
- Identical regions (extract candidates)
- Drift-by-accident regions (extract + unify; pick which version to keep)
- Drift-by-design regions (keep separate; document why — e.g., diff badges, edit chrome, banner row)

Identify shared abstractions:
- Tree flattening: the algorithm that produces visibleExplorerRows / visibleLingoExplorerRows. If structurally similar, extract.
- Selection model: ExplorerSelection enum + view-model property pattern. Extract.
- Expansion state: Set<String> of expanded node ids + toggle helpers. Extract.
- Search filter: case-insensitive name filter. Extract.
- Row rendering primitives: icon + label + badge + chevron layout. Extract if the visual is identical.

Output: a single markdown file at planning-n-design/lingo-explorer-refactor-audit.md or similar, with each pair section, totals, and a recommended extract list ordered by ROI.
acceptance_criteria:
- Written audit report exists, covers all 8 file pairs.
- Each pair has identical/accidental-drift/intentional-drift classification.
- A prioritized list of shared-abstraction candidates is produced (with estimated LOC savings each).
- Recommendation explicit on which file pair to extract first (lowest risk, highest reuse).
notes:
Starting after sandbox-pinned Lingo live data path is in place. Auditing live and Lingo explorer overlap before extracting shared foundation.
Paused before implementation at user request so the current experience can be manually inspected before shared-explorer refactor work starts.

title: Define shared explorer protocol
description: Based on the audit, define the shared-foundation protocol(s) that both explorers will conform to. Avoid over-specifying — only abstractions identified in the audit as 'identical or trivially different' get extracted. Drift-by-design stays in each layer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Shared protocol(s) compile and have at least one fixture conformance for testing.
- Protocol surface is minimal — driven by audit's 'identical' classification, not speculative future needs.
- Snapshot test of the shared view rendering against a fixture host passes.
- Documentation comment on the protocol clarifies what each conformer is responsible for vs what the shared layer handles.

title: Shared explorer foundation refactor
description: After V1 + V3 are live and exercised, audit the duplication between the live entity browser and the Lingo Explorer. Extract genuinely shared abstractions (data flattening, row rendering, selection model, expansion state, search filtering) into a shared explorer foundation. Migrate both to it. Drift that is good (proposal-specific affordances, edit operations, diff badges) stays divergent in the Lingo layer; drift that is accidental gets unified. This is the deliberate 'refactor third time' pass after building the pattern twice.
design:
Audit phase: side-by-side diff of EntityExplorerView vs LingoExplorerView and their satellites (TreeView, RowView, DetailView, InspectorView). Categorize each piece:
(a) Identical or trivially different — candidate for extraction.
(b) Divergent by accident (drift that should not have happened) — extract and unify.
(c) Divergent by design (proposal-specific or live-specific affordances) — keep separate.

Define shared protocol(s):
- ExplorerHostable: a view-model-like interface that produces flattened rows, handles expansion, handles selection. Both OntologyViewModel (live) and a new LingoExplorerHost wrapper conform.
- ExplorerRowKind: the existing ExplorerNode enum or a generalization with associated data per kind.
- DetailRenderer: protocol for rendering type detail given the type + a context indicating 'live' vs 'proposal' so layer-specific adornments can plug in.

Migration order:
1. Extract shared into a new module/group (Views/Explorer/Shared/ or its own GammaCore-side type if appropriate).
2. Migrate the live entity browser first (read-only on shipping data — lower-risk, easier visual parity check).
3. Migrate Lingo Explorer second.
4. Test + visual regression check: both render identical UI for shared sections.

Constraint: the refactor MUST NOT introduce regressions in either explorer. Strategy: each migration is its own commit with before/after screenshots; if regressions appear, the migration unwinds without affecting the other view.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new shared module/types handle tree flattening, row rendering, selection, expansion, and search filtering for both explorers.
- EntityExplorerView, LingoExplorerView, and their satellite files are net-smaller after migration (concrete LOC reduction recorded in completion notes).
- Visual regression: side-by-side screenshots of both explorers before and after refactor are byte-identical for shared UI.
- All existing entity-browser tests pass without modification.
- Proposal-specific UI (banner, diff badges, diff-vs-live footer, edit affordances) remains in the Lingo Explorer's layer; the shared base has no proposal-awareness.
- Both explorers can still evolve independently for layer-specific features without touching the shared base.
notes:
Starting after sandbox-pinned Lingo live data path is in place. Auditing live and Lingo explorer overlap before extracting shared foundation.
Paused before implementation at user request so the current experience can be manually inspected before shared-explorer refactor work starts.
